# Veneer

> Elements' look and motion on Bootstrap 5.3 contracts, with an owned engine and standalone CSS.

## Surface

The core entry publishes the token registry and the types that read it. The browser entry
publishes the color-mode controller, the engine's classes and contracts, and the shared mechanisms
§ Engine describes. The token values those names carry are in § Tokens.

| `ToastEventMap`                           | interface | Maps each verb to the toast event it names, carrying null detail.                                                                                      |
| `ToastHooks`                              | type      | Configures the initial DOM event subscriptions for a toast.                                                                                            |
| `ToastClassMap`                           | interface | Names the tokens a toast writes and tests, `shown`, `transition`, and `fade`, and those the delegate's dismiss route tests, `host` and `disabled`.     |
| `ToastAttributeMap`                       | interface | Names the attributes a toast reads for its options and the one the delegate's dismiss route reads; each default is Bootstrap's attribute name.         |
| `ToastSelectorMap`                        | interface | Names the selector the delegate routes dismiss clicks by; a toast constructed directly matches with none, and the default is Bootstrap's selector.     |
| `ToastOptions`                            | interface | Configures a toast's fade, automatic hiding, markup vocabulary, hooks, and lifetime.                                                                   |
| `ToastInterface`                          | interface | Shows a `.toast` in its container's flow and hides it after a delay.                                                                                   |
| `Toast`                                   | class     | Shows and hides a toast in its container's flow, and hides it after a delay unless the pointer or focus holds it.                                      |
| `TOAST_CLASSES`                           | const     | Names the class tokens a toast writes and tests and the delegate's dismiss route tests by default, the tokens Bootstrap's cascade and data API use.    |
| `TOAST_ATTRIBUTES`                        | const     | Names the attributes a toast and the delegate's dismiss route read by default, Bootstrap's attribute names.                                            |
| `TOAST_SELECTORS`                         | const     | Names the default selector the delegate routes toast dismiss clicks by, Bootstrap's data-attribute selector.                                           |
| `TOAST_DEFAULTS`                          | const     | Sets the fade, automatic hiding, and delay a toast starts from before its attributes and the constructor, Bootstrap's defaults.                        |
| `TOAST_EVENTS`                            | const     | Names the bubbling events a toast dispatches on its host, keyed by the verb each carries.                                                              |
| `isToastEvent`                            | function  | Checks whether a DOM event is a toast event, which carries no payload.                                                                                 |
| `CarouselDetail`                          | interface | Describes the detail each carousel event carries.                                                                                                      |
| `CarouselEventMap`                        | interface | Maps each verb to the carousel event it names.                                                                                                         |
| `CarouselHooks`                           | type      | Configures the initial DOM event subscriptions for a carousel.                                                                                         |
| `CarouselRide`                            | type      | Names when a carousel starts cycling on its own: at construction, or after each slide a call, a key, or a swipe asks for.                              |
| `CarouselClassMap`                        | interface | Names the class tokens a carousel writes and tests; each default is the token the cascade selects on.                                                  |
| `CarouselAttributeMap`                    | interface | Names the attributes a carousel reads; each default is Bootstrap's attribute name.                                                                     |
| `CarouselSelectorMap`                     | interface | Names the selectors a carousel matches with; each default is Bootstrap's selector.                                                                     |
| `CarouselOptions`                         | interface | Configures a carousel's cycling, keyboard and touch input, wrapping, markup vocabulary, hooks, and lifetime.                                           |
| `CarouselInterface`                       | interface | Moves a `.carousel` between its items by call, key, swipe, indicator, or interval.                                                                     |
| `Carousel`                                | class     | Moves a carousel between its items through their order and direction tokens, by call, key, swipe, or its own timer.                                    |
| `CAROUSEL_EVENTS`                         | const     | Names the bubbling events a carousel dispatches on its host, keyed by the verb each carries.                                                           |
| `CAROUSEL_CLASSES`                        | const     | Names the class tokens a carousel writes and tests by default, the tokens Bootstrap's cascade selects on.                                              |
| `CAROUSEL_ATTRIBUTES`                     | const     | Names the attributes a carousel and its slide controls carry by default, Bootstrap's attribute names.                                                  |
| `CAROUSEL_SELECTORS`                      | const     | Names the selectors a carousel finds its items, their images, and its indicator list by default, Bootstrap's selectors.                                |
| `CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS`                       | const     | Names a carousel's default options, Bootstrap's defaults with hover pausing as `true`; no default ride means no automatic cycling.                     |
| `CAROUSEL_TOUCH_DELAY`                    | const     | Names the milliseconds a carousel waits beyond its interval after a touch or pen lifts, which leaves time for the mouse events a tap fires.            |
| `isCarouselEvent`                         | function  | Checks whether a DOM event is a carousel event carrying the item it activates, its direction, and its positions.                                       |
| `parseRide`                               | function  | Parses a ride, or Bootstrap's spelling of one, to the moment a carousel starts cycling on its own.                                                     |

The controller reads its mode from the root on every access. A `dark` attribute selects dark mode;
every other value selects light mode. Applying a mode writes the attribute for that mode, light
included, so a root inside an island of the other mode opens an island of its own rather than
inheriting the one around it. Construction reads the attribute the root already carries, restores a
valid stored mode when you supply storage, and otherwise leaves the root unchanged. Destruction
writes that construction reading back, removes the attribute where the root carried none, and
releases the root, so a later `destroy`, `apply`, or `toggle` call writes neither the root nor
storage, and a later `toggle` call returns the mode the root carries. Storage operations use the
supplied browser storage directly and propagate its errors.

A button's destruction restores whether the host carried its `pressed` token and the
`aria-pressed` value it found at construction, removes the `class` attribute when the host carried
none and the toggle left the list empty, and keeps every class token a consumer added.

The delegate acquires, drives, and releases button hosts as § Engine states under Delegation. The
delegate reads no disabled state: a `disabled` host, a `.disabled` host, and an
`aria-disabled="true"` host are acquired and toggled like any other, which is what Bootstrap's data
API does with the click it receives.

## Methods

The interface exposes the following lifecycle operations.

#### `ColorModeInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apply`   | Writes the mode to the root and to storage when configured.                                                |
| `toggle`  | Flips the mode and returns the applied mode, or returns the root's mode without writing after destruction. |
| `destroy` | Restores the attribute the root carried at construction.                                                   |

#### `ButtonInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toggle`  | Toggles the live host, or returns its state without writing after destruction.                                                |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks and the host's claim, then restores whether the host carried its `pressed` token and its `aria-pressed` value. |

#### `DelegateInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `destroy` | Releases the click and key listeners and destroys every engine it owns, the scrollspies its construction scan acquired included. |

#### `RegistryInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `claim`   | Records the engine as the host's owner.                        |
| `find`    | Returns the host's owner, or undefined when the host has none. |
| `release` | Removes the host's claim when the supplied engine holds it.    |

#### `HostSnapshotInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `save`    | Records the target's value the first time the target is saved. While a restoration has the target still to write back, the value that restoration recorded is recorded instead of the element's. |
| `restore` | Writes every recorded value back, class tokens first and attributes last, and forgets the records.                                                                                               |

#### `IsolationInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                                                |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `destroy` | Releases every inert claim the isolation holds, restoring each value no live isolation still claims, and returns focus to the trigger. |

#### `BackdropInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                            |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Appends the backdrop element and adds its `shown` token.                           |
| `hide`    | Removes its `shown` token and removes the backdrop element after its fade settles. |
| `destroy` | Removes the backdrop element at once and abandons a fade in flight.                |

#### `ScrollLockInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                       |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `destroy` | Releases this reference and restores the document's scroll state when no other lock holds it. |

#### `PlacementInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                         |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `update`  | Measures the side the element resolved to and rewrites the attribute `attributes.side` names.   |
| `destroy` | Removes the popover promotion and restores every declaration and attribute the placement wrote. |

#### `SwipeInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `destroy` | Removes the pointer listeners and its `pointer` token. |

#### `SanitizerInterface`

| Method  | Summary                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `write` | Replaces the element's children with the markup the sanitizer keeps, synchronously, propagating a failure and retaining neither argument. |

#### `SanitizeTargetInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `setHTML` | Replaces the node's children with the markup the sanitizer keeps, mirroring the platform's `setHTML` method. |

#### `CollapseInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Shows the panel and hides its open accordion siblings.                                                                                   |
| `hide`    | Hides the panel.                                                                                                                         |
| `toggle`  | Hides the panel when it is shown and shows it otherwise.                                                                                 |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks, abandons a transition in flight, restores the panel and its triggers, and destroys each sibling collapse it constructed. |

#### `DropdownInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                         |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Opens the menu.                                                                                 |
| `hide`    | Closes the menu.                                                                                |
| `toggle`  | Closes the menu when it is open and opens it otherwise.                                         |
| `update`  | Measures the side the open menu resolved to and rewrites the attribute `attributes.side` names. |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks, closes the menu without events, and restores the toggle and the menu.           |

#### `TabInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                             |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Activates the control and its pane and deactivates the active sibling.                              |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks, abandons a swap in flight, and restores every role, state, and token the tab wrote. |

#### `ScrollSpyInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `refresh` | Re-reads the navigation's links and observes their sections again.                                         |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks, disconnects the observer, and restores each `active` token the scrollspy wrote or removed. |

#### `ModalInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `show`    | Shows the modal, locks document scrolling, and isolates focus inside it.                                     |
| `hide`    | Hides the modal and releases its scroll lock and focus isolation.                                            |
| `toggle`  | Hides the modal when it is shown and shows it otherwise.                                                     |
| `update`  | Recomputes the scrollbar compensation after the modal's content changes height.                              |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks, abandons a transition in flight, and restores the modal, the backdrop, scrolling, and focus. |

#### `OffcanvasInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `show`    | Shows the panel, and isolates focus inside it when it has a backdrop or locks scrolling.                                             |
| `hide`    | Hides the panel and releases its backdrop, scroll lock, and focus isolation.                                                         |
| `toggle`  | Hides the panel when it is shown and shows it otherwise.                                                                             |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks and the resize listener, abandons a transition in flight, and restores the panel, the backdrop, scrolling, and focus. |

#### `TooltipInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Builds, inserts, and shows the tip.                                                               |
| `hide`    | Hides the tip and removes it from its container.                                                  |
| `toggle`  | Hides the tip when it is shown and shows it otherwise.                                            |
| `enable`  | Lets triggers and calls show the tip again.                                                       |
| `disable` | Keeps triggers and calls from showing the tip until it is enabled again.                          |
| `fill`    | Replaces the content of the tip's slots, keyed by each slot's selector, and rebuilds a shown tip. |
| `update`  | Measures the side the shown tip resolved to and rewrites the attribute `attributes.side` names.   |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks and pending delays, removes the tip, and restores the trigger's attributes.        |

#### `PopoverInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Builds, inserts, and shows the tip, removing the header or body slot whose content is empty.      |
| `hide`    | Hides the tip and removes it from its container.                                                  |
| `toggle`  | Hides the tip when it is shown and shows it otherwise.                                            |
| `enable`  | Lets triggers and calls show the tip again.                                                       |
| `disable` | Keeps triggers and calls from showing the tip until it is enabled again.                          |
| `fill`    | Replaces the content of the tip's slots, keyed by each slot's selector, and rebuilds a shown tip. |
| `update`  | Measures the side the shown tip resolved to and rewrites the attribute `attributes.side` names.   |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks and pending delays, removes the tip, and restores the trigger's attributes.        |

#### `AlertInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                                                        |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close`   | Fades the alert out, removes it from the document, dispatches `closed` on it, and releases it. |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks and restores the alert without removing it.                                     |

#### `ToastInterface`

| Method    | Summary                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | Shows the toast and starts the delay after which it hides itself. |
| `hide`    | Hides the toast.                                                  |
| `destroy` | Releases hooks, clears the pending delay, and restores the toast. |

#### `CarouselInterface`

| Method     | Summary                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `next`     | Slides to the following item.                                                                                               |
| `previous` | Slides to the preceding item.                                                                                               |
| `slide`    | Slides to the item at a position, waiting for a slide in flight to finish first.                                            |
| `start`    | Starts or restarts cycling through the items at the active item's interval or the configured interval.                      |
| `pause`    | Pauses cycling until it is started again.                                                                                   |
| `destroy`  | Releases hooks, stops cycling and swipes, abandons a slide in flight, and restores the items, the indicators, and the host. |

## Examples

Construct a controller on the document root, select a mode, toggle it, and release its attribute.

```ts
import { ColorMode } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const controller = new ColorMode()
controller.apply('light')
controller.toggle()
controller.destroy()
```

Supply a particular root and a storage, so construction restores the mode already stored there.

```ts
import { ColorMode } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const controller = new ColorMode({
	root: document.documentElement,
	storage: sessionStorage,
})
controller.apply('dark')
controller.destroy()
```

Check an external value before passing it to the controller.

```ts
import { isColorModeState } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

isColorModeState('dark') // true
isColorModeState('auto') // false
```

Construct a collapse over one panel of an accordion whose other panel is open, and show it: the open
panel hides through its own collapse. Destruction restores both panels.

```ts
import { Collapse } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const accordion = document.createElement('div')
const open = document.createElement('div')
open.className = 'collapse show'
const panel = document.createElement('div')
panel.className = 'collapse'
accordion.append(open, panel)
document.body.append(accordion)
const collapse = new Collapse(panel, { parent: accordion })
const opened = await collapse.show()
collapse.destroy()
```

Construct an alert over a fading alert and close it: the alert removes its `show` class, waits for
the fade a `.fade` rule declares, leaves the document, and releases itself.

```ts
import { Alert } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const host = document.createElement('div')
host.className = 'alert alert-warning fade show'
document.body.append(host)
const alert = new Alert(host)
const removed = await alert.close()
```

Construct a tab over the second control of a tab list and show it: the first control and its pane
deactivate. Destruction restores both controls, both panes, and the roles the tab wrote.

````ts
import { Tab } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const list = document.createElement('div')
list.className = 'nav nav-tabs'
const home = document.createElement('button')
home.className = 'nav-link active'
home.dataset.bsTarget = '#home'
const profile = document.createElement('button')
profile.className = 'nav-link'
profile.dataset.bsTarget = '#profile'
list.append(home, profile)
const homePane = document.createElement('div')
homePane.id = 'home'
homePane.className = 'tab-pane active show'
const profilePane = document.createElement('div')
profilePane.id = 'profile'
profilePane.className = 'tab-pane'
document.body.append(list, homePane, profilePane)
const tab = new Tab(profile)
const activated = await tab.show()
tab.destroy()

Construct a scrollspy over a scrolling container whose section a navigation link names, with smooth
scrolling on the link, refresh it, and destroy it to restore the link.

```ts
import { ScrollSpy } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const nav = document.createElement('nav')
const link = document.createElement('a')
link.className = 'nav-link'
link.href = '#intro'
nav.append(link)
const container = document.createElement('div')
container.style.cssText = 'height: 200px; overflow-y: auto'
const section = document.createElement('section')
section.id = 'intro'
container.append(section)
document.body.append(nav, container)
const spy = new ScrollSpy(container, { target: nav, smooth: true })
spy.refresh()
spy.destroy()
````

Construct a dropdown over a toggle and the menu beside it, keep a click inside the menu from closing
it, open the menu, and restore both.

```ts
import { Dropdown } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const wrapper = document.createElement('div')
wrapper.className = 'dropdown'
const toggle = document.createElement('button')
toggle.type = 'button'
toggle.textContent = 'Options'
const menu = document.createElement('ul')
menu.className = 'dropdown-menu'
wrapper.append(toggle, menu)
document.body.append(wrapper)
const dropdown = new Dropdown(toggle, { dismiss: { inside: false } })
const opened = await dropdown.show()
dropdown.destroy()
```

Construct a carousel over three items, slide it forward and to its last item, and start its timer.
Destruction clears the timer and restores the items.

```ts
import { Carousel } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const host = document.createElement('div')
host.className = 'carousel'
for (const label of ['First', 'Second', 'Third']) {
	const item = document.createElement('div')
	item.className = 'carousel-item'
	item.textContent = label
	host.append(item)
}
host.firstElementChild?.classList.add('active')
document.body.append(host)
const carousel = new Carousel(host, { interval: 3000 })
const moved = await carousel.next()
const last = await carousel.slide(2)
carousel.start()
carousel.destroy()
```

Construct a modal over its dialog and show it with the button that asked for it: the page locks, the
backdrop fades in, and focus moves into the modal until it hides and returns to the button.

```ts
import { Modal } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const button = document.createElement('button')
const host = document.createElement('div')
host.className = 'modal fade'
host.tabIndex = -1
const dialog = document.createElement('div')
dialog.className = 'modal-dialog'
host.append(dialog)
document.body.append(button, host)
const modal = new Modal(host, { dismiss: { backdrop: false } })
const opened = await modal.show(button)
const closed = await modal.hide()
modal.destroy()
```

Construct a toast over a toast element with a three-second delay, show it, and wait for the
`hidden.vn.toast` event it dispatches when it hides itself after the delay. Destruction then
restores the element.

```ts
import { Toast } from '@orkestrel/veneer/browser'

const host = document.createElement('div')
host.className = 'toast'
host.textContent = 'Saved'
document.body.append(host)
const toast = new Toast(host, { delay: 3000 })
const hidden = new Promise((resolve) => {
	host.addEventListener('hidden.vn.toast', resolve, { once: true })
})
const shown = await toast.show()
await hidden
toast.destroy()
```

## Engine

The browser entry drives Bootstrap's markup on the platform's own mechanisms, and its TypeScript
follows Veneer's design rather than Bootstrap's JavaScript. The class tokens, attribute names, and
selectors the engine reads and writes default to the ones Bootstrap's cascade and data API use, and
each engine's vocabulary groups replace them, as § Vocabulary states. Wire event names are Veneer's
own: each one is the event's verb, the `.vn.` namespace, and the entity's name, such as
`toggle.vn.button`, so a page running Bootstrap's scripts beside the engine never crosses events
with it. Importing the entry installs no listener: you construct each engine yourself, or you
construct a `Delegate` instance and it acquires engines from the data attributes. A TypeScript
member keeps Veneer's naming: the `destroy` method replaces Bootstrap's `dispose`, and the static
`find` method replaces `getInstance`.

The `resolveOptions` function merges an engine's options. The engine's defaults come first, then its
declared attributes, then the object you pass to the constructor, each overriding the one before,
and an explicit `false` or `0` survives every layer. A declared key is a one-word option key, and
its attribute is the one the entity's `attributes` group names for that key, which the function
takes as the entity's resolved attribute table, an `AttributeMap` value, beside a `ParserMap` value
that names each declared key's parser. An undeclared attribute is ignored, no JSON configuration
attribute such as Bootstrap's `data-bs-config` is read, a constructor value that is `undefined`
keeps the layer beneath it, and a declared value that fails coercion throws an `AppError` carrying
the engine's `{ENTITY}_OPTION_INVALID` code, the attribute's name, and the host's tag. An option
inside a group, such as a placement or a dismissal setting, has an attribute-table key but no
top-level option key of that name, so the resolver cannot pair them by one key; the first engine
that declares such an option rules how its attribute projects into the group. Each declared key is
coerced by the parser the engine declares for it rather than by Bootstrap's `normalizeData`
function, so a key a boolean parser reads also accepts `1` and `0`.
The `Button` class declares no key, as Bootstrap's Button declares no option, and reads its options
from the constructor alone.

### Vocabulary

Every class token, attribute name, and selector an engine reads or writes is a default you can
replace. An engine's options carry up to one group per kind of name: `classes` for the class tokens
it writes and tests, `attributes` for the attributes it reads and writes, and `selectors` for the
selectors it matches with. Each group is a partial of the entity's map, such as the
`ButtonClassMap` interface, and a key you leave out keeps its default from the entity's frozen
default table, such as the `BUTTON_CLASSES` constant. The default tables equal the tokens the
shipped cascade selects on and the names Bootstrap's data API uses, and the style parity describes
those defaults alone.

A key names the fact a token marks or the option an attribute feeds, such as `pressed` for the
token a pressed button carries. A platform name, such as an `aria-*` attribute, `role`, `tabindex`,
`inert`, `popover`, or `href`, is never a key, and neither is a selector the engine derives from its
own tokens.

Construction validates each value you supply and copies each group, so a later edit to the object
you passed changes nothing the engine reads. The `resolveVocabulary` function does both. A class
value must pass the `isClassToken` function, an attribute name the `isAttributeName` function, and a
selector the `isSelector` function, and a refused value throws an `AppError` carrying the entity's
`{ENTITY}_OPTION_INVALID` code and the key. The groups are read from the constructor alone.

The button validates its `selectors` group and keeps none of it: the delegate routes button clicks
by the selector, and a button you construct directly matches with none. Each component under
§ Components lists its own default tables beside its attribute table. The following table lists the
default vocabulary of the button and the color-mode controller.

| Entity      | Group        | Key       | Default                     | Names                                    |
| ----------- | ------------ | --------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `Button`    | `classes`    | `pressed` | `active`                    | The token a pressed button carries       |
| `Button`    | `selectors`  | `trigger` | `[data-bs-toggle="button"]` | The buttons a delegated click toggles    |
| `ColorMode` | `attributes` | `theme`   | `data-bs-theme`             | The root attribute that carries the mode |

### Events

An engine dispatches its wire events on its host as bubbling `CustomEvent` instances through the
`emitEvent` function. A pre-change event is cancelable: the function returns `false` when a
listener's `preventDefault` call prevented it, which is how an engine refuses a change a listener
prevented. A completed event, such as `toggle.vn.button`, is not cancelable. A listener's return
value refuses nothing. The detail travels in the event's `detail` member alone, and no field of it
is defined on the event itself, so a listener reads `event.detail.relatedTarget` where a Bootstrap
listener reads `event.relatedTarget`.

An engine's wire table, such as `BUTTON_EVENTS`, maps each key of its event map to the wire name its
event carries, and the `EventWire` type refuses a table that names another namespace or another
entity. The `on` option takes hooks keyed the same way, and the `bindEventMap` function binds them
to the wire names until the engine is destroyed. An event under a bound name whose payload fails
the engine's event guard, such as the `isButtonEvent` function, reaches no hook.

### Delegation

The `Delegate` class is the engine's only data API. It listens for clicks and keys on its root, the
document unless you pass another, and routes each click by the selectors it resolves for each entity
it serves, and the carousel by the `step` and `index` attributes its `carousel` group resolves. The
`button` option carries the button's `classes` and `selectors` groups: a click inside a host the
resolved `trigger` selector matches drives that host's button, and each button the delegate
constructs receives the same groups. A replaced selector is not an alias, so the default selector
then routes nothing. The driven engine is the one the static `find` method of the `Button` class
returns, whoever constructed it, or an engine the delegate constructs and acquires when the host has
none; an engine you constructed keeps its own groups. The button route prevents the click's default
action, as Bootstrap's data API does. The `collapse` option carries the collapse's groups the same
way, and § Components states its route under Collapse. At construction the delegate acquires every
carousel inside its root whose ride attribute reads `load`, and when one refuses construction it
destroys itself and rethrows the carousel's error, as § Components states under Carousel. A click
whose button host is one of the panels its collapse trigger names inside the root is refused when
neither engine exists there, as § Components states under Collapse. The alert, tab, dropdown,
modal dismiss, and toast dismiss routes read a trigger or a control as disabled through the
`isDisabled` function: it
carries its entity's `disabled` token, it matches the platform's `:disabled` state, or it carries a
`disabled` attribute whose value is not `false`. The token and attribute reads are Bootstrap's `isDisabled`
reading, and the `:disabled` match also reads as disabled a control that an ancestor `fieldset`
disables, which Bootstrap's read of the element's own `disabled` property does not. The button,
collapse, carousel, and modal toggle routes read no disabled state, as Bootstrap's data API for
those components reads none. A host under nested delegate roots is driven
once per click for each entity whose selector matches, by the first live delegate whose root
contains it to reach it. A listener that destroys a delegate during a click leaves every panel the
click has not reached to the delegates still live.

While the delegate owns an engine it observes its root, and at the observer delivery that follows a
removal it restores and releases every host it acquired that the root no longer contains, whether
the host left the document or moved outside the root. A host removed and reinserted in the same
synchronous run, before the observer delivers, keeps its engine and its state, because the root
contains it again when the delivery arrives. A host reinserted after that delivery is already
released and restored. When a click route serves it, its next delegated click acquires it again with
a fresh engine; a host the delegate acquired by its construction scan stays released. A click that
reaches a delegate while a host is being restored, such as one a custom element's attribute reaction
sends, finds no owner, and the first live delegate whose root contains the host to reach it acquires
a fresh engine at once; that engine's snapshot takes the values the restoration has still to write
back. At each click and each delivery the delegate also drops every engine you destroyed directly,
and it stops observing when it owns none. Destruction removes the listeners and the observer and
restores every host the delegate still owns; an engine you constructed stays yours.

A trigger names the element it controls by its target attribute, `data-bs-target` by default, which
the `TARGET_ATTRIBUTE` constant names, or by the fragment of its `href` attribute when the target
attribute is absent, empty, or a bare `#`. The `readTarget` and `readTargets` functions take the
entity's resolved attribute table, resolve that selector as Bootstrap's `getSelector` function does,
escape each id through `CSS.escape`, and return only HTML elements.

### Ownership and restoration

Each engine class keeps one `Registry` instance, so a host carries at most one engine of each class.
Construction validates the host, then claims it before binding any hook, and a second engine of the
same class on the same host throws an `AppError` carrying the class's `{ENTITY}_HOST_OWNED` code,
such as `BUTTON_HOST_OWNED`. Every engine class has a static `find` method, Bootstrap's
`getInstance`, which returns the live engine that owns a host, or undefined when none does.
Destruction releases the claim before it restores the host, so a click or a construction that a
reaction to the restoration sends finds no destroyed engine and can claim the host. A button also
destroys itself when the `signal` you pass it aborts, and at construction when that signal has
already aborted.

Each engine keeps one `HostSnapshot` instance. It records every attribute, class token, and inline
property the engine writes before the first write, and destruction writes each recorded value back:
a value recorded as absent is removed. The first token save records whether the host carried a
`class` attribute, and the first property save records whether it carried a `style` attribute.
Restoration writes class tokens first, then removes each `class` attribute the snapshot recorded as
absent and the tokens left empty, then writes inline properties, removes each `style` attribute
recorded as absent and left empty by the properties, and writes attributes last. The snapshot owns
what its restoration publishes: the targets it has still to write back, each withdrawn as soon as
it is written back. A snapshot saved for one of those targets, by an engine of any class and from
any caller, the restoring snapshot included, records the value the restoration recorded rather
than the half-restored host, and the restoration leaves that target to it; a target already written
back is read from the host. An engine constructed in reaction to any restoration write therefore
records none of the destroyed engine's writes: it takes each value the restoration has still to
write back and reads each target already written back from the host, edits you made included, and
no later write of the destroyed engine overwrites it.
Where two restorations overlap on a target neither has yet written back, the restoration holding
the earliest recording of that target writes it back, a taken value keeping the order of the
recording it came from, because the earliest recording holds the value the target carried before
either engine wrote it. A restoration that publishes a target another restoration already wrote
back writes its own recorded value. A restoration whose write throws withdraws every target it has
not written back, a target whose earliest recording it held included, so no restoration writes that
target back. State the snapshot never recorded keeps every edit you made.
Each restoration judges the removal of a `class` or `style` attribute it recorded as absent once,
after its own token or property writes, so an overlapping or later restoration by another engine
can leave that attribute present and empty; the tokens and properties themselves are restored
unless a write throws.

Two doors let other code run inside an engine's write sequence: a custom element's reaction runs
inside each attribute, class, style, or child-list write, and a synchronous listener runs inside
each event dispatch, including the events `focus()` and `showPopover()` dispatch before they return.
Either one can destroy the engine or call its method again. After each such write or dispatch, every
engine's write sequence reads its lifetime and the host again, stops, writing and dispatching
nothing more, when it was destroyed, and takes what it writes next and what it returns from that
read. A sequence that awaits meets a third door at each `await`, because any code can run before it
resumes. At each of its doors (every write, dispatch, and `await`) it reads its lifetime and the
host again, and it stops, an asynchronous sequence resolving `false`, when the engine was destroyed
or when the host shows that another call has taken the change over. Each engine's own subsection
states what that reads as for its host. A button whose own token write or `aria-pressed` write
toggles it again writes `aria-pressed` from the read after the token write, dispatches the state the
host carries after the attribute write, and returns the state it carries after the dispatch; a
button destroyed by its own write or by a listener returns the state the host carries. A color-mode
controller whose attribute write applies the other mode stores the mode the root then carries, and
one destroyed by its attribute write leaves storage untouched.

### Motion

The `settleAnimations` function waits for an element's transitions. It reads the element's own
animations, leaves infinite and paused animations out, and resolves when each running animation
finishes, is cancelled, or leaves with its element. It re-reads the list after each round, so a
transition that starts when another finishes is awaited as well. No timer and no emulated
`transitionend` event stand in for the animation. A transition of zero length creates no animation,
so under reduced motion the wait resolves in a microtask. Aborting the signal the function takes
resolves the wait at once.

A class or dimension written on an element whose style the browser has not computed starts no
transition. The `reflow` function forces that computation, so the write that follows it in the same
task transitions from the element's present state.

### Components

Each component's subsection names its host, its default tables beside the attributes it reads and
the option paths they feed, its events, what a call taken over reads as, and where it departs from
Bootstrap.

#### Collapse

The `Collapse` class owns one panel, the element Bootstrap's markup marks with the `host` token, and
shows and hides it through a size transition. Construction validates and copies the `classes`,
`attributes`, and `selectors` groups, resolves the `parent` option, claims the panel, binds the
hooks, and writes nothing. A trigger is any element the `trigger` selector matches in the panel's
document whose target attribute or `href` fragment names the panel, read at each change, so a
trigger added after construction is written at the next one.

Showing adds the `transition` token, removes the `host` token, sizes the panel to zero, sets each
trigger's `aria-expanded` attribute to `true` without its `collapsed` token, and writes the panel's
scroll height in pixels, which the cascade's `.collapsing` rule transitions. After the transition
settles it adds the `host` and `shown` tokens, removes the `transition` token, clears the inline
size, and dispatches `shown.vn.collapse`. Hiding writes the panel's measured height, adds the
`transition` token, removes the `host` and `shown` tokens, gives the `collapsed` token and an
`aria-expanded` value of `false` to each trigger none of whose panels is shown, and clears the inline
size, so the cascade's zero height transitions; after the transition settles it adds the `host`
token back, removes the `transition` token, and dispatches `hidden.vn.collapse`. A panel carrying
the `horizontal` token sizes its width instead of its height. The `show`, `hide`, and `toggle`
methods resolve `true` after the completed event. Each resolves `false` when the panel already
carries the state, a transition is in flight on the panel, a listener prevented the pre-change
event, or the collapse is destroyed, and `show` also resolves `false` while an open sibling
transitions. The `shown` property reads the `shown` token on every access.

With a `parent`, showing first hides every open first-level sibling inside the parent: a panel that
carries the `host` and `shown` tokens or the `transition` token and sits inside no other panel
within the parent carrying the `host` or `transition` token. Each one hides through its own collapse
and dispatches its own events. That collapse is the one the static `find` method returns, or one
constructed with this collapse's groups and parent, which this collapse owns: it destroys one whose
panel left the document at its next `show` or `hide` call, and the rest when it is destroyed.

The collapse writes, removes, and tests the following class tokens, under the names its `classes`
group resolves; each default is the token the shipped cascade selects on.

| Key          | Default               | Marks                                                    |
| ------------ | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`       | `collapse`            | A panel while its size is not transitioning              |
| `shown`      | `show`                | A shown panel                                            |
| `transition` | `collapsing`          | A panel while its size transitions                       |
| `horizontal` | `collapse-horizontal` | A panel that transitions its width instead of its height |
| `collapsed`  | `collapsed`           | A trigger none of whose panels is shown                  |

The collapse reads the following attributes, under the names its `attributes` group resolves; each
default is Bootstrap's attribute name.

| Key      | Default          | Feeds                                                   | Read through                |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `target` | `data-bs-target` | The panels a trigger names, before its `href` fragment  | The `readTargets` function  |
| `parent` | `data-bs-parent` | The `parent` option, unless the constructor supplies it | The `parseElement` function |

The collapse matches its triggers with the following selector, under the name its `selectors` group
resolves; the default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key       | Default                       | Selects                                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger` | `[data-bs-toggle="collapse"]` | The triggers a collapse writes and a delegated click drives |

The collapse dispatches the following events on its panel. Each one bubbles and carries no detail,
which the platform reads as `null`.

| Key      | Wire name            | Cancelable | Dispatched                                           |
| -------- | -------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`   | `show.vn.collapse`   | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the show        |
| `shown`  | `shown.vn.collapse`  | No         | After the transition settles and the size is cleared |
| `hide`   | `hide.vn.collapse`   | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the hide        |
| `hidden` | `hidden.vn.collapse` | No         | After the transition settles                         |

A call reads the panel at each of its doors for the phase it is in. From its write of the
`transition` token until it removes that token, the panel must carry the token; at completion the
panel must carry the `host` and `shown` tokens without the `transition` token after a show, and the
`host` token without the `shown` or `transition` token after a hide; before a hide writes its token,
the panel must still carry the `shown` token without the `transition` token, and from the moment a
hide removes the `shown` token until the transition settles, the panel must lack it. A call that
finds the panel otherwise, the collapse destroyed, or a later call of the same collapse started
reads the change as taken over: it stops, writing and dispatching nothing more, and resolves
`false`. A listener that shows the panel again inside `show.vn.collapse` therefore runs the one
transition and dispatches the one `shown.vn.collapse` event: its own call resolves `true`, and the
call whose event it heard resolves `false`. Destruction aborts the wait, so a call awaiting the
transition resolves `false` and dispatches no completed event, and restoration writes back the
panel's tokens and inline size and each trigger's `collapsed` token and `aria-expanded` value.

The delegate's `collapse` option carries the collapse's groups. A click inside a trigger the resolved
`trigger` selector matches toggles each panel the trigger names that the root contains, through the
collapse the static `find` method returns or one the delegate acquires with the group. Under nested
roots each panel is driven once per click, by the first live delegate whose root contains it to
reach it, so a panel one delegate leaves alone is left for another. A listener that destroys a
delegate during a click leaves every panel the click has not reached to the delegates still live. A
click whose button host is one of the panels its collapse trigger names inside the root, with no
button and no collapse constructed on that element, is refused before either route runs: the
delegate marks, drives, constructs, and prevents nothing. Where one of the two engines exists on
that element, only the other route constructs, and both drive it once. The delegate prevents the
click's default action only when the trigger or the clicked element is an anchor, as Bootstrap's
data API does.

The collapse departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- Construction writes nothing. Bootstrap writes each trigger's `aria-expanded` and `collapsed` state
  at construction and toggles the panel when its `toggle` option is `true`, its default. The collapse
  has no `toggle` option: you call the `toggle` method, and the triggers take their state at the
  first change.
- Triggers are read at each change. Bootstrap finds them once, at construction.
- A trigger that names several panels takes the `collapsed` token only when none of them is shown.
  Bootstrap reads only the first panel the trigger names.
- The refusals read the panel's tokens, before the pre-change event and again after it. Bootstrap
  reads its own transitioning flag once, before the event.
- A call while an open sibling transitions resolves `false`. Bootstrap's sibling query,
  `.collapse.collapsing`, matches no transitioning panel, because its transition removes the
  `collapse` class.
- A panel inside a transitioning ancestor within the parent counts as nested and is not a sibling.
  Bootstrap counts only an ancestor carrying the `collapse` class.
- The sibling collapses are found or constructed after the accepted `show.vn.collapse` event.
  Bootstrap finds or constructs them before it dispatches its `show` event.
- Showing writes the `transition` token before it removes the `host` token, and each completion
  writes the `host` token, and the `shown` token after a show, before it removes the `transition`
  token. Bootstrap's `show` removes `collapse` before it adds `collapsing`, its `hide` adds
  `collapsing` before it removes `collapse` and `show`, and each of its completions removes
  `collapsing` before it adds the next class.
- Completion waits on the panel's running finite animations. Bootstrap waits on a `transitionend`
  listener with a fallback timer.
- A `data-bs-parent` value that names no HTML element throws an `AppError` carrying the
  `COLLAPSE_OPTION_INVALID` code, unless the constructor supplies `parent`. Bootstrap reads it as no
  parent.
- Destruction abandons a transition in flight, restores the panel and its triggers, and destroys
  each sibling collapse it constructed. Bootstrap's `dispose` method removes its instance data and
  event handlers and restores nothing.
- The delegate leaves a panel outside its root alone. Bootstrap's data API listens on the document,
  so it reaches every panel.

#### Alert

The `Alert` class owns one alert, the element Bootstrap's markup marks with the `host` token, and
closes it by removing it from the document. Construction validates and copies the `classes`,
`attributes`, and `selectors` groups, claims the alert, binds the hooks, and writes nothing. The
alert keeps the `classes` group. The delegate's dismiss route reads the `attributes` and `selectors`
groups, so the alert keeps neither, and it still refuses an invalid value in either at construction.
The alert declares no option of its own, as Bootstrap's Alert declares no default, so it reads no
attribute from its host.

The `close` method dispatches `close.vn.alert`, removes the `shown` token, and, when the alert
carries the `fade` token, waits for the alert's running animations to settle. It then removes the
alert from the document, dispatches `closed.vn.alert` on the removed alert, and resolves `true`. An
alert without the `fade` token leaves the document and dispatches `closed.vn.alert` before the call
returns its promise. The close reads the alert's layout before it removes the `shown` token, so an
alert inserted in the same task has a computed style and its fade still runs. The shipped cascade
declares no `.fade` rule, so under it alone a close finds no animation and completes in a
microtask; a stylesheet that declares Bootstrap's `.fade` transition makes the close wait for it.
The `close` method resolves `false` when a close is in flight, a listener prevented
`close.vn.alert`, or the alert is destroyed.

A completed close ends the alert's lifetime, as Bootstrap's `dispose` call after `closed` does: the
alert releases its hooks and its claim, so the static `find` method returns undefined for the host,
a later `close` call resolves `false`, and a later `destroy` call writes nothing. The removed alert
keeps the state the close left it in, and you can construct a fresh alert on it. The `destroy`
method called before the close completes restores the `shown` token and leaves the alert where it
is: destruction never removes the alert, and never inserts it again.

The alert and the delegate's dismiss route test and remove the following class tokens, under the
names the `classes` group resolves; each default is the token Bootstrap's markup carries.

| Key        | Default    | Marks                                                              |
| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `host`     | `alert`    | The alert a dismiss trigger that names no alert closes from inside |
| `shown`    | `show`     | A shown alert, whose token a close removes first                   |
| `fade`     | `fade`     | An alert whose close waits for its animations to settle            |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | A dismiss trigger that closes nothing                              |

The delegate's dismiss route reads the following attribute, under the name the `attributes` group
resolves; the default is Bootstrap's attribute name.

| Key      | Default          | Feeds                                                         | Read through              |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `target` | `data-bs-target` | The alert a dismiss trigger names, before its `href` fragment | The `readTarget` function |

The delegate matches dismiss triggers with the following selector, under the name the `selectors`
group resolves; the default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key       | Default                     | Selects                                             |
| --------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `dismiss` | `[data-bs-dismiss="alert"]` | The triggers a delegated click closes an alert from |

The alert dispatches the following events on its host. Each one bubbles and carries no detail,
which the platform reads as `null`.

| Key      | Wire name         | Cancelable | Dispatched                                         |
| -------- | ----------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `close`  | `close.vn.alert`  | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the close     |
| `closed` | `closed.vn.alert` | No         | On the removed alert, after it leaves the document |

The alert dispatches `closed.vn.alert` on itself after it leaves the document, so the event reaches
the alert and nothing above it: a listener on the document or on the alert's former ancestor never
hears it. Subscribe on the alert itself, or through the `on` option.

A close reads the alert at each of its doors. From its removal of the `shown` token until it
dispatches `closed.vn.alert`, the alert must lack the `shown` token, and after its removal of the
alert, the alert must be out of the document. A close that finds the alert otherwise, or the alert
destroyed, reads the change as taken over: it stops, writing and dispatching nothing more, resolves
`false`, and leaves no close in flight, so a later call can close the alert. A close is in flight
from its dispatch of `close.vn.alert`, so a `close` call that a listener or a reaction makes inside
that dispatch resolves `false` and dispatches nothing, and the call whose event it heard goes on to
remove the alert, dispatch `closed.vn.alert` once, and resolve `true`. A listener to
`closed.vn.alert` that destroys the alert makes the call resolve `false`, and the destruction writes
the `shown` token back on the removed alert. Destruction aborts the wait, so a close awaiting the
fade resolves `false` and dispatches no `closed.vn.alert` event.

The delegate's `alert` option carries the alert's groups. A click inside a trigger the resolved
`dismiss` selector matches inside the root closes one alert: the element the trigger's target
attribute or `href` fragment names, or else the closest element carrying the `host` token, when
the root contains it. It closes the alert through the engine the static `find` method returns, or
one it acquires with the group. It prevents the click's default action when the trigger is an anchor
or an area, whether or not the trigger closes anything, as Bootstrap's data API does, and a trigger
the `isDisabled` function reads as disabled closes nothing. Under nested roots each alert is closed
once per click, by the first live delegate whose root contains it to reach it. A click whose button
host is the alert its dismiss trigger closes, or whose collapse trigger names that alert, is refused
before any route runs when neither route's engine exists on that element: the delegate marks,
drives, constructs, and prevents nothing. A dismiss trigger that is itself a button host is a
different element from its alert, so one click toggles the trigger and closes the alert.

The alert departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- The alert writes no `role` attribute and no open-state attribute. Write `role="alert"` in the
  markup where the alert needs one, as Bootstrap's own examples do.
- A close while another is in flight resolves `false`. Bootstrap's `close` method has no such guard:
  a second call dispatches its event again and queues a second removal.
- Completion waits on the alert's running finite animations. Bootstrap waits on a `transitionend`
  listener with a fallback timer.
- A close reads the alert's layout before it removes the `show` class. Bootstrap's `close` method
  reads no layout.
- A `close` call after a completed close resolves `false`. Bootstrap's `dispose` call removes its
  instance, and a later `close` call on that instance throws.
- Destruction during the fade restores the `show` class, keeps the alert in the document, and
  dispatches no `closed.vn.alert` event. Bootstrap's `dispose` method removes its instance data and
  event handlers and restores nothing.
- The delegate leaves an alert outside its root alone. Bootstrap's data API listens on the document,
  so it reaches every alert.

#### Tab

The `Tab` class owns one control, the element Bootstrap's markup marks with a `data-bs-toggle` value
of `tab`, `pill`, or `list`, and shows the pane the control names. Construction validates and copies
the `classes`, `attributes`, and `selectors` groups, resolves the pane from the control's target
attribute or its `href` fragment, claims the control, and binds the hooks; the `pane` property
carries that pane, or undefined when the control names none. When the control or one of its
ancestors matches the `list` selector, construction then writes the roles and states Bootstrap
writes, each only where the markup does not already carry that value: `role="tablist"` on a list
with no role; on each control of the list, `aria-selected`, `tabindex="-1"` when the control is not
active, and `role="tab"` when it has no role; `role="presentation"` on the wrapper of a control when
the wrapper has no role; and on the pane of each control, `role="tabpanel"` when it has no role and
an `aria-labelledby` attribute naming the control's id when it has none. The controls of a list are
the elements inside it the `link` or `entry` selector matches and the `toggle` selector does not,
and every element inside it the `trigger` selector matches, which the `readControls` function
returns. The wrapper of a control is the closest element, from the control up, that the `wrapper` or
`entry` selector matches, or the control itself when none does. A control outside any list
constructs, writes nothing, and has no sibling.

The `show` method dispatches `hide.vn.tab` on the active sibling, the other control of the list that
carries the `active` token, and then `show.vn.tab` on the control, and refuses when a listener
prevented either one. It then deactivates the sibling: it removes the sibling's `active` token,
blurs it, removes the `active` and `shown` tokens from its pane, and, for a sibling whose role is
`tab`, writes `aria-selected="false"` and `tabindex="-1"` and closes the dropdown that holds it. It
activates the control: it adds the control's `active` token and, for a control whose role is `tab`,
writes `aria-selected="true"`, removes `tabindex`, and opens the dropdown that holds it. It adds the
`active` token to the control's pane and then the `shown` token. A pane carrying the `fade` token is
laid out between those two writes, so the `shown` token starts its fade, and the call waits for the
fade to settle. The shipped `_nav.scss` sheet transitions a control's colors and supplies no pane
fade, so a pane fades only under a stylesheet of your own that animates the `fade` token. The call
then dispatches `hidden.vn.tab` on the sibling and `shown.vn.tab` on the control, and resolves
`true`. A dropdown holds a control when the control's wrapper carries the `dropdown` token: opening
it adds the `active` token to the element inside the wrapper the `toggle` selector matches, adds the
`shown` token to the element the `menu` selector matches, and writes `aria-expanded="true"` on the
wrapper, and closing it removes both tokens and writes `aria-expanded="false"`. The `show` method
resolves `false` when the control is already active, a listener prevented either pre-change event, a
listener activated another control before the swap, the tab is destroyed, or the call reads the
change as taken over. The `active` property reads the control's `active` token on every access. The
tab listens for no key: the delegate carries the keyboard.

The tab writes, removes, and tests the following class tokens, under the names its `classes` group
resolves; each default is the token the shipped cascade selects on.

| Key        | Default    | Marks                                                                             |
| ---------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `active`   | `active`   | The active control and its pane, and the toggle of a dropdown holding the control |
| `shown`    | `show`     | A shown pane, and the open menu of a dropdown holding the active control          |
| `fade`     | `fade`     | A pane whose fade the call waits for after it writes the `shown` token            |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | A control a delegated click leaves inactive and the delegated keys pass over      |
| `dropdown` | `dropdown` | A wrapper holding a dropdown whose toggle and menu follow the control it holds    |

The tab reads the following attribute, under the name its `attributes` group resolves; the default
is Bootstrap's attribute name. The tab declares no option an attribute feeds, so the tab has no
`TAB_DEFAULTS` table.

| Key      | Default          | Feeds                                                | Read through              |
| -------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `target` | `data-bs-target` | The pane a control names, before its `href` fragment | The `readTarget` function |

The tab matches with the following selectors, under the names its `selectors` group resolves; each
default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key       | Default                                                                    | Selects                                                         |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger` | `[data-bs-toggle="tab"], [data-bs-toggle="pill"], [data-bs-toggle="list"]` | The controls a delegated click or key drives                    |
| `list`    | `.list-group, .nav, [role="tablist"]`                                      | The list that holds a control and its siblings                  |
| `wrapper` | `.nav-item`                                                                | The element that wraps a link inside its list                   |
| `entry`   | `.list-group-item`                                                         | The list-group items, each a control and its own wrapper        |
| `link`    | `.nav-link, [role="tab"]`                                                  | The links of a list, each a control unless it is a toggle       |
| `toggle`  | `.dropdown-toggle`                                                         | The dropdown toggle that follows the control its dropdown holds |
| `menu`    | `.dropdown-menu`                                                           | The dropdown menu that follows the control its dropdown holds   |

The tab dispatches the following events. Each one bubbles and carries the other control of the swap
as `detail.relatedTarget`, or undefined when no control was active.

| Key      | Wire name       | Cancelable | Dispatched on      | Dispatched                                        |
| -------- | --------------- | ---------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `hide`   | `hide.vn.tab`   | Yes        | The active sibling | Before any write; prevention refuses the swap     |
| `show`   | `show.vn.tab`   | Yes        | The control        | After `hide.vn.tab`; prevention refuses the swap  |
| `hidden` | `hidden.vn.tab` | No         | The active sibling | After the swap and the fade of the control's pane |
| `shown`  | `shown.vn.tab`  | No         | The control        | After `hidden.vn.tab`                             |

A call reads its list, the control, and its pane at each of its doors for the phase it is in. After
the pre-change events it reads again whether the control is active and whether the active sibling is
still the one `hide.vn.tab` named. From its removal of the sibling's `active` token on, no control
of the list but the control may carry the `active` token. From its write of the control's `active`
token the control must carry that token, and from each write to the pane the pane must carry the
`active` token and, from its write on, the `shown` token, through the fade and the `hidden.vn.tab`
dispatch. A call that finds the list, the control, or the pane otherwise, the tab destroyed, or a
later call of the same tab started reads the change as taken over: it stops, writing and dispatching
nothing more, and resolves `false`. A sibling that shows during the swap therefore takes it over,
whether a listener to the sibling's blur or a reaction to one of the call's writes shows it: the
call it took over writes and dispatches nothing more and resolves `false`, and the sibling's own
call dispatches its completed events once. A listener that shows the control again inside
`show.vn.tab` runs the one swap and dispatches the one `shown.vn.tab` event: its own call resolves
`true`, and the call whose event it heard resolves `false`. A list whose markup marks two controls
with the `active` token never swaps, because the second one fails the read after the first one's
removal. Destruction aborts the wait, so a call awaiting the fade resolves `false` and dispatches no
completed event, and restoration writes back every value the tab wrote: the roles and states it
wrote at construction, and the tokens and states of the control, its pane, the sibling it
deactivated, that sibling's pane, and each dropdown. Each tab records a value when it first writes
it, so a value another tab of the same list wrote reads to it as the markup's own. A delegate
destroys the tabs it acquired in the reverse of their acquisition, which restores a list when each
tab's first swap saved the list's own values. A tab acquired by a click on a control that was
already active saves no swap tokens at that click, though its construction still records the initial
attributes it writes; when another tab of the list swaps before it and it saves the list only at its
own later swap, destruction leaves the list with the values the other tab wrote. J-SNAPSHOT-SHARED
closes that bound after W2 with one record per saved target across engines.

The delegate's `tab` option carries the tab's groups. A click inside a control the resolved
`trigger` selector matches prevents the click's default action when the control is an anchor or an
area, as Bootstrap's data API does, and, unless the `isDisabled` function reads the control as
disabled, shows it through the tab the static `find` method returns or one the delegate acquires
with the group. The delegate's `keydown` listener on its root carries the keyboard Bootstrap binds
on each tab: `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `Home`, and `End` pressed on such a
control inside a list stop propagating and lose their default action. Focus then moves, without
scrolling, to the previous or the next control of the list, wrapping at either end, or to its first
or last control, passing over each control the `isDisabled` function reads as disabled, and that
control shows through its tab. The `computeNeighbor` function picks the previous or the next
control. Under nested roots each control is driven once per click or key, by the first live delegate
whose root contains it to reach it. A click whose button host is the tab control, with no button and
no tab constructed on it, is refused before either route runs, as a click on a collapse panel's own
button host is; where one of the two engines exists there, only the other route constructs, and both
drive it once.

The tab departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- The tab has no `Default` table and reads no `data-bs-config` attribute, so it declares no
  `TAB_DEFAULTS` table and its groups, hooks, and signal are read from the constructor alone.
- A control outside any list still constructs, as Bootstrap's does, and its `show` method activates
  the control and its pane with no sibling. Bootstrap's `show` throws when the control has no list.
- The `show` method of an active control resolves `false` and dispatches nothing. Bootstrap's
  returns nothing.
- The refusals and the active sibling are read again after the pre-change events. Bootstrap reads
  them once, before `hide.bs.tab`.
- The wait runs on the pane's own fade, through the pane's running animations, after the pane is
  laid out with its `active` token and takes its `shown` token. Bootstrap waits on each element that
  took the `active` token and carries the `fade` token, the control and then the pane, through a
  `transitionend` listener and a fallback timer, and adds `show` to the pane after that wait.
- The completed events are dispatched after the whole swap: `hidden.vn.tab` and then `shown.vn.tab`.
  Bootstrap dispatches `hidden.bs.tab` when the sibling's completion runs, which waits on a sibling
  carrying the `fade` token and otherwise runs before the control takes its `active` token, and
  `shown.bs.tab` when the control's own completion runs, which waits on the control rather than on
  its pane.
- The sibling's pane loses its `active` and `shown` tokens together, with no wait. Bootstrap removes
  `show` after the pane's own wait.
- A control whose role is not `tab` takes no `shown` token. Bootstrap adds `show` to every element
  it activates whose role is not `tab`.
- The pane is resolved once, at construction. Bootstrap reads it at each activation. The sibling's
  pane is the one the sibling's own tab carries, or the one the sibling names at the swap.
- The keyboard is the delegate's `keydown` route rather than a listener on each control, and it
  answers on a control the `trigger` selector matches; focus moves from that control rather than
  from the key's target. Bootstrap listens on each control that has an instance.
- Wire events carry the `.vn.` namespace, and the other control travels in `detail.relatedTarget`.
- Destruction restores every value the tab wrote. Bootstrap's `dispose` method removes its instance
  data and event handlers and restores nothing.
- The delegate leaves a control outside its root alone. Bootstrap's data API listens on the
  document, so it reaches every control.

#### ScrollSpy

The `ScrollSpy` class owns one scrolling element, its host, and marks the navigation link whose
section is in view with the `active` token. Construction validates and copies the `classes`,
`attributes`, and `selectors` groups, resolves the `target`, `smooth`, and `intersection` options,
claims the host, binds the hooks, and refreshes. The `target` option is the navigation whose links
follow the scroll, the host's document body by default, and the `target` property reads it.

A refresh, which the `refresh` method repeats, reads every link inside the target that carries an
`href` attribute whose fragment names a visible HTML element inside the host. It skips a link that
carries the `disabled` token or a `disabled` attribute whose value is not `false`, and a section
whose `checkVisibility` method, asked to read the `visibility` property, returns `false`. It then
replaces its `IntersectionObserver` instance with one that observes each named section. The
observer's root is the host when the host's computed `overflow-y` value is not `visible`, and the
viewport otherwise; its root margin is the `intersection.margin` option and its thresholds are the
`intersection.threshold` option. A link added, removed, enabled, or disabled after a refresh counts
from the next one.

At each delivery the scrollspy compares the root's scroll position with the one it read at the
previous delivery. A section that leaves the root area clears its link's `active` token. Scrolling
down, each entering section whose offset is not higher than the section activated last activates its
link, so the lowest entering section wins; scrolling up, each entering section higher than it
activates its link, so the highest wins. Scrolling down while the root's scroll position is zero,
the first activation ends the delivery. An activation clears the `active` token from the target and
from every link inside it that carries an `href` attribute, gives the token to the link, and then
gives it to the links that lead to the link. For a link carrying the `entry` token, that is the
element the `toggle` selector matches inside the nearest ancestor the `dropdown` selector matches.
For any other link, that is the nearest preceding sibling the `parent` selector matches of each
ancestor inside the target that the `list` selector matches. The activation then dispatches
`activate.vn.scrollspy` on the host. When the link is the one the last activation selected and it
