still carries the `active` token, the activation writes and dispatches nothing. The `link` property
reads the link the last activation selected while that link carries the `active` token, and
undefined otherwise; a refresh that no longer observes that link's section forgets it.

With the `smooth` option, a click on a link inside the target whose section the scrollspy observes
prevents the click's navigation and scrolls the root to that section with a `smooth` scroll
behavior. The host scrolls until the section's top meets the host's top padding edge, and with the
viewport as the root the document scrolls until the section's top meets the viewport's top. The
click is read from the nearest ancestor of the clicked element that carries an `href` attribute, so
a click on text inside the link counts.

The `intersection` group has no top-level option key of its own, so the scrollspy resolves it as its
own layer: the group's defaults, then the attributes its `margin` and `threshold` keys name, then
the constructor's `intersection` group, key by key. A constructor that supplies the margin alone
therefore still reads the threshold attribute. The resolved margin and threshold must be values the
observer accepts, whichever layer supplied them, and a constructor value it refuses throws an
`AppError` carrying the `SCROLL_SPY_OPTION_INVALID` code and the key, before the host is claimed.
The scrollspy keeps a frozen copy of the ratios, so a later change to the array you passed leaves
the ratios it read. The `parseRootMargin` function refuses a blank margin and hands any other to an
`IntersectionObserver` constructor, which accepts one to four pixel or percentage lengths. The
`parseThreshold` function reads a comma-separated list, as Bootstrap splits one, or a JSON array,
and refuses an empty list, a blank or non-numeric member, and a ratio outside zero to one.

The scrollspy writes, removes, and tests the following class tokens, under the names its `classes`
group resolves; each default is the token the shipped cascade selects on.

| Key        | Default         | Marks                                                                     |
| ---------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `active`   | `active`        | The active link, and the links and dropdown toggle that lead to it        |
| `entry`    | `dropdown-item` | A link inside a dropdown menu, whose dropdown toggle turns active with it |
| `disabled` | `disabled`      | A disabled link, whose section the scrollspy does not observe             |

The scrollspy reads the following host attributes, under the names its `attributes` group resolves;
each default is Bootstrap's attribute name.

| Key         | Default                 | Feeds                                                                           | Read through                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `target`    | `data-bs-target`        | The `target` option, unless the constructor supplies it                         | The `parseElement` function    |
| `margin`    | `data-bs-root-margin`   | The `intersection.margin` option, unless the constructor's group supplies it    | The `parseRootMargin` function |
| `threshold` | `data-bs-threshold`     | The `intersection.threshold` option, unless the constructor's group supplies it | The `parseThreshold` function  |
| `smooth`    | `data-bs-smooth-scroll` | The `smooth` option, unless the constructor supplies it                         | A boolean parser               |

The scrollspy matches with the following selectors, under the names its `selectors` group resolves;
each default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key        | Default                                              | Selects                                                                    |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`     | `[data-bs-spy="scroll"]`                             | The scrolling elements the delegate constructs a scrollspy on              |
| `list`     | `.nav, .list-group`                                  | The nested lists whose preceding links turn active with a link inside them |
| `parent`   | `.nav-link, .nav-item > .nav-link, .list-group-item` | The links that precede a nested list                                       |
| `dropdown` | `.dropdown`                                          | The dropdown that holds an active menu link                                |
| `toggle`   | `.dropdown-toggle`                                   | That dropdown's toggle                                                     |

The `SCROLL_SPY_DEFAULTS` constant carries the following option defaults, Bootstrap's own; the
`target` option's default is the host's document body.

| Option                   | Default         |
| ------------------------ | --------------- |
| `smooth`                 | `false`         |
| `intersection.margin`    | `0px 0px -25%`  |
| `intersection.threshold` | `[0.1, 0.5, 1]` |

The scrollspy dispatches the following event on its host. It bubbles, and its `detail.relatedTarget`
field carries the link that became active.

| Key        | Wire name               | Cancelable | Dispatched                                                           |
| ---------- | ----------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `activate` | `activate.vn.scrollspy` | No         | After the link and the links that lead to it take the `active` token |

A delivery reads the scrollspy at each of its doors. After each token write and after the dispatch
it reads its lifetime and whether a refresh replaced its observer. After each removal of an `active`
token, from a leaving section's link, the target, or a link the activation clears, that token must
be absent, and after its write of the link's `active` token and after the dispatch, the link must
carry that token. A delivery that finds the scrollspy destroyed, its observer replaced, a removed
token back, or the link without its token reads the change as taken over: it stops, writing and
dispatching nothing more, and reads no further entry. Destruction disconnects the observer, forgets
the selected link, and restores every `active` token the scrollspy wrote or removed, on the target,
the links, and the dropdown toggles, keeping every edit you made to anything else.

The delegate's `scrollspy` option carries the scrollspy's groups. At construction, before it
installs its click listener, the delegate scans its root and acquires a scrollspy, constructed with
the group, for every element inside the root the resolved `host` selector matches that has no
scrollspy yet; one you constructed stays yours. A host inserted after the delegate's construction is
not scanned, so you construct its scrollspy yourself. The delegate's observer releases a scanned
scrollspy whose host the root no longer contains, as it releases any engine it owns. When a scanned
host's attributes fail coercion, the delegate destroys every scrollspy the scan acquired, and its
construction throws the scrollspy's `AppError`.

The scrollspy departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- The `data-bs-offset` attribute is not read, and no offset converts to a root margin. Bootstrap's
  deprecated `offset` option replaces its `rootMargin` option with a margin built from the offset.
- The `rootMargin` and `threshold` options are the `intersection.margin` and
  `intersection.threshold` options, and the `smoothScroll` option is the `smooth` option.
- The `activate.vn.scrollspy` event is not cancelable. Bootstrap's event is built cancelable, and
  its plugin ignores a prevention.
- The delegate constructs the scrollspies at its own construction, inside its root. Bootstrap's data
  API constructs one for every `[data-bs-spy="scroll"]` element in the document at the window's
  `load` event.
- No `data-bs-config` attribute is read.
- A `data-bs-target` value that names no HTML element throws an `AppError` carrying the
  `SCROLL_SPY_OPTION_INVALID` code, unless the constructor supplies `target`. Bootstrap falls back to
  the document body. A margin or a threshold the observer refuses throws the same code before the
  host is claimed, where Bootstrap's observer throws the platform's error.
- A threshold member that is not wholly numeric, such as `0.5abc`, is refused, where Bootstrap's
  `Number.parseFloat` call reads it as `0.5`. A single ratio such as `0.5` is a list of one, where
  Bootstrap's type check refuses the number its `normalizeData` function reads it as.
- A fragment names an id, escaped through `CSS.escape`. Bootstrap passes the decoded fragment to its
  selector engine as a selector, so a fragment such as `#intro.lead` names an element whose id is
  `intro` and that carries the `lead` class, and a fragment that is not a valid selector throws.
- A link whose fragment carries a malformed percent escape, such as `#%E0%A4%A`, is skipped.
  Bootstrap's `decodeURI` call throws, so its refresh and its construction throw.
- A section that leaves forgets the selected link only when it is that section's link, so the `link`
  property keeps reading the active link. Bootstrap forgets its active target whenever any section
  leaves.
- The walk for the links that lead to the active one stays inside the target. Bootstrap walks every
  `.nav` or `.list-group` ancestor up to the document, and never clears a link it activates outside
  the target. A menu link whose dropdown has no toggle activates no toggle, where Bootstrap throws.
- A smooth scroll reads the nearest ancestor of the clicked element that carries an `href` attribute,
  where Bootstrap reads the clicked element's own fragment, so a click on text inside the link does
  not scroll there. The host scrolls to the section's offset inside its scrolled content, measured
  from bounding rectangles, where Bootstrap subtracts the host's `offsetTop` value from the
  section's, which misplaces the section inside a positioned host. With the viewport as the root the
  document scrolls to the section's offset in the document, where Bootstrap scrolls the window to the
  section's offset from the host.
- Each refresh reads the host's `overflow-y` value and replaces the observer. Bootstrap reads the
  value at construction alone and keeps its first observer.
- The smooth scroll's click listener is bound at construction and reads the sections the last
  refresh observed. Bootstrap binds it again at each refresh.
- Destruction restores each `active` token the scrollspy wrote or removed. Bootstrap's `dispose`
  method disconnects the observer and restores nothing.

#### Dropdown

The `Dropdown` class owns one toggle and opens and closes the menu beside it. The menu is the first
element the `menu` selector matches after the toggle among its siblings, else before it, else
inside the toggle's parent, as Bootstrap finds it, and a toggle with no such menu throws an
`AppError` carrying the `DROPDOWN_MENU_MISSING` code. Construction validates and copies the
`classes`, `attributes`, and `selectors` groups, finds the menu, resolves the dismissal, the
placement, and the reference, claims the toggle, binds the hooks, and listens for clicks and key
releases on the toggle's document. It writes nothing.

Showing places the menu through a `Placement` instance, focuses the toggle, sets its `aria-expanded`
attribute to `true`, adds the `shown` token to the menu and then to the toggle, writes the side the
menu resolved to, and dispatches `shown.vn.dropdown`. When a `beforetoggle` listener prevents the
promotion, the placement restores what it wrote, and the show resolves `false` with no focus, no
`aria-expanded` write, no token, and no `shown.vn.dropdown` event. Hiding restores the placement,
removes the `shown` token from the menu and then from the toggle, sets `aria-expanded` to `false`,
and dispatches `hidden.vn.dropdown`. Neither waits on a transition, because the cascade declares
none on the menu. The `show`, `hide`, and `toggle` methods resolve `true` after the completed event.
Each resolves `false` when the menu already carries the state, the toggle carries the `disabled`
token or is disabled, another change of the same dropdown is in flight, a listener prevented the
pre-change event or the menu's promotion, or the dropdown is destroyed. The `shown` property reads
the menu's `shown` token on every access, and the `update` method measures the side of the open menu
and writes it again.

The side and edge come from the toggle's parent, as Bootstrap's placement reads them. The `end`
token opens the menu to the right of its reference with their top edges aligned, the `start` token
opens it to the left, the `center.up` and `center.down` tokens open it centered above and below, and
the `up` token opens it above. Every other parent opens it below. Opening above through the `up`
token or below by default, a menu whose `--bs-position` property reads `end`, which the
`.dropdown-menu-end` class declares, aligns its right edge with the reference's, and every other
menu aligns its left edge; a centered menu aligns neither edge. Inside an element the `navbar`
selector matches, or when `placement.static` is `true`, the menu stays in flow: the placement writes
`static` to the attribute `attributes.popper` names, which the cascade's `[data-bs-popper]` rules
position, and promotes nothing.

The `Placement` class promotes every other menu to the top layer with `popover="manual"`, unless a
`beforetoggle` listener prevents the promotion: then it restores what it wrote and throws an
`AppError` carrying the `PLACEMENT_PROMOTION_REFUSED` code, which the dropdown reads as a refused
show. It reads the border, padding, background, color, and overflow the menu has in flow, promotes
it, and writes each of those back as an inline declaration wherever the platform's popover rule
changed it, so the promoted menu reads the values the cascade gives it in flow; the
`POPOVER_PROPERTIES` constant names the properties it reads. It then writes `position: fixed`, an
`auto` inset, the offset as margins, the `position-area` value the `PLACEMENT_AREAS` constant maps
the position to, a `position-try-fallbacks` value that flips the menu to the opposite side when the
preferred side overflows the viewport, and `position-try-order: normal`, and adds a generated name
to the reference's `anchor-name` list, keeping every name already there. It measures the side by
comparing the menu's rectangle with the reference's, and writes it to the attribute
`attributes.side` names at each show, at each `update` call, at each resize of the reference, and at
each scroll end in the document. Each hide destroys the placement, which hides the popover and
writes back every attribute and declaration it wrote.

While the menu is open, a click anywhere in the toggle's document hides it when the `dismiss` option
allows, and the hide carries the click as the `click` detail of the `hide.vn.dropdown` and
`hidden.vn.dropdown` events. The `dismiss.inside` switch rules a click inside the menu and the
`dismiss.outside` switch every other click. A click on the toggle, a click with the secondary
button, and a click inside the menu on an element whose tag name contains `input`, `select`,
`option`, `textarea`, or `form`, as Bootstrap's check reads it, never hide it. A Tab key release
outside the menu hides it when `dismiss.outside` allows, and one inside the menu never does. Every
hide that no click caused carries an undefined `click`.

The dropdown writes and tests the following class tokens, under the names its `classes` group
resolves; each default is the token the shipped cascade selects on. The `center` key is a group of
its own, and a `center` group you pass replaces its `down` and `up` tokens together.

| Key           | Default           | Marks                                                     |
| ------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shown`       | `show`            | An open menu and its toggle                               |
| `disabled`    | `disabled`        | A toggle that neither opens nor closes its menu           |
| `up`          | `dropup`          | A parent whose menu opens above the toggle                |
| `end`         | `dropend`         | A parent whose menu opens beside the toggle, on its right |
| `start`       | `dropstart`       | A parent whose menu opens beside the toggle, on its left  |
| `center.down` | `dropdown-center` | A parent whose menu opens centered below the toggle       |
| `center.up`   | `dropup-center`   | A parent whose menu opens centered above the toggle       |

The dropdown reads and writes the following attributes, under the names its `attributes` group
resolves; each default is Bootstrap's attribute name. The `dismiss` attribute feeds the whole
`dismiss` group: a `dismiss` group the constructor supplies replaces the attribute's reading, and a
key it leaves out keeps its default. The `offset` and `static` attributes feed the `placement` group
key by key, so a constructor group that sets one of those keys leaves the other to its attribute. A
present attribute whose option the constructor leaves unset and that fails coercion throws an
`AppError` carrying the `DROPDOWN_OPTION_INVALID` code, the attribute's name, and the toggle's tag.

| Key         | Default                 | Feeds                                                               | Read through                               |
| ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `dismiss`   | `data-bs-auto-close`    | The `dismiss` group, unless the constructor supplies it             | The `parseDismiss` function                |
| `offset`    | `data-bs-offset`        | The `placement.offset` option, unless the constructor supplies it   | The `parseOffset` function                 |
| `static`    | `data-bs-display`       | The `placement.static` option, unless the constructor supplies it   | The `parseStatic` function                 |
| `reference` | `data-bs-reference`     | The `reference` option, unless the constructor supplies it          | `toggle` or `parent`, read at construction |
| `popper`    | `data-bs-popper`        | Nothing; the placement writes `static` to it on a menu left in flow | Written, never read                        |
| `side`      | `data-popper-placement` | Nothing; the placement writes the side the open menu resolved to    | Written, never read                        |

The dropdown and the delegate match with the following selectors, under the names the `selectors`
group resolves; each default is Bootstrap's selector. A dropdown constructed directly matches with
`menu` and `navbar` alone: the delegate routes by `trigger` and `menu` and moves focus by `entry`,
each read from the delegate's own group.

| Key       | Default                       | Selects                                                  |
| --------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger` | `[data-bs-toggle="dropdown"]` | The toggles a delegated click or key press drives        |
| `menu`    | `.dropdown-menu`              | The menu a toggle opens                                  |
| `navbar`  | `.navbar`                     | The navbar inside which the menu stays in flow           |
| `entry`   | `.dropdown-item`              | The entries the delegate's arrow keys move focus between |

The options take the following defaults when neither an attribute nor the constructor sets them.

| Option             | Default    | Source                           |
| ------------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------- |
| `dismiss.inside`   | `true`     | The `DROPDOWN_DEFAULTS` constant |
| `dismiss.outside`  | `true`     | The `DROPDOWN_DEFAULTS` constant |
| `placement.offset` | `[0, 2]`   | The `DROPDOWN_DEFAULTS` constant |
| `placement.static` | `false`    | The `DROPDOWN_DEFAULTS` constant |
| `reference`        | The toggle | Construction                     |

The dropdown dispatches the following events on its toggle, which is each event's target. Each one
bubbles and carries a detail whose `click` member is the click that hid the menu, or undefined.

| Key      | Wire name            | Cancelable | Dispatched                                            |
| -------- | -------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`   | `show.vn.dropdown`   | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the show         |
| `shown`  | `shown.vn.dropdown`  | No         | After the menu and the toggle carry the `shown` token |
| `hide`   | `hide.vn.dropdown`   | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the hide         |
| `hidden` | `hidden.vn.dropdown` | No         | After the toggle reads `aria-expanded="false"`        |

A call reads the menu at each of its doors. Until a show writes the menu's `shown` token the menu
must lack it, and from that write on the menu must carry it; a hide reads the reverse, and before
its first token write the menu must still carry the token. A call that finds the menu otherwise, the
dropdown destroyed, or a later call of the same dropdown started reads the change as taken over: it
stops, writing and dispatching nothing more, and resolves `false`. While a change is in flight every
other call of the same dropdown resolves `false` at once, so a listener to the toggle's `focus`
event that calls `hide` leaves the show to complete. A listener that shows the menu again inside
`show.vn.dropdown` promotes it once and dispatches the one `shown.vn.dropdown` event: its own call
resolves `true`, and the call whose event it heard resolves `false`. The dropdown passes its
lifetime to the placement as the `signal` option, and the placement reads that signal after its
`popover` attribute write and after the promotion, so a dropdown destroyed by the menu's
`beforetoggle` event or by a reaction to that write leaves the placement restored and writing
nothing more. A show that finds a placement a taken-over show left restores it first and reads its
door before placing the menu again. Destruction closes an open menu without events, destroys the
placement, and writes back the `shown` tokens of the menu and the toggle and the toggle's
`aria-expanded` value. A `destroy` call made from a custom element's reaction to one of that
restoration's own attribute writes returns before the restoration's remaining writes land, because a
nested call on the shared snapshot restores only the records saved since; J-SNAPSHOT-SHARED closes
that bound.

The delegate's `dropdown` option carries the dropdown's groups. A click inside a toggle the resolved
`trigger` selector matches, unless the toggle carries the `disabled` token or is disabled, prevents
the click's default action and toggles that toggle's dropdown, the one the static `find` method
returns or one the delegate acquires with the group. The delegate also listens for key presses on
its root. An `ArrowUp` or `ArrowDown` press on such a toggle, or inside a menu the `menu` selector
matches, that the tab route leaves alone, prevents the default action, shows the dropdown, and,
while the delegate is still live, moves focus to the neighboring entry the `entry` selector matches
that carries no `disabled` token, is not disabled, renders, and is visible, as the `checkVisibility`
method reads it with its `visibilityProperty` option. From outside the entries, `ArrowDown` focuses
the first entry and `ArrowUp` the last; among the entries, focus stops at each end. An `Escape`
press prevents the default action and, when the menu is open, hides it and, while the delegate is
still live, focuses the toggle. Inside an `input` or `textarea` element every key but `Escape` is
left to the field. A press inside a menu drives the toggle before the menu among its siblings, else
the one after it, else the first one inside the menu's parent. Under nested roots each toggle is
driven once per click and once per key press. A click whose dropdown toggle is also its button host,
or one of the panels its collapse trigger names inside the root, is refused, as a button and
collapse conflict is, when no engine of either route exists on that element.

The dropdown departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- Popper is not used, and no `TypeError` reports its absence. The platform's popover and anchor
  positioning place the menu, and the top layer leaves no ancestor to clip it, so Bootstrap's
  `boundary` and `popperConfig` options and their attributes are excluded rather than accepted.
- The `autoClose` option is the `dismiss` group, and the `display` option is `placement.static`, a
  boolean.
- A declared attribute that Bootstrap reads loosely throws: `data-bs-auto-close` takes `true`,
  `false`, `inside`, or `outside`, `data-bs-offset` takes exactly two numbers separated by a comma,
  `data-bs-display` takes `static` or `dynamic`, and `data-bs-reference` takes `toggle` or
  `parent`. Bootstrap reads any other auto-close string as `true`, reads `10px` as `10`, reads any
  other display as dynamic, and falls back to the toggle for any other reference.
- The `reference` option takes an element. Bootstrap also takes an object with a
  `getBoundingClientRect` method, and its `offset` option also takes a function.
- The menu is positioned `fixed` in the top layer, where Popper positions it `absolute`, so the
  viewport is the boundary it flips against.
- Light dismissal belongs to each open dropdown, which listens on its own document, so a dropdown
  you construct directly closes on an outside click without a delegate. Bootstrap's `clearMenus`
  handler is part of its data API.
- The events carry `click` and no `relatedTarget`, because the toggle is each event's target.
- The `update` method measures the side and writes it again. The navbar is read at each show, which
  is when Bootstrap's reading of it in `update` takes effect.
- No `mouseover` listeners are added to the body's children on touch devices.
- A dropdown constructed directly answers no key: the delegate carries `Escape` and the arrow keys.
  Bootstrap's key handler is part of its data API, which reaches every instance after the module
  loads.
- The delegate's key route stops no propagation; nested delegates mark each press instead.
  Bootstrap's key handler stops propagation for the arrow keys and for `Escape` on an open menu.
- A toggle without a menu throws at construction. Bootstrap constructs the instance and fails at
  its first show.
- Destruction closes an open menu and restores the toggle and the menu. Bootstrap's `dispose`
  method destroys Popper and restores nothing.

#### Carousel

The `Carousel` class owns one carousel, the element Bootstrap's markup marks with the `host` token,
and moves it between its items. Construction validates and copies the `classes`, `attributes`, and
`selectors` groups, resolves the `interval`, `keyboard`, `pause`, `ride`, `touch`, and `wrap`
options, claims the host, binds the hooks, and listens on the host for the input those options turn
on. An item is an element the `entry` selector matches inside the host that sits inside no other
item, and the active item is the first item carrying the `active` token. The `index` property reads
the active item's position, or undefined when no item carries the token. The items are read at each
call, so an item added after construction takes part in the next slide.

A slide dispatches `slide.vn.carousel`. Unless a listener prevents it, the slide moves the
indicator: inside the first element the `indicators` selector matches, each element carrying the
`active` token loses the token and its `aria-current` attribute, and each element whose `index`
attribute carries the incoming position gains the token and an `aria-current` value of `true`. The
slide then adds the order token to the incoming item, `next` for a forward slide and `previous` for
a backward one, forces a layout read through the `reflow` function, and adds the direction token to
both items, `start` for a forward slide and `end` for a backward one, which the cascade's transforms
move. When the host carries the `slide` token, the slide waits for the incoming item's transition
through the `settleAnimations` function: its transform, or its opacity under the `carousel-fade`
class. The slide then removes the order and direction tokens from the incoming item, adds its
`active` token, removes the `active`, order, and direction tokens from the outgoing item, and
dispatches `slid.vn.carousel`. A host without the `slide` token completes the slide in the same
task, before the call returns.

The `next` and `previous` methods slide one item forward or back, and past either end onto the other
end when `wrap` is true. Each resolves `false` while a slide is in flight, when no item is active,
and when the neighbour is the active item: the last or the first item without wrapping, and the only
item of a carousel that has one. The `slide` method waits for a slide in flight to finish, reads the
items again, and slides to the item at a position. It resolves `false` for a position out of range,
not an integer, or already active, and when no item is active. Each method resolves `true` after
`slid.vn.carousel`, and `false` when a listener prevented `slide.vn.carousel`, the carousel is
destroyed, or the change was taken over. A refused call dispatches nothing.

The `start` method records that cycling is wanted and arms a timer that slides forward at the
active item's interval attribute, or at the `interval` option when that item carries no numeric
one; the `pause` method clears both. The timer is a chain of native timeouts: each tick arms the
next one at the interval of the item then active, and slides only while the document is visible and
the host is rendered. Arming reads its standing conditions and arms nothing while cycling is not
wanted, while a touch deferral is pending, while `pause` is true and the host matches `:hover`, or
while the view prefers reduced motion, which the `matchesReducedMotion` function reads at each
arming, because the automatic cycle is the motion that preference stops; a call, a key, or a swipe
still slides. A slide clears the timer, and after the slide completes or stops it arms the timer
again where it was running when the slide began, so a pointer that entered the host during the
slide keeps the timer clear. A `load` ride starts the timer at construction. An `interaction` ride
starts it after each slide a call, a key, or a swipe asks for completes, which is how a slide
control's click starts it. A `pause` call made during a slide, a `slide.vn.carousel` or
`slid.vn.carousel` listener's included, holds through both: the slide arms no timer after it, and
the `interaction` ride does not start.

With `keyboard` true, the host's `keydown` listener slides forward on `ArrowRight` and back on
`ArrowLeft` and prevents each key's default action, and it leaves both keys to a text input or a
textarea that holds them. With `pause` true, the pointer entering the host clears the timer, and the
pointer leaving the host arms it, which arms only while cycling is wanted. With `touch` true, the
carousel constructs a `Swipe` instance on the host with its own `pointer` token and slides forward
on a leftward swipe and back on a rightward one, and it refuses the native drag of each image the
`image` selector matches inside an item. With `touch` and `pause` both true, a touch or pen release
clears the timer and holds it until the milliseconds the `CAROUSEL_TOUCH_DELAY` constant names and
the interval have passed, then arms it. The hover a tap leaves behind holds nothing until the pointer
leaves the host or a mouse moves, presses, or releases inside it; at that mouse movement, press, or
release, with the pointer over the host, the timer clears as it does when the pointer enters.

The `Swipe` class reads horizontal swipes from a host's pointer events. Construction writes its
`pointer` token, `pointer-event` by default, which the cascade reads to leave horizontal panning to
the swipe, and listens for `pointerdown`, `pointerup`, and `pointercancel` on the host. The release
of a touch or pen pointer measures the distance from where the same pointer went down, and a
distance past the `threshold` option, `40` pixels by default, calls the handler with `left` or
`right`, the way the content moved. A pointer going down replaces the pointer recorded before it, a
cancelled pointer is discarded, and a mouse pointer is never read. Destruction removes the listeners
and restores the token. A carousel passes its own `pointer` token to the swipe it constructs, and a
swipe constructed while a reaction to its token write destroyed the carousel is destroyed at once.

The carousel writes and tests the following class tokens, under the names its `classes` group
resolves; each default is the token the shipped cascade selects on.

| Key        | Default               | Marks                                                            |
| ---------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`     | `carousel`            | A carousel; a slide control whose carousel lacks it does nothing |
| `active`   | `active`              | The active item and the active indicator                         |
| `slide`    | `slide`               | A carousel whose items transition as they change                 |
| `start`    | `carousel-item-start` | Both items of a forward slide while they move                    |
| `end`      | `carousel-item-end`   | Both items of a backward slide while they move                   |
| `next`     | `carousel-item-next`  | The incoming item of a forward slide                             |
| `previous` | `carousel-item-prev`  | The incoming item of a backward slide                            |
| `pointer`  | `pointer-event`       | The carousel while its swipe reads pointer events                |

The carousel and the delegate read the following attributes, under the names the `attributes` group
resolves; each default is Bootstrap's attribute name. An option the constructor supplies wins over
its attribute, and an attribute that fails coercion throws an `AppError` carrying the
`CAROUSEL_OPTION_INVALID` code.

| Key        | Default            | Feeds                                                          | Read through                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`   | `data-bs-target`   | The carousel a slide control names, before its `href` fragment | The `readTarget` function                                                                         |
| `step`     | `data-bs-slide`    | A slide control's move, `next` or `prev`                       | The delegate                                                                                      |
| `index`    | `data-bs-slide-to` | A slide control's position, and the indicator a slide marks    | The `parseInteger` function of `@orkestrel/contract`, and an attribute selector for the indicator |
| `ride`     | `data-bs-ride`     | The `ride` option                                              | The `parseRide` function                                                                          |
| `interval` | `data-bs-interval` | The `interval` option, and an item's own interval              | The `parseNumber` function of `@orkestrel/contract`                                               |
| `keyboard` | `data-bs-keyboard` | The `keyboard` option                                          | The `parseBoolean` function of `@orkestrel/contract`                                              |
| `pause`    | `data-bs-pause`    | The `pause` option                                             | The `parseBoolean` function of `@orkestrel/contract`                                              |
| `touch`    | `data-bs-touch`    | The `touch` option                                             | The `parseBoolean` function of `@orkestrel/contract`                                              |
| `wrap`     | `data-bs-wrap`     | The `wrap` option                                              | The `parseBoolean` function of `@orkestrel/contract`                                              |

The carousel matches with the following selectors, under the names its `selectors` group resolves;
each default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key          | Default                | Selects                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entry`      | `.carousel-item`       | The items; an item inside another item is not an item of this carousel |
| `image`      | `img`                  | The images inside an item whose native drag the carousel refuses       |
| `indicators` | `.carousel-indicators` | The indicator list, the first match inside the host                    |

The `CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS` constant carries the options a carousel resolves when neither its attributes
nor the constructor supply them.

| Option     | Default | Behaviour                                                 |
| ---------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interval` | `5000`  | The milliseconds each item shows while the timer runs     |
| `keyboard` | `true`  | The arrow keys slide                                      |
| `pause`    | `true`  | The pointer over the host stops the timer until it leaves |
| `touch`    | `true`  | A touch or pen swipe slides                               |
| `wrap`     | `true`  | A step past either end continues at the other end         |

The `ride` option has no default: with none, the carousel cycles only after the `start` method
starts it. The `parseRide` function reads the ride attribute: `load` and Bootstrap's `carousel` are a
`load` ride, and `interaction` and Bootstrap's `true` are an `interaction` ride.

The carousel dispatches the following events on its host. Each one bubbles and carries a
`CarouselDetail` value in `detail`: the incoming item as `relatedTarget`, the `direction` the items
move, `left` for a forward slide and `right` for a backward one, and the `from` and `to` positions.
Each event carries its own detail object.

| Key     | Wire name           | Cancelable | Dispatched                                          |
| ------- | ------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `slide` | `slide.vn.carousel` | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the slide      |
| `slid`  | `slid.vn.carousel`  | No         | After the `active` token moves to the incoming item |

A slide reads, at each of its doors, its lifetime, that both items are still items of the host, and
the items and indicators for the phase it is in. Each indicator write's door reads the `active` token
and the `aria-current` value the slide has written to that indicator so far. Until its completion
moves the `active` token, the outgoing item must carry that token and the incoming item must lack
it. From its write of the incoming item's order token, the outgoing item must lack the order token
and the incoming item must carry it until the completion removes it; from its write of each item's
direction token, that item must carry the direction token until the completion removes it. At
completion the incoming item must carry the `active` token without the order and direction tokens,
and after the last write the outgoing item must carry none of the `active`, order, and direction
tokens. A slide that finds the items or an indicator otherwise, an item gone from the host, or the
carousel destroyed reads the change as taken over: it stops, writing and dispatching nothing more,
and resolves `false`. A slide also reads a tally of slides across its `slide.vn.carousel` dispatch,
so a listener that slides the carousel inside that dispatch, back to the outgoing item included,
takes the change over: its own calls resolve as their slides do, and the call whose event it heard
resolves `false`. Destruction aborts the wait, so a slide awaiting the transition resolves `false`
and dispatches no completed event, and a `slide` call waiting on it resolves `false` as well.
Restoration writes back each item's tokens and each indicator's `active` token and `aria-current`
value first, and the swipe then writes back the host's `pointer` token from its own snapshot, so a
carousel a reaction to that token constructs finds the items restored. The `pointer` token is a
second snapshot over the host: a carousel constructed while the items are restored that writes its
own `pointer` token before the swipe's restoration runs has that token written back over, a bound
the shared per-host record of J-SNAPSHOT-SHARED closes.

The delegate's `carousel` option carries the carousel's groups. A click inside a slide control, an
element carrying the resolved `step` or `index` attribute, slides the carousel the control's target
attribute or `href` fragment names inside the root, when that carousel carries the `host` token and
the control names a move: the position its `index` attribute carries, or a `step` value of `next` or
`prev`. The delegate drives the carousel the static `find` method returns or one it acquires with
the group, and it prevents the click's default action. A control whose carousel lacks the `host`
token, lies outside the root, or is not named, and a control that names no move, is left alone with
its default action kept. Under nested roots each carousel is slid once per click. A listener in an
earlier route that destroys the delegate during a click, before the carousel is marked, leaves the
carousel unmarked and undriven, for a live delegate whose root contains it to drive. A destruction
from the carousel's own `slide.vn.carousel` listener comes after the mark, so the mark stays and an
outer delegate refuses that carousel for the click. A carousel the delegate constructs while a
reaction to that construction destroys the delegate is destroyed and driven nowhere. A click whose
slide control names a carousel with no carousel engine that is also the click's button host with no
button engine, or one of the panels its collapse trigger names with no collapse engine, is refused
before any route runs. Construction acquires every carousel inside the root whose ride attribute
reads `load`, and leaves one a consumer constructed to that consumer; when one refuses construction,
the delegate destroys itself and rethrows the carousel's error.

The carousel departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- The members follow Veneer's naming: `previous` replaces `prev`, `slide` replaces `to`, `start`
  replaces `cycle`, and `nextWhenVisible` is not a member.
- The timer is a chain of native timeouts that re-reads the active item's interval at each tick, and
  it restarts after the slide completes or stops. Bootstrap's `cycle` method runs one `setInterval`
  call at the interval read when it started, and restarts it when the slide starts.
- The `start` method arms nothing while the view prefers reduced motion. Bootstrap cycles whatever
  the preference.
- The `pause` option is a boolean, and a `data-bs-pause` value of `hover` throws. Bootstrap reads
  `'hover'` as pausing and any other value as not pausing.
- The `ride` option is `load` or `interaction`, and its absence is no ride. A `data-bs-ride` value of
  `false`, or any value the `parseRide` function refuses, throws. Bootstrap reads any truthy value
  other than `carousel` as its interaction ride.
- An `interaction` ride starts after each slide a call, a key, or a swipe asks for. Bootstrap starts
  it after a slide control's click and after a touch, and never after a key or a call.
- A slide control's click restarts no `load` ride that a `pause` call stopped. Bootstrap's click
  restarts any carousel with a ride.
- The `start` method and an `interaction` ride arm nothing while `pause` is true and the host
  matches `:hover`, and the timer arms when the pointer leaves. Bootstrap's `cycle` method arms its
  interval whatever the pointer.
- The pointer leaving the host restarts only a timer the `start` method started. Bootstrap's hover
  end starts any carousel with a ride, even one that never cycled.
- The `interval` option is a number, and a `data-bs-interval` value of `false` throws. An item's
  interval of `0` is kept, and an item's value that is not a number falls back to the option.
  Bootstrap reads `0` as the option.
- The arrow keys keep their direction in a right-to-left document. Bootstrap's `isRTL` check swaps
  them.
- A `slide` call made while a slide is in flight waits for that slide and then reads the items
  again. Bootstrap's `to` method listens for one `slid.bs.carousel` event and calls itself again.
- The `pause` method leaves a slide in flight to finish. Bootstrap's `pause` method fires a
  transition end that completes it at once.
- A refused call dispatches nothing. Bootstrap dispatches its `slide` event before it finds no active
  item and returns.
- The items exclude a nested carousel's items. Bootstrap's item and active-item queries match inside
  a nested carousel as well.
- Every indicator carrying the `active` token loses it, and a list where none carries it still marks
  the incoming indicator. Bootstrap reads the first one alone, and throws when none carries it.
- The keyboard guard reads whether a text input or a textarea holds the key. Bootstrap tests the
  target's tag name against a pattern that also matches a custom element whose name contains
  `input`.
- The drag refusal listens on the host, so an image added after construction is refused too.
  Bootstrap binds each image present at construction.
- The swipe listens on every device and pairs each release with the pointer that went down.
  Bootstrap constructs its swipe only where the document reports touch support, reads touch events
  where pointer events are absent, and reads a release from any pointer.
- The touch delay follows a touch or pen release alone, and restarts only a timer the `start` method
  started. Bootstrap's delay follows the end of every swipe gesture and starts any carousel with a
  ride.
- Completion waits on the incoming item's running finite animations. Bootstrap waits on the
  outgoing item's `transitionend` event with a fallback timer.
- Destruction clears both timers, abandons a slide in flight, and restores the items and the
  indicators, then the host's `pointer` token. Bootstrap's `dispose` method removes its swipe and its instance data and
  restores nothing.
- A slide control whose `step` value is neither `next` nor `prev` does nothing. Bootstrap's data API
  reads any value other than `next` as a backward step.
- The delegate leaves a carousel outside its root alone, and it acquires the carousels whose ride
  attribute reads `load` inside its root when it is constructed. Bootstrap's data API listens on the
  document and constructs every `[data-bs-ride="carousel"]` element at the window's load event.
- The wire names carry the `.vn.` namespace, and the detail travels in `detail` alone.

#### Modal

The `Modal` class owns one modal, the element Bootstrap's markup marks with the `host` token, and
shows it over the cascade's backdrop in the page's flow: the modal and its backdrop keep the
cascade's `z-index` rungs and never enter the top layer. Construction validates and copies the
`classes`, `attributes`, and `selectors` groups, resolves the options, finds the dialog the `dialog`
selector matches inside the host, claims the host, binds the hooks, and listens on the host for
Escape and for a press beside the dialog and on the window for a resize. It writes nothing.

Showing takes a reference to the document's scroll lock, adds the `open` token to the body, adjusts
the host's padding as the `update` method does, and, when the `backdrop` option is `true`, shows the
backdrop and waits for its fade. It then appends the host to the body when the body does not contain
it, writes `display: block`, removes `aria-hidden`, writes `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`,
scrolls the host and the element the `body` selector matches inside the dialog to the top, forces a
layout read, and adds the `shown` token. When the host carries the `fade` token, the show waits for
the dialog's transition to settle, or for the host's own when the host holds no dialog. With the
`focus` option `true`, it isolates the rest of the document and moves focus to the host. It then
dispatches `shown.vn.modal`. Hiding releases the isolation, removes the `shown` token, waits for the
host's own fade when the host carries the `fade` token, writes `display: none` and
`aria-hidden="true"`, removes `aria-modal` and `role`, hides and removes the backdrop, releases the
`open` token, removes the host's padding, releases the scroll lock, and dispatches
`hidden.vn.modal`. The `show`, `hide`, and `toggle` methods resolve `true` after the completed event.
Each resolves `false` when the modal already carries the state, a change is in flight, a listener
prevented the pre-change event, the modal is destroyed, or another write changed the host's `shown`
token at a door the call read before it dispatched its completed event. A listener to the completed
event that hides or shows the modal starts a change of its own, so a hide a `shown.vn.modal` hook
completes leaves the show's `true` in place. The `shown` property reads the `shown` token on every
access.

Escape on the host hides the modal when `dismiss.escape` is `true`. A press whose `mousedown` and
`click` both land on the host itself, beside the dialog, hides the modal when `dismiss.backdrop` is
`true`, and does nothing when the `backdrop` option is `false`. When `dismiss.escape` is `false`,
Escape on the shown modal instead dispatches `prevent.vn.modal`, and so does such a press when
`dismiss.backdrop` is `false` and the `backdrop` option `true`. After that dispatch, while the modal
is still shown with no change in flight and no bounce under way, the modal moves focus to the host
when the `focus` option is `true`. When the modal is still shown with no change in flight after that
focus, it adds the `static` token and removes it after the dialog's transition settles. A listener that hides the modal inside the
dispatch or the focus therefore leaves the host without the token.

The `update` method pads the shown host as Bootstrap's `handleUpdate` method does. It measures the
document's scrollbar as the window's inner width less the root element's client width, writes that
width as the host's `padding-right` when the document shows a scrollbar and the host does not
overflow the viewport, and writes it as the host's `padding-left` when the document shows none and
the host overflows it. A window resize runs it while no change is in flight, and it writes nothing
while the modal is hidden or destroyed. A browser that hides its scrollbars measures zero, so there
only the `padding-left` write of `0px` occurs.

The modal composes the following mechanisms, which the browser entry exports as well:

- The `ScrollLock` class holds one reference to a document's scroll lock. The document's first
  reference writes `overflow: hidden` on the body, adds the measured scrollbar width to the computed
  `padding-right` of the body and of each fixed and sticky element that spans the window, and
  subtracts it from each such sticky element's computed `margin-right`. The release that leaves no
  reference restores them. Its `selectors` group names the fixed and sticky elements, and the
  `SCROLL_LOCK_SELECTORS` constant holds Bootstrap's defaults. The modal passes the `fixed` and
  `sticky` selectors its own `selectors` group resolves, and the selectors of the document's first
  holder are the ones the lock compensates. An aborted `signal` releases a lock's reference, and the
  first lock reads it after the body's overflow write and after each padding and margin write, so
  one released there writes nothing more. The modal passes its own lifetime as that signal.
- The `Backdrop` class shows and hides one `div` element carrying the `host` token, and the `fade`
  token when `animated` is `true`, in its parent, the body by default. Showing appends the element,
  forces a layout read when animated, and adds the `shown` token; hiding removes the token and
  removes the element after the fade settles. The modal passes its own `backdrop`, `shown`, and
  `fade` tokens, and the `BACKDROP_CLASSES` constant holds the defaults.
- The `Isolation` class claims every HTML element of the host's ancestor chain up to the body, the
  host included, as not inert, and every HTML element beside that chain at each level as inert, and
  it observes each of those levels for insertions, so an isolation constructed inside another one
  keeps its host reachable. The live isolations share their claims on each element: the newest claim
  decides the attribute, a release hands the element to the newest claim left, and the last release
  restores the recorded value, so isolations may end in any order and an ancestor stays clear while
  any isolation beneath it lives. An aborted `signal` destroys the isolation, and one that aborts
  inside a claim's write during construction stops the construction there. The modal passes its own
  lifetime as that signal. Destruction moves
  focus to the trigger, the one the options name or else the element that held focus at
  construction; the platform moves no focus to a trigger that is disconnected or not rendered. The
  modal passes the trigger its `show` call received. The backdrop sits beside the chain and becomes
  inert with the rest of the page; the modal's host covers it, so no press reaches it either way.

The modal writes and tests the following class tokens, under the names its `classes` group
resolves; each default is the token the shipped cascade selects on.

| Key        | Default          | Marks                                                                  |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`     | `modal`          | The modal, which a dismiss trigger naming no target hides from inside  |
| `shown`    | `show`           | A shown modal, and its shown backdrop                                  |
| `fade`     | `fade`           | A modal whose show and hide wait for the transitions, and its backdrop |
| `static`   | `modal-static`   | A modal while it bounces after a refused dismissal                     |
| `open`     | `modal-open`     | The body while a modal holds it                                        |
| `backdrop` | `modal-backdrop` | The modal's backdrop element                                           |
| `disabled` | `disabled`       | A dismiss trigger that hides nothing                                   |

The modal and its triggers read the following attributes, under the names the `attributes` group
resolves; each default is Bootstrap's attribute name. The `backdrop` attribute feeds two option
paths: `backdrop`, which only `false` or `0` turns off, and `dismiss.backdrop`, which only `static`
turns off.

| Key        | Default            | Feeds                                                                                  | Read through                                         |
| ---------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`   | `data-bs-target`   | The modal a trigger names, before its `href` fragment                                  | The `readTarget` function                            |
| `backdrop` | `data-bs-backdrop` | The `backdrop` and `dismiss.backdrop` options, each unless the constructor supplies it | The `parseBackdrop` function                         |
| `escape`   | `data-bs-keyboard` | The `dismiss.escape` option, unless the constructor supplies it                        | The `parseBoolean` function of `@orkestrel/contract` |
| `focus`    | `data-bs-focus`    | The `focus` option, unless the constructor supplies it                                 | The `parseBoolean` function of `@orkestrel/contract` |

The modal and the delegate match with the following selectors, under the names the `selectors`
group resolves; each default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key       | Default                                | Selects                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger` | `[data-bs-toggle="modal"]`             | The triggers a delegated click shows a modal from              |
| `dismiss` | `[data-bs-dismiss="modal"]`            | The triggers a delegated click hides a modal from              |
| `dialog`  | `.modal-dialog`                        | The dialog inside the modal, whose transition a show waits for |
| `body`    | `.modal-body`                          | The body inside the dialog, scrolled to its top at each show   |
| `fixed`   | `.fixed-top, .fixed-bottom, .is-fixed` | The fixed elements the scroll lock pads                        |
| `sticky`  | `.sticky-top`                          | The sticky elements the scroll lock pads and pulls back        |

The `MODAL_DEFAULTS` constant holds the option values a modal takes when neither its attributes nor
its constructor supply them, which are Bootstrap's defaults.

| Option             | Default | Decides                                             |
| ------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `backdrop`         | `true`  | Whether the backdrop shows behind the modal         |
| `dismiss.backdrop` | `true`  | Whether a press beside the dialog hides the modal   |
| `dismiss.escape`   | `true`  | Whether Escape hides the modal                      |
| `focus`            | `true`  | Whether the modal isolates the page and takes focus |

The modal dispatches the following events on its host. Each one bubbles and carries a detail object
whose `relatedTarget` member names the trigger, as the following table states; the `isModalEvent`
function checks that shape.

| Key       | Wire name          | Cancelable | Detail `relatedTarget`       | Dispatched                                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------ | ---------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show`    | `show.vn.modal`    | Yes        | The trigger passed to `show` | Before any write; prevention refuses the show                                     |
| `shown`   | `shown.vn.modal`   | No         | The trigger passed to `show` | After the transition settles and focus moves                                      |
| `hide`    | `hide.vn.modal`    | Yes        | Undefined                    | Before any write; prevention refuses the hide                                     |
| `hidden`  | `hidden.vn.modal`  | No         | Undefined                    | After the backdrop leaves and the scroll lock is released                         |
| `prevent` | `prevent.vn.modal` | No         | Undefined                    | When Escape or a press beside the dialog meets a dismissal option that is `false` |

A call reads the host at each of its doors for the phase it is in: until a show adds the `shown`
token, and from the moment a hide removes it, the host must lack the token, and in between it must
carry it. A call that finds the host otherwise or the modal destroyed reads the change as taken
over: it stops, writing and dispatching nothing more, and resolves `false`. The doors end when the
call dispatches its completed event: a listener to that event that shows or hides the modal starts
a new change, and the call whose event it heard still resolves `true`. Every other `show` or
`hide` call is refused while a change is in flight, so a listener that shows the modal again inside
`show.vn.modal` runs the one show and dispatches the one `shown.vn.modal` event: its own call
resolves `true`, and the call whose event it heard resolves `false`. A call that only the host took
over also ends the change in flight. What that call acquired, such as the scroll lock or the
backdrop, stays held until one of the following exits releases it: a later `show` call, which
takes the held resources over, and the `hide` call after it; a `hide` call made after the host
carries the `shown` token again; or destruction. A `hide` call while the host lacks the token resolves `false`
and releases nothing. The scroll lock and the isolation each read the modal's lifetime as their
signal while they are built, so a destruction a reaction runs inside either construction stops it
and releases what it took, and a lock or an isolation whose construction another write took the
show over from is released rather than kept. Destruction aborts the wait, releases the isolation,
the backdrop, the `open` token, and the scroll lock, and restores the host's tokens, its `display`
and padding properties, and its `aria-hidden`, `aria-modal`, and `role` attributes. A host that a
show appended to the body stays in the body.

The modals of one document that resolve the same `open` token share one recording of it, and the
last to release the token restores the body. Modals that resolve different `open` tokens each
record whether the body carried a `class` attribute, so where the modal that took its token first
releases first, the body can keep an empty `class` attribute after every such modal releases, the
bound § Ownership and restoration states.

The delegate's `modal` option carries the modal's groups. A click inside a trigger the resolved
`trigger` selector matches shows the modal the trigger's target attribute or `href` fragment names
inside the root, passing the trigger to `show`, through the modal the static `find` method returns
or one the delegate acquires with the group. First it hides the first shown modal inside the root,
the first element carrying the `host` and `shown` tokens, through the modal `find` returns for it.
The route arms the focus return before it calls `show`, so a hide a hook runs inside the
`shown.vn.modal` event returns focus as well, and it disarms the return when the show resolves
`false`: the modal's next `hidden.vn.modal` event returns focus to the trigger, which the platform
refuses while the trigger is disconnected or not rendered. A delegate that a listener earlier in the
click destroyed prevents, marks, and drives nothing through the `trigger` route, and one that a
listener to the shown modal's `hide.vn.modal` event destroys marks and shows nothing, which leaves
the named modal to a live outer delegate. A click inside a trigger the `dismiss` selector matches
hides the modal its target attribute or `href` fragment names inside the root, or else the closest
element around it carrying the `host` token, through the modal `find` returns or one the delegate
acquires. That route shares the alert's dismiss resolution: it prevents an anchor's or an area's
default action first, hides nothing when the `isDisabled` function reads the trigger as disabled
with the `disabled` token, and marks and drives nothing once a listener earlier in the click
destroyed the delegate. Each route leaves a modal outside the root alone. A click is refused before
any route runs, as § Delegation states, when a modal its modal trigger names, or its enabled modal
dismiss trigger reaches, is also another route's constructing host, such as its button host or one
of the panels its collapse trigger names, and neither engine exists on that element.

The modal departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- The `prevent` event replaces `hidePrevented` and is not cancelable, so calling `preventDefault` on
  it does not veto the bounce; the bounce still stops when a listener inside the dispatch or the
  focus hides or destroys the modal. Bootstrap's `hidePrevented.bs.modal` event is cancelable, and
  preventing it skips the bounce.
- `backdrop: 'static'` is `backdrop: true` with `dismiss.backdrop: false`, and `keyboard: false` is
  `dismiss.escape: false`. The `data-bs-backdrop` attribute feeds both backdrop paths, and each takes
  the constructor's value where the constructor supplies one. Bootstrap's constructor `backdrop`
  option replaces the attribute's value whole.
- The `data-bs-backdrop` attribute accepts `static` exactly, `true`, `false`, `1`, and `0`, and any
  other value throws an `AppError` carrying the `MODAL_OPTION_INVALID` code unless the constructor
  supplies both backdrop paths. Bootstrap first normalizes the value: `true` and `false` become
  booleans; a string becomes a number only when it equals that number's own string form
  (`value === Number(value).toString()`), so `0` and `1` do and fail the check that follows, while
  `01`, `00`, and `0x10` stay strings, pass it, and read as a backdrop that hides on a press; an
  empty value or `null` becomes `null`; and any other value becomes
  `JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(value))`, or stays the original string when either step throws. It then requires a boolean or a string and throws a `TypeError` otherwise. So
  `0` and `1` become numbers and fail, a raw empty value and `null` fail, and `[]` parses to an
  array and fails. `["%"]` stays a string, because its URI decoding throws, and reads as a backdrop
  that hides on a press. The JSON-encoded empty string `""` parses to an empty string, which passes
  the string check, and its falsy value turns the backdrop and its dismissal off. Any other truthy
  string except `static` reads as a backdrop that hides on a press. Veneer accepts `0` and `1`.
- Focus stays inside the modal because the rest of the document is inert, which also keeps the
  pointer and assistive technology out. Bootstrap's `FocusTrap` utility listens for `focusin` on the
  document and moves focus back to the first or last focusable element inside the modal.
- The isolation returns focus to the trigger when the modal hides, and the bounce moves focus to the
  host only under the `focus` option. Bootstrap's `FocusTrap` returns none, its data API alone
  returns focus to the trigger, and its bounce focuses the modal whatever the `focus` option reads.
- The bounce writes the `static` token only while the modal stays shown with no change in flight
  after the `prevent.vn.modal` dispatch and the focus. Bootstrap's bounce writes `modal-static`
  unless its `hidePrevented.bs.modal` event is prevented.
- The toggle route arms its focus return before the show, where Bootstrap's data API arms it inside
  the `show.bs.modal` event, and disarms it when the show resolves `false`.
- The scroll lock and the `open` token are shared by reference count, so another shown modal keeps
  the page locked until the last one hides. Each Bootstrap modal's hide resets the scrollbar
  compensation and removes the `modal-open` class.
- The backdrop is created at each show and destroyed after each hide, and it reads the host's `fade`
  token at each show. Bootstrap creates one backdrop per modal and reads the `fade` class at
  construction.
- Escape is the host's own `keydown` event, as Bootstrap's is; no `CloseWatcher` is adopted.
- Completion waits on the running finite animations of the dialog on show and of the host on hide,
  with no timer. Bootstrap waits on a `transitionend` listener with a fallback timer.
- The bounce writes no inline `overflow-y`. Bootstrap hides the modal's vertical overflow during the
  bounce when the modal does not overflow the viewport.
- Wire events carry the `.vn.` namespace, and the trigger travels in `detail.relatedTarget`, as
  § Events states.
- The toggle route calls `show` with the trigger where Bootstrap's data API calls `toggle`, so a
  trigger naming its own shown modal whose hide a listener prevented leaves it shown with one
  `hide.vn.modal` event, where Bootstrap dispatches a second `hide.bs.modal`.
- The toggle route hides the first shown modal inside the root, through the modal `find` returns for
  it. Bootstrap's data API hides the first `.modal.show` element in the document and fails when that
  element has no instance; the delegate leaves such an element alone.
- Destruction abandons a transition in flight and restores the host, the body, and the page.
  Bootstrap's `dispose` method removes its listeners and the backdrop and restores nothing.

#### Toast

The `Toast` class owns one toast, the element Bootstrap's markup marks with the `host` token, and
shows and hides it in its container's flow. Construction validates and copies the `classes`,
`attributes`, and `selectors` groups, resolves the `animated`, `autohide`, and `delay` options,
claims the toast, binds the hooks and its pointer and focus listeners, and writes nothing. The toast
validates its `selectors` group and keeps none of it: the delegate routes dismiss clicks by the
selector, and a toast you construct directly matches with none.

Showing adds the `fade` token when the `animated` option is `true`, reads the layout, and adds the
`shown` and `transition` tokens; when `animated` is `true` it then waits for the toast's transitions
to settle. It removes the `transition` token and dispatches `shown.vn.toast`. Hiding reads the
layout, adds the `transition` token, waits the same way, removes the `transition` and `shown`
tokens, and dispatches `hidden.vn.toast`. With `animated` set to `false`, neither call waits, so
each dispatches its completed event before it returns. The `show` and `hide` methods resolve `true`
after the completed event. Each resolves `false` when a transition is in flight on the toast, a
listener prevented the pre-change event, or the toast is destroyed, and `hide` also resolves
`false` when the toast is hidden. Showing a shown toast runs the sequence again, dispatching both
events, and restarts the delay. The `shown` property reads the `shown` token on every access.

The shipped cascade declares no transition on the toast, and no Veneer rule reads the `fade` token,
so under the shipped cascade both calls complete in a microtask. Where a sheet of yours carries
Bootstrap's `.fade` transition, hiding waits for the fade out. Showing takes the toast from no
display to displayed at no opacity, which starts no transition, so `shown.vn.toast` dispatches in a
microtask and the fade in runs after it, as the `transition` token leaves.

With the `autohide` option `true`, a shown toast hides itself through a native `setTimeout` timer
`delay` milliseconds after `shown.vn.toast`. The timer is cleared while the pointer or focus is
inside the toast, focus moving between the toast's descendants included, and started again in full
when both have left. When a `mouseout` event's related target is outside the toast, the toast reads
whether focus is still inside through the `:focus-within` pseudo-class; when a `focusout` event's
related target is outside, it reads whether the pointer is still inside through the `:hover`
pseudo-class; and a toast that shows with either one inside starts no timer until both leave. An
accepted `show` or `hide` call clears the pending timer, and so does destruction.

The toast writes and tests the `shown`, `transition`, and `fade` tokens, and the delegate's dismiss
route tests the `host` and `disabled` tokens, under the names the `classes` group resolves; each
default is the token Bootstrap's cascade and data API use.

| Key          | Default    | Marks                                                               |
| ------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`       | `toast`    | A toast, which a dismiss trigger naming no target hides from inside |
| `shown`      | `show`     | A shown toast                                                       |
| `transition` | `showing`  | A toast while it shows or hides                                     |
| `fade`       | `fade`     | A toast that fades, written when the `animated` option is `true`    |
| `disabled`   | `disabled` | A dismiss trigger that hides nothing                                |

The toast reads the `animated`, `autohide`, and `delay` attributes, and the delegate's dismiss route
reads the `target` attribute, under the names the `attributes` group resolves; each default is
Bootstrap's attribute name.

| Key        | Default             | Feeds                                                         | Read through                |
| ---------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `animated` | `data-bs-animation` | The `animated` option, unless the constructor supplies it     | The `parseBoolean` function |
| `autohide` | `data-bs-autohide`  | The `autohide` option, unless the constructor supplies it     | The `parseBoolean` function |
| `delay`    | `data-bs-delay`     | The `delay` option, unless the constructor supplies it        | The `parseNumber` function  |
| `target`   | `data-bs-target`    | The toast a dismiss trigger names, before its `href` fragment | The `readTarget` function   |

The `TOAST_DEFAULTS` constant holds the options the toast starts from, before the attributes and
the constructor; each default is Bootstrap's.

| Option     | Default | Controls                                                                |
| ---------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `animated` | `true`  | Whether the toast writes the `fade` token and waits for its transitions |
| `autohide` | `true`  | Whether a shown toast hides itself after the delay                      |
| `delay`    | `5000`  | The milliseconds a shown toast waits before it hides itself             |

The delegate matches dismiss triggers with the following selector, under the name the `selectors`
group resolves; the default is Bootstrap's selector.

| Key       | Default                     | Selects                                              |
| --------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `dismiss` | `[data-bs-dismiss="toast"]` | The triggers a delegated click hides a toast through |

The toast dispatches the following events on its host. Each one bubbles and carries no detail,
which the platform reads as `null`.

| Key      | Wire name         | Cancelable | Dispatched                                      |
| -------- | ----------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `show`   | `show.vn.toast`   | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the show   |
| `shown`  | `shown.vn.toast`  | No         | After the `transition` token leaves             |
| `hide`   | `hide.vn.toast`   | Yes        | Before any write; prevention refuses the hide   |
| `hidden` | `hidden.vn.toast` | No         | After the `transition` and `shown` tokens leave |

A call reads the toast at each of its doors for the phase it is in. Before a show writes the
`transition` token, the toast must lack it, and after its `fade` write the toast must carry the
`shown` token exactly when it carried it as the call began writing; from a call's write of the
`transition` token until it removes that token, the toast must carry the `transition` and `shown`
tokens; at completion the toast must carry the `shown` token without the `transition` token after
a show, and neither token after a hide. A call that finds the toast otherwise, the toast destroyed,
or a later call of the same toast started reads the change as taken over: it stops, writing and
dispatching nothing more, and resolves `false`. A call takes its identity before it dispatches its
pre-change event, so a listener that calls `show` inside `show.vn.toast` or `hide.vn.toast` takes
the change over, whether that call is still waiting or has already completed: the call whose event
it heard resolves `false` and writes nothing, and the listener's call completes or stops by its own
cancellation, lifetime, and door reads. A listener that prevents the nested `show.vn.toast` its own
call dispatches therefore leaves both calls resolving `false`, with no token written and no
completed event. Destruction clears the timer and
aborts the wait, so a call awaiting the transition resolves `false` and dispatches no completed
event, and restoration writes back the toast's `shown`, `transition`, and `fade` tokens.

The delegate's `toast` option carries the toast's groups. A click inside a trigger the resolved
`dismiss` selector matches inside the root hides the toast the trigger's target attribute or `href`
fragment names, or, when the trigger names none, the closest element carrying the `host` token,
through the toast the static `find` method returns or one the delegate acquires with the group, by
the dismiss resolution the alert and modal dismiss routes share. The route runs last, after the
modal routes. It prevents the click's default action when the trigger is an anchor or an area, as
Bootstrap's data API does, and only then reads the trigger through the `isDisabled` function and
the delegate's lifetime, so a disabled trigger, or a delegate a listener earlier in the click
destroyed, hides nothing. The delegate leaves a toast outside its root alone, and under nested roots
each toast is driven once per click. While no toast engine sits on it, the toast an enabled dismiss
trigger reaches is one of the elements the delegate's conflict refusal counts, so a click whose
toast is also its button host or one of the panels its collapse trigger names inside the root is
refused before any route runs where both routes would construct an engine on it: the delegate
marks, drives, constructs, and prevents nothing.

The toast departs from Bootstrap's in these ways:

- No `hide` token is written. Bootstrap's `hide` method adds its deprecated `hide` class at
  completion, and its `show` method removes it.
- The option Bootstrap names `animation` is `animated`, read from the `data-bs-animation` attribute
  by default, and no `data-bs-config` attribute is read.
- The events carry the `.vn.` namespace, such as `shown.vn.toast`, where Bootstrap's carry `.bs.`.
- Completion waits on the toast's running finite animations, and the delay runs on a native
  `setTimeout` timer with no fallback timer beside it. Bootstrap waits on a `transitionend`
  listener with a fallback timer, so its `shown.bs.toast` event arrives after the fade's duration
  even though showing starts no transition.
- A call while a transition is in flight resolves `false`. Bootstrap's `show` and `hide` methods
  have no such guard, and each runs its sequence again.
- Hiding reads the layout before it writes the `transition` token, so a toast inserted shown in the
  same task still fades out. Bootstrap's `hide` method reads no layout.
- The toast reads whether the pointer or focus is still inside through the `:hover` and
  `:focus-within` pseudo-classes. Bootstrap keeps a flag for each, which its `mouseover`,
