  `mouseout`, `focusin`, and `focusout` listeners set.
- An accepted `hide` call clears the pending timer. Bootstrap leaves it running, so it later calls
  `hide` on the hidden toast.
- The toast stays in its container's flow and is never promoted to the top layer, so a toast
  container keeps its stacking level above a modal's, as Bootstrap's does. A native popover toast
  would leave the container's flow.
- Destruction clears the timer, abandons a transition in flight, and restores the `shown`,
  `transition`, and `fade` tokens the toast carried before its first change. Bootstrap's `dispose`
  method clears the timer and removes the `show` class.
- The delegate leaves a toast outside its root alone. Bootstrap's data API listens on the document,
  so it reaches every toast.

## Styles

Veneer publishes its cascade through a standalone stylesheet subpath, `./styles`. The
`build:src:styles` script compiles the `src/styles/index.scss` barrel to the
`dist/src/styles/index.css` stylesheet, and the manifest's `exports` map names that file under the
subpath. The manifest lists the `**/*.css` pattern in its `sideEffects` field, so a bundler keeps
an import of that subpath rather than dropping it as unused.

Load the cascade from your entry module, ahead of the rules of your own that override it.

```ts
import '@orkestrel/veneer/styles'
```

The specifier resolves to standalone CSS rather than to a JavaScript module, so the import carries a
stylesheet and declares no binding. A consumer with no bundler resolves the same subpath and serves
the resolved file with a `<link>` element instead.

The `src/styles/_tokens.scss` partial declares the
`theme, reset, base, elements, components, utilities` cascade order, and the entry reaches that
statement through the barrel's first `@use` rule, so the order is declared before any rule fills a
layer.

The barrel loads the forms partials in the order the release's `_forms.scss` partial imports them,
so the validation partial loads after the other forms partials: where a validation rule and a forms
rule tie on one property, the validation rule wins, as it does in the release. The
`Bootstrap source order` case pins that sequence; see
[Bootstrap conformance](../tests/conformance.test.ts).

Every Bootstrap utility Veneer ships carries the `!important` Bootstrap writes for it, and Veneer
adds none Bootstrap does not write. Outside the class utilities, the `[hidden]` rule in the `reset`
layer, the calendar-picker indicator rule in the `elements` layer, and the color swatch rules in
the `components` layer carry one as well, each matching Bootstrap's own declaration. The
conformance proof holds that agreement for every declaration both sheets make: each shared selector,
property, and media condition carries the same priority on both sides, because the oracle records
values without their priority. The condition is part of that comparison because the release writes
one selector's property at both priorities under different conditions: each responsive offcanvas
panel's fill is normal below its boundary and important at and above it. Where a class name exists
in Bootstrap and in Tailwind, the declaration Veneer ships is Bootstrap's; § Tailwind states how a
paired build keeps that true.

The `utility` mixin in the `src/styles/_mixins.scss` file writes a utility key's classes, and the
`utility-variable` mixin writes a utility entry whose value is a `--bs-*` custom property alone, as
a release `css-var` utility is. The `src/styles/utilities/_gap.scss` partial writes its gap keys
through the `utility` mixin; its gutter classes are the release's grid classes rather than utility
entries, and stay hand-written with normal declarations. The `utility` mixin names each class the
way the release's utility API names it: the class, then the breakpoint infix, then a hyphen and the
value's key, so the `gap` utility's
step `3` at the `-md` infix is `.gap-md-3`. An entry with no class drops the infix's leading
hyphen, as the release does. Each pseudo-class an entry names as a state adds a class after the base
class, suffixed with a hyphen and that pseudo-class and matched only in that state, so a `hover`
state pairs a class with its `-hover` variant under the `:hover` pseudo-class. The `utility` mixin
writes every property with `!important` and every local variable in `$locals` as a normal
declaration. The `utility-variable` mixin writes its custom property as a normal declaration, as
the release writes a `css-var` utility, so a rule that reads the variable decides its own priority.
The `tests/src/styles/mixins.test.ts` proof reads the mixins' naming, their breakpoint gating, their
state classes, and the priority of each declaration they write, from a fixture that calls them the
way a utility partial does.

Override an important utility from inside that utility's own layer, which your sheet re-opens by
name. An important declaration in a layer beats an important declaration outside every layer,
because the cascade reverses layer order for important declarations and sorts the unlayered ones
last, so an unlayered `!important` of your own leaves the shipped utility in place.

```css
@layer utilities {
	.row-gap-1 {
		row-gap: 2rem !important;
	}
}
```

The token proof executes the escape: that sheet loads after the shipped cascade and moves the
resolved `row-gap` to `2rem`, beside an unlayered override of the same declaration that leaves the
shipped `0.25rem` in place; see [token parity and values](../tests/src/styles/tokens.test.ts).

The barrel's `@use` rules name the `_tokens.scss` and `_theme.scss` partials and the element
partials under the `elements/`, `components/`, and `utilities/` directories; the `_mixins.scss` partial reaches the build through the
token and theme partials rather than through the barrel. The entry imports the `./index.scss`
barrel and nothing else, and the JavaScript wrapper the build emits from it stays unexported,
because the `./styles` subpath names the stylesheet.

A rule in the `elements` layer treats a tag by its name, never by where the markup puts that tag.
The exception is a pair the HTML content model mandates, where the descendant is legal only under
the parents the `MANDATED_TAG_PAIRS` constant in the `tests/setupStyles.ts` module lists for it,
such as the `li` element under the `ol` and `ul` elements. The browser's own selector engine answers
the question: the `scanPositionalPairs` function in the `tests/setupBrowser.ts` module mounts each
styled tag alone, then inside each tag (itself included), then after each tag, and compares the
rules the `Element.matches` method reports across those placements. A rule reaching a tag through
its position reports as a pair. Nothing here parses a selector, and a construct such as the `:has()`
or `:is()` pseudo-class is answered by the engine that ships it.

A bare button is a `button` element that carries no `class` attribute and no `data-bs-target`
attribute, and the calibrated button surface and its states reach a bare button alone. Every other
button takes the release's reboot alone from the `elements` layer, at the release's values: no
margin, the parent's font family, size, and line height, square corners, no text transform, the
button appearance, the pointer cursor while enabled, and no outline on a focus the browser does not
mark as visible. So the `elements` layer paints no surface of its own on a component's button form,
and a disabled `button.nav-link` element reads the same opacity and type as the disabled
`a.nav-link` element beside it. A button carrying a class of your own, a utility class, or an empty
`class` attribute takes that reboot and nothing more from the `elements` layer. The
`data-bs-target` attribute keeps the release's carousel indicators out as well, because the release
gives a resting indicator no class. The attribute sits on the tag itself, so the rule still treats
the tag by what it carries rather than by where the markup puts it. Add the `btn` class to a classed
button to paint it with the Button treatment. The elements proof reads a classed button, an empty
`class` attribute, and a `data-bs-target` button resolving the reboot alone beside the bare
button's calibrated values; see
[the bare button proof](../tests/src/styles/elements/button.test.ts).

The wrapper replaces the plugins, the output directory, the library entry, the build options
(keeping the root's build-log handler and dropping the browser externals and output paths), and the
test fields it inherits, and it declares the `src:styles` project. The check-only project extends
the root `tsconfig.json` file, narrows the `lib` option to the `ESNext` value and the `types` option
to the `vite/client` value over the `src/styles/**/*.ts` sources, and emits nothing. The styles
proofs load the host-independent `tests/setupStyles.ts` module, which holds the case tables and the
markup strings, the value lists copied from Bootstrap's own stylesheet and from Elements' built
showcase, the shadow readers, and the selector normalizer. They read the installed cascade through
the Node-only `tests/setupServer.ts` module; the `tests/setup.ts` module carries the shared helpers
and the `tests/setupBrowser.ts` module the DOM helpers. Each setup module has its own proof of the
same name, and none imports a stylesheet: the styles project loads the built cascade through its
`setupFiles` array instead. Every module test under `tests/src/styles/` other than the
`integration.test.ts` file names a source module at the same relative path under the `src/styles/`
directory, a leading-underscore partial resolved, which the `npm run test:policy` command enforces,
and the `tests/src/styles/integration.test.ts` proof reads the customization recipe beside them.
§ Tests links the cascade-wide proofs, the document and body baselines, the class proofs, and the
gutter utilities; each remaining tag proof sits beside its element partial.

### Tailwind

Veneer declares no Tailwind dependency and ships no rule whose reason is Tailwind. A consumer who
already builds with Tailwind pairs the two by choosing a profile, which is the entry stylesheet
their build compiles. Veneer supports Tailwind 4.3.

The following table names each profile, what its entry declares, and where the pairing is proved.

| Profile      | Entry                                                                       | Layers Tailwind fills in a consumer build | Tailwind parts                                          | Proof                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `standalone` | The cascade alone.                                                          | None.                                     | None.                                                   | [layer order and position independence](../tests/src/styles/index.test.ts)                                                                 |
| `tailwind`   | The order line, the composable imports, the cascade, then the source rules. | `theme` and `utilities`.                  | `tailwindcss/theme.css` and `tailwindcss/utilities.css` | [stylesheet profiles](../tests/service/tailwind/profiles.test.ts) and [the consumer pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/consumer.test.ts)   |
| `preflight`  | The order line, the bare import, the cascade, then the source rules.        | `theme`, `base`, and `utilities`.         | `tailwindcss`                                           | [stylesheet profiles](../tests/service/tailwind/profiles.test.ts) and [the preflight pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/preflight.test.ts) |

Under the composable imports, Tailwind fills a layer only for the utilities it generates from the
markup your `@source` rule names: the `utilities` layer carries those rules and the `theme` layer
carries the variables those rules read. A build whose markup uses no Tailwind utility therefore
fills no layer at all. The bare import differs, because preflight is not generated from your
markup: it fills `base` and reads font variables of its own, so the `preflight` profile carries
`theme` and `base` whatever your markup uses. The stylesheet profiles proof reads that
difference; see [stylesheet profiles](../tests/service/tailwind/profiles.test.ts).

Where a generated utility registers a custom property of its own, Tailwind also generates a
`properties` layer and declares `@layer properties;` ahead of the order line your entry wrote. That
placement adds a layer in front of Veneer's and leaves Veneer's named layers in their declared
order. The profiles proof reads both orders, the compiled stylesheet's own and the one the document
resolves against; see [stylesheet profiles](../tests/service/tailwind/profiles.test.ts). It takes
the document's order as the first placement of each layer across the built cascade followed by the
compiled profile, which is the sequence in which a page links the cascade and then loads the
profile; the proof fixes that sequence rather than observing it on a page.

The `standalone` profile is the product, and § Styles states it: import `@orkestrel/veneer/styles`
and nothing else.

In each recipe that follows, the `@source './src'` line is the one you change: it names your own
markup directory, which is what Tailwind scans to decide which utilities to generate. A `@source`
rule is unknown to a browser, so the placement rule that drops an `@import` rule written after one
is not the browser's own: it is the `postcss-import` plugin's, and Vite runs that plugin ahead of
the Tailwind plugin that would otherwise see the file. The plugin refuses an `@import` rule preceded
by anything other than a `@charset` rule, a comment, an empty `@layer` statement, or another
`@import` rule, and drops it. The plugin follows CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5 for the rules
a browser treats as valid ahead of an `@import` rule; see [§ Importing Style
Sheets](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-5/#at-import) and [§ Declaring Without
Styles](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-5/#layer-empty). Each recipe writes its imports first, so
the rule holds whichever tool inlines them. The first recipe is the `tailwind` profile, which
composes Tailwind's theme and utilities and leaves the reset to Veneer's own `reset` and `elements`
layers.

```css
@layer theme, reset, base, elements, components, utilities;
@import 'tailwindcss/theme.css' layer(theme);
@import 'tailwindcss/utilities.css' layer(utilities);
@import '@orkestrel/veneer/styles';
/* Your own markup directory. */
@source './src';
@source not inline("caption-bottom caption-top col-auto col-1 col-2 col-3 col-4 col-5 col-6 col-7 col-8 col-9 col-10 col-11 col-12 collapse container table end-0 end-50 end-100 start-0 start-50 start-100 shadow shadow-sm shadow-lg shadow-none border-1 border-2 border-3 border-4 border-5 text-wrap text-nowrap mx-0 mx-1 mx-2 mx-3 mx-4 mx-5 mx-auto my-0 my-1 my-2 my-3 my-4 my-5 my-auto me-0 me-1 me-2 me-3 me-4 me-5 me-auto ms-0 ms-1 ms-2 ms-3 ms-4 ms-5 ms-auto px-0 px-1 px-2 px-3 px-4 px-5 py-0 py-1 py-2 py-3 py-4 py-5 pe-0 pe-1 pe-2 pe-3 pe-4 pe-5 ps-0 ps-1 ps-2 ps-3 ps-4 ps-5");
```

The following recipe is the `preflight` profile, which takes the bare import so Tailwind's own reset
fills the `base` layer. Veneer's `elements` layer sits after the `base` layer, so the reset arrives
under Veneer's element treatment rather than over it.

```css
@layer theme, reset, base, elements, components, utilities;
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@orkestrel/veneer/styles';
/* Your own markup directory. */
@source './src';
@source not inline("caption-bottom caption-top col-auto col-1 col-2 col-3 col-4 col-5 col-6 col-7 col-8 col-9 col-10 col-11 col-12 collapse container table end-0 end-50 end-100 start-0 start-50 start-100 shadow shadow-sm shadow-lg shadow-none border-1 border-2 border-3 border-4 border-5 text-wrap text-nowrap mx-0 mx-1 mx-2 mx-3 mx-4 mx-5 mx-auto my-0 my-1 my-2 my-3 my-4 my-5 my-auto me-0 me-1 me-2 me-3 me-4 me-5 me-auto ms-0 ms-1 ms-2 ms-3 ms-4 ms-5 ms-auto px-0 px-1 px-2 px-3 px-4 px-5 py-0 py-1 py-2 py-3 py-4 py-5 pe-0 pe-1 pe-2 pe-3 pe-4 pe-5 ps-0 ps-1 ps-2 ps-3 ps-4 ps-5");
```

The workspace compiles the `tailwind` recipe as written. The `tests/fixtures/tailwind/consumer.css`
fixture is that fence with one line changed — its `@source './markup.html';` line names the markup
fixture beside it in place of your own directory — and the consumer pairing holds every other line
of the file equal to the fence, so a recipe edited here and not there reddens rather than shipping a
recipe nothing compiled; see [the consumer pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/consumer.test.ts). The
workspace compiles the recipe with the installed PostCSS plugin in Node, from the fixture's own
path, so the `@orkestrel/veneer/styles` specifier resolves through the manifest's `exports` entry
the way a consumer's install resolves it, and no alias, wrapper, or bundler stands in. The same
proof reads the sheet that recipe compiles to: the sheet carries Veneer's token namespace and its
component rules; the markup's `px-8` utility is generated, so the `@source` line reached the
scanner; every element carrying a shared class name resolves exactly what the shipped cascade alone
resolves for it; and the `px-8` utility moves the button's padding off the `.btn` declaration, which
is the override a consumer pairs Tailwind for. The `tests/fixtures/tailwind/unexcluded.css` fixture
is the negative control: with the exclusion line dropped, the same reading moves the
`grid-column-start` property of the `.col-1` element from `auto` to `1`, which is what shows the
equality can see a Tailwind rule winning.

The order line never changes between profiles. It is the line the `src/styles/_tokens.scss`
file declares, and declaring it ahead of the Tailwind import is what makes Tailwind's own
narrower order merge as a no-op.

A button styled with utility classes carries a `class` attribute, so it is no bare button and takes
the release's reboot rather than the calibrated surface, as § Styles states. Add the `btn` class
where that button needs the Button treatment; a utility in the `utilities` layer still overrides the
`btn` class declaration it shares a property with.

The exclusion line names the class names Veneer and Tailwind both declare. A shared name leaves
the exclusion line only where Veneer declares with `!important` every longhand that Tailwind's
rule for that name declares; a name Veneer declares important on some other longhand stays on the
line, because that importance does not cover every longhand Tailwind's rule would otherwise win.
The line withholds a name that stays on it from Tailwind's generation, so Veneer's declaration is
the only one the page carries for it. The `collapse` class is one such name: Tailwind's `collapse`
utility writes `visibility: collapse`, so a paired build that generated it would hide every shown
panel. [The consumer pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/consumer.test.ts) reads the `.collapse.show`
element in its markup fixture as visible, which is what the shipped cascade alone resolves for it.

The `tests/setup.css` file is where the workspace writes that line. The profiles proof reads it from
that file rather than repeating it, and holds every written copy equal to it — the recipes in this
section and the `tests/fixtures/tailwind/preflight.css` and `tests/fixtures/tailwind/consumer.css`
files; see [stylesheet profiles](../tests/service/tailwind/profiles.test.ts). So a release that
ships another shared class name extends the line, and every copy left behind reddens until it
matches.

Nothing writes the shared set down either; see [the consumer
pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/consumer.test.ts). That proof derives it per run as the class
names the built cascade and the unexcluded instrument both declare, and asserts that the
`container`, `table`, `col-1`, `caption-top`, and `caption-bottom` classes are among them, so a
derivation that reached an empty stylesheet cannot read as a clean result. It then holds the
exclusion line equal to the derived names that the rule stated with the exclusion line keeps on the
line, which states that rule as an equality: a name that joins the set joins the line, and a name
that gains the `!important` declarations the rule asks for leaves the line. The proof reads
Tailwind's longhands from the unexcluded instrument and Veneer's importance from the built cascade,
each as Chromium expands it, so a shorthand counts as the longhands it sets. The importance branch
runs over the shared names that rule lets leave the line. The gap steps `gap-0` to `gap-5` are
shipped names off the line: Tailwind's rule for each declares the `gap` shorthand, which Chromium
expands to the `row-gap` and `column-gap` longhands, and Veneer declares the same shorthand with
`!important`. Every other shipped name off the line reads the same way; Tailwind's `order-first`
rule declares the `order` longhand alone, and Veneer declares it with `!important`, so the
`order-first` class resolves Veneer's `-1` rather than Tailwind's `-9999`. The width and height
steps, the `top-*` and `bottom-*` offsets, the `z-0` to `z-3` levels, and the `visible` and
`invisible` classes are shipped names off the line too: Tailwind's rule for each declares the one
longhand Veneer declares with `!important`. The `start-*` and `end-*` offsets stay on the line:
Tailwind's rule for each declares the logical `inset-inline-start` or `inset-inline-end` longhand,
and Veneer's important declaration is on the physical `left` or `right` longhand, which does not
cover it. The `opacity-0` to `opacity-100` steps are shipped names off the line: Tailwind's rule for
each declares the one `opacity` longhand Veneer declares with the `!important` flag. The `shadow`,
`shadow-sm`, `shadow-lg`, and `shadow-none` classes stay on the line: Tailwind's rule for each
declares the `--tw-shadow` custom property beside the `box-shadow` longhand, the proof counts a
custom property among the longhands a rule declares, and Veneer's important declaration is on the
`box-shadow` longhand alone. The `float-*` sides and every `overflow-*`, `overflow-x-*`, and
`overflow-y-*` class are shipped names off the line. Tailwind's `float-start` and `float-end` rules
declare the `float` longhand at the logical `inline-start` and `inline-end` values, and Veneer
declares the same longhand with the `!important` flag at the physical `left` and `right` values, so
a paired build floats each box to the physical side the release names. Tailwind's `overflow-*` rules
declare the `overflow` shorthand, which Chromium expands to the `overflow-x` and `overflow-y`
longhands, and Veneer declares the same shorthand with the `!important` flag. The proof asserts that
the `gap-3` name is in the branch and reads what the rule claims: with the exclusion line dropped
and Tailwind's own rule on the page, every element carrying a name in the branch resolves, for every
property that rule declares, what it resolves under the cascade alone. Each element is read on the
longhands its own name's rule declares, because a longhand another name declares can move for a
reason outside the equality: the gap rows sit inside the `.container` element, whose width moves
when the line is dropped, and the width steps declare the `width` longhand. A planted rule drives
the partial-importance case: it declares `!important` on the `grid-column-start` longhand alone,
leaving the `grid-column-end` longhand that Tailwind's `col-1` rule also declares normal, and the
equality still holds with the `col-1` class on the line.
cover it. The `bg-black`, `bg-white`, `bg-transparent`, `border-black`, `border-white`, and
`rounded` classes are shipped names off the line: Tailwind's rule for each declares the background
color, the border color, or the corner radii that Veneer declares with the `!important` flag. So are
the `border` and `border-0` classes: Tailwind's rule for each declares the border style and width
longhands, and Veneer's `border` shorthand sets both with the `!important` flag. The `border-1` to
`border-5` widths stay on the line: Tailwind's rule for each declares the border style longhands
beside the widths, and Veneer's important declaration is on the widths alone. The proof asserts that
cover it. The `text-start`, `text-end`, and `text-center` alignments and the `text-black` and
`text-white` colors are shipped names off the line: Tailwind's rule for each declares the
`text-align` or the `color` longhand, which Veneer declares with the `!important` flag, so the
`text-start` class resolves Veneer's physical `left` value rather than Tailwind's logical `start`
value. The `text-wrap` and `text-nowrap` classes stay on the line: Tailwind's rule for each declares
the `text-wrap` shorthand, which Chromium expands to the `text-wrap-mode` and `text-wrap-style`
longhands, and Veneer's important `white-space` shorthand expands to the `white-space-collapse` and
`text-wrap-mode` longhands, which leave the `text-wrap-style` longhand uncovered. The proof asserts
that the `gap-3` name is in the branch and reads what the rule claims:

The margin and padding steps split the same way the offsets do. The `m-*`, `mt-*`, `mb-*`, `p-*`,
`pt-*`, and `pb-*` names are shipped names off the line: Tailwind's rule for each declares the
physical margin or padding longhands, and Veneer declares each of those with the `!important` flag.
The `mx-*`, `my-*`, `me-*`, `ms-*`, `px-*`, `py-*`, `pe-*`, and `ps-*` names stay on the line:
Tailwind's rule for each declares logical longhands, such as the `margin-inline-start` or the
`padding-block-end` longhand, and Veneer's important declarations sit on the physical sides, which
do not cover them. The `pe-none`, `pe-auto`, and `user-select-*` names are not shared, because
Tailwind writes those as the `pointer-events-none`, `pointer-events-auto`, and `select-*` utilities.

The workspace executes the profiles from `tests/setup.css` for the `tailwind` profile and
`tests/fixtures/tailwind/preflight.css` for the `preflight` profile. Those profiles scan a
candidate list derived from the built cascade rather than your markup, so every utility an executed
profile emits is a shared name, and the stylesheet profiles proof holds each profile's emitted
utilities equal to the shared names off the exclusion line, the gap steps among them. A name that
stays on the line is withheld, and a name that leaves it is generated and loses to Veneer's
important declaration. The `tests/fixtures/tailwind/unexcluded.css` instrument drops the line and
adds an `@source inline(…)` control naming utilities the cascade declares no class for, so its
compilation emits something whatever the line holds, and the composed imports are read from what
it emits.

The proofs under `tests/service/tailwind/` run in the `service` project. They compile each profile
in Node through the installed `@tailwindcss/postcss` plugin, from the profile's own path; they read
what a compiled sheet declares from its text, and what a page resolves from a headless Chromium page
that links the built cascade. Before any proof runs, the `tests/setupService.ts` module verifies the
compiler, the built cascade, the pinned Chromium, and the candidate list, writes that list, and
refuses loudly, naming the command that restores each gate where one does. Run the
`npm run build:src:styles` command, then the `npm run test:service` command. The `prepublishOnly`
chain runs the `test:service` script, and the `test` script does not.

Veneer's `elements` layer sits after the `base` layer, so Tailwind's reset arrives under Veneer's
own element treatment rather than over it: every property Veneer declares for an overlapping element
keeps the value the standalone cascade resolves for it, and what the `preflight` profile adds is the
properties Veneer leaves alone; see [the preflight
pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/preflight.test.ts). That proof derives the overlap — the tags the
compiled `base` layer's type selectors name, intersected with the tags Veneer's elements partials
style — renders one neutral element per tag, and reads every longhand that layer declares, as
Chromium expands it, before and after the profile loads. Each property Veneer's own rules declare
for the tag is asserted unchanged, and each property that moved is a row of the following table.

The border style and the tab size move on every overlapping element, because the reset's universal
rule declares them: it sets a border style the elements never paint, because it sets the border
width to zero beside it, and it lowers the tab size. The rest of the rows are the form controls and
the document root, which preflight resets to inherit the page's own font, color, and background.

The `Tag`, `Property`, `Standalone`, and `Preflight` columns name the element, the property, the
value the shipped cascade alone resolves for it, and the value the `preflight` profile resolves,
each read on Chromium 141. A build's own user-agent default for an element such as `select` or
`table` moves the standalone column across a Chromium version, so the proof compares each measured
move by tag, property, and the preflight value alone, and asserts the measured standalone value
differs from it, rather than equating a user-agent default with a recorded reading. The Standalone
column stays the Chromium 141 reading, informational. The proof holds the measured pairs and the
recorded rows equal by tag, property, and preflight value, in both directions, so a move this table
does not carry and a row the pairing no longer produces each redden.

### Scripts

Each styles script names the styles target alone, and the `src` chain it belongs to runs it after
the core and browser targets. The `test:service` script runs the Tailwind proofs, and the
`prepublishOnly` chain runs it.

| Script             | Contract                                                                                                                                | Chained from                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `build:src:styles` | Builds the `dist/src/styles` directory from the `configs/src/vite.styles.config.ts` wrapper.                                            | The `build:src` chain, after the `build:src:core` and `build:src:browser` scripts.        |
| `check:src:styles` | Typechecks the `src/styles/**/*.ts` sources against the `configs/src/tsconfig.styles.json` project.                                     | The `check:src` chain, after the `check:src:core` and `check:src:browser` scripts.        |
| `test:src:styles`  | Builds the cascade, then runs the `src:styles` project.                                                                                 | The `test:src` chain, after the root's `src:core` and `src:browser` projects.             |
| `test:service`     | Runs the `service` project, whose proofs under `tests/service/tailwind/` drive the installed Tailwind compiler and the pinned Chromium. | The `prepublishOnly` chain, after the `test:distribution` script; never the `test` chain. |

The `test:src:styles` script builds first because the proof's subject is the compiled cascade: the
project loads the `dist/src/styles/index.css` file through its `setupFiles` array, and a case
reading that file reads the rules the browser resolved from it rather than the declarations the SCSS
sources carry. The mixin proofs compile their own `tests/src/styles/fixtures/mixins.scss` fixture
partial, and the token proofs also drive declarations the case writes.

The `test:service` script does not build. The `service` project's readiness refuses a missing
`dist/src/styles/index.css` file and names the `npm run build:src:styles` command, and the
`prepublishOnly` chain runs the `npm run build` command, which builds the styles target, before the
`test:service` script.

### Table classes

The table key ships whole, including compact cells, bordered and borderless cells, row and column
stripes, active and hover states, contextual colors, the group divider, the caption class, and
responsive wrappers.

Veneer's `elements` treatment puts a caption above its table, so the family carries a second caption
class beside Bootstrap's `.caption-top` class: the `.caption-bottom` class returns one caption to
the bottom placement Bootstrap's own `caption` rule gives every caption. It is Veneer's own addition
to that family, and both classes sit in the `components` layer at the same specificity, so a caption
carrying the pair resolves to `bottom`, the later of the two rules.

Cells resolve state color before stripe color before base color. Their inset shadow resolves state
background before stripe background before accent background; the base background paints underneath.
The stripe alias reads the existing `--vn-state-stripe` percentage. Active and hover retain the
recorded 10% and 7.5% accents; Button's 22% and 12% percentages do not change table states.

Contextual table backgrounds tint the canonical role fill with white at 20%, except light and dark,
which use their canonical fills directly. Borders mix the text into that background at 20%; stripe,
active, and hover mixes use 5%, 10%, and 7.5%. This is a recorded color departure: the canonical
palette retunes Bootstrap's fixed contextual colors, and runtime mixes retain fractional channels
instead of rounding them to hexadecimal bytes. The state slots and their precedence are retained.
The class restores inherited cell alignment and border color over the bare-cell treatment: header
cells resolve bottom, body cells resolve top, and cell borders receive the table's contextual color.
Class padding overrides the bare cell's density spacing.

Responsive wrappers use physical horizontal overflow, and the `breakpoint-each-down` mixin writes
every wrapper from one rule set. Their overflow scrolls below the named boundary and is absent at
and above it. The unconditional wrapper scrolls at every viewport. The vocabulary proof compares
Bootstrap's `max-width: (N - 0.02)px` boundary with Veneer's `width < Npx` form by adding 0.02 to
the recorded boundary.

### Form label classes

The form label partial ships the form label, the help text, and the horizontal label at each size.
The release records the form label and the help text under the umbrella `form` key and the
horizontal labels under the `col` key, so the ledger files each one there. With this partial the
`form` key ships whole: every other rule the umbrella key records ships from the partial of the key
its classes name, and the switch row's inset ships from the check partial.

A label sits above its control, and help text sits under its control at `0.875em` of the type around
it, in the secondary text color. Name the help text as the control's description through the
`aria-describedby` attribute, so a screen reader announces the help text after the control's name. A
horizontal label, or a `legend` element that labels a horizontal group, takes the control's own
block inset plus the control's border width, and the control's line height, so its line box opens
level with the control's at each size. A sized label takes the sized control's type step. The
unsized horizontal label reads `--vn-size-3`, the control's type step, so its text sits level with
the control's, and the stacked `.form-label` class keeps inheriting the surrounding type. On a
`legend` element the horizontal label also clears the element's own trailing margin and type size,
so the legend reads at its control's type step.

These are the keys' recorded departures.

- **The margins read the space scale.** The label's trailing margin reads `--vn-space-4` and the
  help text's leading margin reads `--vn-space-2`, so each rescales with `--vn-factor-density`.
- **The horizontal label reads the control's inset and type tokens.** Its block inset reads
  `--vn-space-3`, `--vn-space-4`, or `--vn-space-2` over `--bs-border-width`, and its type reads
  `--vn-size-3`, `--vn-size-5`, or `--vn-size-2` with `--vn-line-body`, the tokens the control of
  the same size reads.
  The label and its control therefore move together under `--vn-factor-density` and under a
  `--bs-border-width` retune.

The help text's `0.875em` size stays the release's value, because no published Veneer scale is
relative to the element's own font size, and its color reads `--bs-secondary-color` byte for byte,
so a retune of that variable repaints the help text. Neither records a departure, and neither does
the horizontal label's `0` margin, which is the release's own value.

The showcase's Form label region carries a label above its control with the help text the control
names as its description, and a horizontal label level with the control beside it at each size and
as the legend of a group.

The form label proof reads the resolved treatment in the browser; see [the form label
classes](../tests/src/styles/components/form-label.test.ts). It reads the label's margin at the
resting and a doubled density, the help text's margin, its size under a `20px` parent, and its color
against the resolved `--bs-secondary-color` in each mode and under a wrapper override, the
horizontal label's content box level with its control's at each size, at a doubled density, and
under a `4px` border-width and a line-height retune, each horizontal label's type step and the sized
labels' insets, the legend's cleared margin and its control's type step, and the components layer.
Each case table is held against the pinned inventory; see [the styles setup
proof](../tests/setupStyles.test.ts). The capture journey writes a resting element frame of each
specimen.

### Form control classes

The text-control key ships whole: the control itself, its file button, date parts, and placeholder,
its focus and disabled states, the plaintext form, the small and large sizes, the textarea heights,
the color control and its swatches, and the reduced-motion twins of the control and file-button
transitions. The rules keyed to a bare element or a bare part stay in the elements layer — the
date-field padding, the color swatch wrapper's padding, and the file button's font and appearance —
and the `src/styles/components/_form-control.scss` partial restates none of them.

The file button ships on the standard `::file-selector-button` part. The prefixed
`::-webkit-file-upload-button` alias the official cascade also writes, with its hover and size
forms, is withheld under § Deferred selectors with the `Excluded` owner, because the partial does
not write that alias and the standard part paints the same button. The button's inline-end margin
and inline-end border ship as the logical properties the official cascade compiles, written as it
writes them, and Chromium resolves them as the right margin and right border the release draws.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The geometry reads the space and type scales.** The control's padding, the file button's padding
  and its cancelling margins, the plaintext form's block padding, each size's padding and type step,
  and the color control's width and padding read the `--vn-space-2`, `--vn-space-3`, `--vn-space-4`,
  `--vn-space-6`, `--vn-space-8`, and `--vn-space-24` tokens and the `--vn-size-2`, `--vn-size-3`,
  and `--vn-size-5` tokens; the weight and line height read the `--vn-weight-body` and
  `--vn-line-body` tokens. Each resolves to the official value at the default factors, and the whole
  control rescales with the `--vn-factor-density` factor as the shipped partials do.
- **The heights multiply the padding token.** A textarea's minimum height, each size's minimum
  height, and the color control's height are the line box plus the block padding twice plus the
  border twice, which is how the official cascade derives them, so each reads the padding token
  multiplied by two: at the default factor the height is the official value, and a density retune
  moves the padding and the height together.
- **The focus ring binds the focus tokens.** The official shadow is a quarter-rem ring in the
  official brand color; Veneer reads the `--vn-focus-width` and `--vn-focus-color` tokens, the
  binding the `.btn` class already carries, which resolves to a `0.1875rem` ring. The focused border
  mixes half of the `--vn-palette-blue` entry over the `--vn-palette-white-base` entry, which lands
  within one channel step of the official `#86b7fe` value in either mode. The border reads the
  palette entry rather than the primary role, so a `--vn-color-primary-base` retune leaves it on the
  release's tint, and a `--vn-palette-blue` retune moves it.
- **The transitions read the motion tokens.** The official timing is the `0.15s ease-in-out` value;
  Veneer writes the `var(--vn-motion-feedback) var(--vn-ease-standard)` value, which resolves to the
  `0.15s ease` value, and emits each reduced-motion twin through the shared transition mixin.
- **The prefixed appearance aliases are absent.** The official cascade writes the
  `-webkit-appearance` and `-moz-appearance` properties beside the standard property; the build's
  targets emit the standard property alone.

Under forced colors the focused control's rule also writes an outline in the system highlight
color through the `forced-ring` mixin, because forced colors paint no shadow ring. § Additions
records it.
The validation partial's focus rules write a border and a shadow and no outline, so a validated
control keeps that outline. The plaintext form's focus rule writes the release's `outline: 0`
declaration and no ring. The plaintext form therefore draws no focus indicator in any mode, so
forced colors remove nothing there and the rule includes no outline.

The text, surface, border, placeholder, disabled, and file-button colors, the radii, and the border
width read the `--bs-*` variables this package already declares, so each matches the official
value and records no departure. The `.form-control.is-valid:focus` and
`.form-control.is-invalid:focus` rows of the validation partial are recorded under this key,
because the ledger attributes a selector to the most specific shipped key among its own classes.
The validated color control's width is the same `--vn-space-24` token the resting one reads plus
the icon room, so a density retune widens the resting and the validated color control together.

The form control proof reads each recorded declaration on the control its selector matches and
records each limit that bounds what it can claim beside the reading it bounds; see
[the form control classes](../tests/src/styles/components/form-control.test.ts). Each part, and the
file control's `overflow` declaration, takes one rung of the evidence ladder:

- The `::placeholder` and `::file-selector-button` parts have resolved readings, the part's own
  color, geometry, hover surface, and transition included.
- The `::-webkit-date-and-time-value`, `::-webkit-datetime-edit`, and `::-webkit-color-swatch` parts
  have no resolved reading, because Chromium answers a computed-style request for those parts with
  the control's own style. Their declarations are read out of the CSSOM, which is compiled-contract
  evidence rather than a rendered reading, with each declaration's priority read beside its value.
  The `form-control-date` frame shows the rendered date fields, and the `form-control-color` frame
  shows the rendered swatch.
- The `::-moz-color-swatch` part has no reading in this browser at all, because Chromium discards a
  selector naming a Gecko part at parse time. The Node binding case reads its declarations and their
  priority out of the compiled cascade; see [the styles setup proof](../tests/setupStyles.test.ts).
- The file control's `overflow` declaration has no resolved reading either, because the user agent
  already resolves every text and file control to the `clip` value; its declaration is read out of
  the CSSOM.

The focus ring is read after keyboard traversal and its contrast ratio is held to the calibrated
ratio the Button sweep pins in each mode. The outline is read under staged forced colors on the text
control and on a validated one, by its style and width, because a color reading cannot fail under
forced colors: the installed color reader resolves each side through a probe whose color forced
colors also replace. The capture journey writes a resting element frame of every specimen and a page
frame of the text control under keyboard focus.

### Form select classes

The select key ships every rule the release writes on the select itself: the control, its focus, its
list forms, its disabled surface, the Gecko focus-ring reset, the small and large sizes, the
reduced-motion twin of its transition, and the dark caret rule. The floating-label and input-group
rules the key also records belong to those components' own partials, and the validation rules on the
select ship from the `src/styles/components/_validation.scss` partial.

The caret is the release's own glyph. A data URI cannot read a custom property, so the caret comes
from the maps in the `src/styles/_tokens.scss` file at compile time: the
`--bs-form-select-bg-img` property on the `.form-select` class takes the icon map's
`select-indicator` entry, and the release's own `[data-bs-theme='dark'] .form-select` rule takes
the dark map's entry of the same name. Both declarations sit on the element, and the dark theme
scope declares nothing for that variable, so the component rules decide the caret in both modes.
The dark rule matches any select under a dark scope, so a light island nested
inside a dark one keeps the dark caret, as it does in the official cascade. The image reads the
`--bs-form-select-bg-img` property and then the `--bs-form-select-bg-icon` property, so retune the
caret on the select itself and add a mark through the second property, which is how the validation
classes add theirs.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The select's spacing reads the space scale.** The padding, the caret's inset, and the size
  classes' padding read the `--vn-space-2`, `--vn-space-3`, `--vn-space-4`, `--vn-space-6`, and
  `--vn-space-8` tokens, and the end padding that clears the caret is the `--vn-space-6` token three
  times over, the release's own derivation. A select with no validation state rescales with the
  `--vn-factor-density` token as the shipped partials do. A validation state keeps the release's
  literal icon geometry, as § Validation classes states, so a validated single-row select keeps the
  release's end padding and caret inset at any density. A validated list form (a `[multiple]`
  attribute, or a `[size]` attribute above one row) carries no caret and keeps the list padding,
  which follows density. The caret's own `16px 12px` size stays literal.
- **The select's type reads the size, weight, and line scales.** The font size reads the
  `--vn-size-3` token, and the `--vn-size-2` and `--vn-size-5` tokens on the small and large
  selects; the weight and line height read the `--vn-weight-body` and `--vn-line-body` tokens. Each
  resolves to the official value.
- **The focus treatment binds the focus tokens.** The official ring is a quarter-rem literal in the
  official brand color; the partial writes the `0 0 0 var(--vn-focus-width) var(--vn-focus-color)`
  value, the binding the `.btn` class already carries, which resolves to a `0.1875rem` ring. The
  focused border is the official tint written as half the `--vn-palette-blue` token over the
  `--vn-palette-white-base` token, the mix the official cascade bakes into its `#86b7fe` literal.
  The border reads the palette entry rather than the primary role, so a `--vn-color-primary-base`
  retune leaves it on the release's tint, and a `--vn-palette-blue` retune moves it.
- **The transition reads the motion tokens.** The official cascade writes the `0.15s ease-in-out`
  value; the partial writes the `var(--vn-motion-feedback) var(--vn-ease-standard)` value, which
  resolves to the `0.15s ease` value, and emits the reduced-motion twin through the shared transition mixin.
- **The prefixed appearance aliases are absent.** The official cascade writes the
  `-webkit-appearance` and `-moz-appearance` aliases beside the standard property; the build's
  targets emit the standard property alone.
- **The validated select's focus ring is measured here.** The ledger attributes the
  `.form-select.is-valid:focus` and `.form-select.is-invalid:focus` selectors to this key, the
  longest class each selector carries, so their tokenized ring width is recorded under this key's
  table rather than under the validation keys'.

Under forced colors the focused select's rule also writes an outline in the system highlight color
through the `forced-ring` mixin, because forced colors paint no shadow ring. § Additions records
it.

The fill, the text, the border, the corners, the disabled surface, and the Gecko reset read the
`--bs-body-bg`, `--bs-body-color`, `--bs-border-width`, and `--bs-border-color` variables, the
`--bs-border-radius` family, and the `--bs-secondary-bg` variable, all of which this package
already declares, so each matches the official value and records no departure.

The select proof reads the resolved treatment in the browser; see [the select
classes](../tests/src/styles/components/form-select.test.ts). Each row of the proof's case table is
resolved on the element its selector matches and compared with the value the same engine resolves
for the official text, so the text and fill colors, the list forms' missing image, and the size
geometry answer to the official record rather than to figures written by hand. The table carries
every declaration the release writes on the select's own rules except the image, the transition and
its reduced-motion twin, and the prefixed appearance aliases on the `.form-select` rule, and the
whole `.form-select:focus` rule. The caret cases read the image in each mode, on a single-row
select, and under a direct retune; the reduced-motion case reads the transition; the keyboard focus
case reads the focused border, ring, and outline, and the forced-colors case reads the outline under
staged forced colors. A wrapper that sets its own text color leaves the select's text in the body
color in each mode. The focused border is held within one channel step of the official tint, because
the official compiler rounds the mix's half-step channel to a whole one and the engine keeps the
half step. Chromium discards the `:-moz-focusring` selector at parse time, so no reading in that
browser reaches the Gecko reset, and the styles setup proof reads its declarations out of the
compiled cascade instead, which is evidence of the compiled contract rather than of a rendered
result; see [the styles setup proof](../tests/setupStyles.test.ts). The capture journey writes a
resting frame of each specimen and a page frame of the plain select under keyboard focus.

### Form check classes

The check key ships whole: the check row and its floated box, the checkbox and radio shapes, the
held, focused, checked, mixed, and disabled states, the reverse and inline layouts, and the switch
with its track, its knob positions, and the reduced-motion twin of the knob transition. The release
records the switch row's own inset only under the umbrella `form` key, and it ships here, because
the switch track needs it. The validation rules that reach a check ship from the
`src/styles/components/_validation.scss` partial. The `.btn-check` rules the release writes in its
own check partial are recorded under the `btn` key, and they ship in Button's own form from the
`src/styles/components/_button.scss` partial. This partial writes none of either.

Each glyph is an escaped SVG data URI with the release's own fill baked into it. A data URI cannot
read a custom property, so the `src/styles/components/_form-check.scss` partial reads each glyph out
of the `$icons` map in the `src/styles/_tokens.scss` file into the `--bs-form-check-bg-image` and
`--bs-form-switch-bg` variables the release writes, and a state rule sets the variable rather than
restating the paint around it. The resting knob is the one glyph the release repaints by mode, so
the partial declares its dark value on the release's own
`[data-bs-theme='dark'] .form-switch .form-check-input:not(:checked):not(:focus)` dark rule, reading
the `switch-knob` entry of the `$dark` map: the theme scopes declare nothing for that variable, so
the control's own rules decide the knob in both modes. The descendant rule also reaches a resting
switch inside a light island nested in a dark one, as the release's own rule does, and the partial
adds no light-scope reset. Retune one control's glyph by declaring the variable on that control.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The row's floor and gaps read the space scale.** The row's minimum height, its trailing margin,
  and the inline row's trailing margin read `--vn-space-12`, `--vn-space-1`, and `--vn-space-8`, so
  each rescales with `--vn-factor-density`. The `em` lengths stay the release's own: they size the
  box, its inset, its radius, and the switch track against the label's type, and no published
  Veneer scale is relative to the element's own font size.
- **The filled states paint the blue palette entry.** The checked and mixed fill and border read
  `--vn-palette-blue`, the entry that resolves to the release's own `#0d6efd`. Every glyph that
  fill carries bakes the release's white, so the fill reads the mode-independent palette entry
  rather than the role fill, which the dark mode lightens under that white. A
  `--vn-color-primary-base` retune therefore leaves a checked box on the release's blue, and a
  `--vn-palette-blue` retune moves it.
- **The focus ring binds the focus tokens, and the focus border tints the blue palette entry.** The
  focused border mixes `--vn-palette-blue` at half strength over `--vn-palette-white-base`, which is
  how the release derives its `#86b7fe`; the exact midpoint reads half a channel step under that
  literal. The ring reads `--vn-focus-width` and `--vn-focus-color`, which resolves to a
  `0.1875rem` ring and is the binding `.btn` already carries. A `--vn-color-primary-base` retune
  moves the ring and leaves the border on the release's tint, and a `--vn-palette-blue` retune moves
  the border.
- **The knob transition reads the motion tokens.** The release's value is `0.15s ease-in-out`;
  Veneer writes `var(--vn-motion-feedback) var(--vn-ease-standard)`, which resolves to `0.15s ease`,
  and emits the reduced-motion twin through the shared transition mixin, as the `.btn` class does.
- **The prefixed appearance and color-adjust aliases are absent from the source.** The release
  writes `-webkit-appearance`, `-moz-appearance`, `-webkit-print-color-adjust`, and `color-adjust`
  beside the standard properties; the partial writes the standard properties alone, and the build
  adds back only the `-webkit-print-color-adjust` alias its targets need.

Under forced colors the focused box's rule also writes an outline in the system highlight color
through the `forced-ring` mixin, because forced colors paint no shadow ring. § Additions records
it.

The resting fill reads `--bs-body-bg`, and the border reads `--bs-border-width` and
`--bs-border-color`, each of which this package already declares, so each matches the release's
value and records no departure.

The check proof reads the resolved treatment in the browser; see [the check
classes](../tests/src/styles/components/form-check.test.ts). It reads the row and box geometry, each
shape, the resting fill in the light and dark modes, the filled states against the palette entry,
every glyph against the release's own URI, the dark knob, the ring after keyboard traversal and its
ratio in each mode, the outline under staged forced colors, the held and disabled states, the
reverse and inline layouts, and the knob transition at rest and under the staged reduced-motion
preference. Each case table is held against the pinned inventory; see [the styles setup
proof](../tests/setupStyles.test.ts). The capture journey photographs each specimen at rest as an
element frame, the resting checkbox under keyboard focus as a page frame, and a lifted copy of that
checkbox marked mixed as an element frame, because the mixed state is a property no attribute
declares. No proof prints, so the proof reads the `print-color-adjust` declaration as its resolved
value alone.

### Form range classes

The range key ships whole: the control itself, its focus and disabled states, the thumb and the
track each engine names with its own pseudo-element, the held thumb, and the reduced-motion twin of
the thumb transition. No rule keyed to the bare `[type=range]` attribute ships with it, so a slider
carrying no class renders as the user agent paints it.

WebKit and Gecko name the thumb and the track with pseudo-elements of their own, and an engine
discards a selector naming the other engine's. Bootstrap writes the family out once per engine for
that reason, and the `src/styles/components/_form-range.scss` partial emits the same rules from one
declaration of the pair, so a retune reaches both halves together.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The control's geometry reads the space and radius scales.** The control's height, the thumb's
  width and height, its track-centring offset, the track's height, and the thumb and track radius
  read `--vn-space-12`, `--vn-space-8`, `--vn-space-2`, `--vn-space-4`, and `--vn-radius-xlarge`, so
  the whole control rescales with `--vn-factor-density` and `--vn-factor-radius` as the shipped
  partials do.
- **The thumb paints the blue palette entry.** The resting thumb reads `--vn-palette-blue`, the
  entry that resolves to the official cascade's own `#0d6efd`, and the held thumb lightens it to
  three tenths of that entry over `--vn-palette-white-base`, which is the tint the official cascade
  bakes into its own literal. A `--vn-color-primary-base` retune therefore leaves the thumb on the
  official blue, because the rule reads the palette entry rather than the role fill, and a
  `--vn-palette-blue` retune moves it.
- **The focus ring binds the focus tokens.** The official shadow is a hairline over a quarter-rem
  ring in the official brand color; Veneer keeps the hairline and reads `--vn-focus-width` and
  `--vn-focus-color` for the ring, which resolves to a `0.1875rem` ring and is the binding `.btn`
  already carries. The hairline paints `--vn-surface-body-base`, the variable the official cascade
  compiles to white.
- **The thumb transition reads the motion tokens.** The official value is `0.15s ease-in-out`;
  Veneer writes `var(--vn-motion-feedback) var(--vn-ease-standard)`, which resolves to `0.15s ease`,
  and emits the reduced-motion twin through the shared transition mixin, as the `.btn` class does.
- **The prefixed appearance and transition aliases are absent.** The official cascade writes
  `-webkit-appearance`, `-moz-appearance`, `-webkit-transition`, and `-moz-transition` beside the
  standard properties; the build's targets emit the standard property alone.

Under forced colors the focused control's rule writes an outline in the system highlight color on
the host through the `forced-ring` mixin, because forced colors paint no thumb shadow ring.
§ Additions records it.

The track fill reads `--bs-secondary-bg` and the disabled thumb reads `--bs-secondary-color`,
both of which this package already declares, so each matches the official value and records no
departure.

The range proof reads the resolved treatment in the browser, and each limit that bounds what the
proof can claim is recorded there beside the reading it bounds; see [the range
classes](../tests/src/styles/components/form-range.test.ts). Chromium answers a computed-style
request for a slider part with the host's own resolved style rather than the part's, so the thumb's
geometry, paint, and transition have no resolved reading. Chromium discards a selector naming a
Gecko pseudo-element at parse time, so no reading taken in that browser reaches the Gecko half at
all. A pointer hold on a slider part is not reachable through the installed browser exports, and a
hold on the control itself moves the value rather than entering the part's `:active` state, so the
held thumb has a declaration reading and no drive. The styles setup proof reads the declarations
both halves carry out of the compiled cascade; see [the styles setup
proof](../tests/setupStyles.test.ts). The page frame the capture journey writes shows the rendered
thumb and the rendered track; the ring paints on a part with no resolved reading, so its rendered
evidence is open, and its contrast ratio is uncompared for this key because the `readRing` function
reads the chrome the focused element itself wears and this ring sits on a part Chromium withholds.
The host's outline under staged forced colors has a resolved reading, because the host wears it.

### Form floating classes

The floating-label key ships the container and the floated geometry of the controls inside it: the
text control, the plaintext control, and the select. It ships the label with its transforms under
focus, when filled, and when autofilled, beside the reduced-motion twin of the label transition. It
also ships the textarea label backdrop and the disabled and plaintext labels. Where a validation
rule and a floating rule tie on one property, the validation rule wins under the forms order
§ Styles states, so a valid or invalid floating control keeps the end padding its state icon sits
in. The validation partial emits the validation rules the release records against the container. The
input-group partial emits the input-group rules for a floating child, and the ledger attributes a
selector naming both classes to this key, so any departure those rules carry is recorded in this
key's table.

The label sits over its control and fills the container. At rest its inset matches the control's
own, so the label's text sits where the control's text would, and its transparent border matches the
control's border width for the same reason. Keyboard focus, a value, or the browser's autofill
scales the label to `0.85` of its size from its top-left corner and lifts it, and the control's text
moves down to the floated top inset beneath it. A select's label and a plaintext control's label are
floated at rest. The label's text is the body color at `0.65` alpha, so it reads as a hint over the
control rather than as the control's value. A control reports itself empty through
`:placeholder-shown` only when it carries a placeholder, so each floating control carries one, and
the partial hides the placeholder text so the label alone names the control at rest.

A textarea's text scrolls under its floated label, so the label paints a backdrop behind its own
text on the body surface whenever the textarea is focused or filled, and on the secondary surface
when the textarea is `disabled`. The plaintext control draws its border on the block axis alone, and
its label does the same. The label of a `disabled` control paints `--vn-gray-600`, which holds the
release's own gray in both color modes.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The whole control scales with density.** The resting inset of the label and the control, the
  select's start inset, the floated bottom inset, and the backdrop's inset read `--vn-space-8`,
  `--vn-space-6`, `--vn-space-5`, and `--vn-space-3`, the tokens that resolve to the release's
  lengths. No token resolves to the control's `3.5rem` height or to the `1.625rem` floated top
  inset, so each multiplies the `--vn-space-8` token by its ratio to that token's `1rem`: the height
  is `calc(var(--vn-space-8) * 3.5 + calc(var(--bs-border-width) * 2))` and the floated top inset is
  `calc(var(--vn-space-8) * 1.625)`. Each resolves the release's length at the resting factor. A
  `--vn-factor-density` retune moves the height's `3.5rem` term and every inset by the same factor,
  while the border width, a Bootstrap global, holds, so at a factor of 2 each control keeps room for
  its text inside the height it declares. The backdrop's `em` height and the `1.25` line height are
  relative to the text already and stay the release's values, as do the stacking and the transform.
  The scale is specified for factors of 1 and above, the range the proof reads: below 1 the line
  height, which is relative to the text and does not shrink, outgrows the shrinking floated inset.
  Sass flattens the nested `calc()` call in the height to one sum, which computes the same length.
- **The disabled label reads the gray token.** The release compiles `#6c757d`; the partial writes
  `var(--vn-gray-600)`, which resolves to that color and holds it in both modes.

The transform and its origin are the release's own bytes in the source, so the comparison records no
difference there. The build spells the trailing `translateX(0.15rem)` as the equivalent
`translate(0.15rem)` in the published stylesheet, and the resolved matrix the proof reads is the
release's. The border width, the body color, the body and secondary surfaces, and the backdrop
radius read the `--bs-*` variables the release names, so each declaration matches the release's own
text and moves with a consumer's retune of that variable.

The floating label proof reads the resolved treatment in the browser; see [the floating label
classes](../tests/src/styles/components/form-floating.test.ts). It reads the container's
positioning, each control's height and insets at rest, under keyboard focus, and after typing, the
label's position, fade, transform, and origin in each of those states, the backdrop's geometry and
its `disabled` surface, the plaintext label's border, the disabled label's gray, the end padding a
valid or invalid control keeps for its state icon, and the transition at rest and under the staged
reduced-motion preference. It also reads the height and every inset at a doubled density factor, the
backdrop radius at a doubled radius factor, the label and the backdrop in each color mode, and the
declarations under an ancestor retune of each `--bs-*` variable the family reads. Each limit that
bounds what the proof can claim is recorded in the
`tests/src/styles/components/form-floating.test.ts` file beside the reading it bounds. The installed
browser exports offer no way to put a control into the autofilled state, so the autofill rules have
no resolved reading, and the proof reads the declarations the cascade authors for them, which is
compiled-contract evidence rather than a rendered proof. The class-qualified disabled label rule
paints what the bare disabled rule already paints, so it takes the same declaration reading. The
`.form-select` rule removes the select's native appearance, so the floating select's
`line-height: 1.25` declaration resolves against its type size and the proof reads it resolved. The
select's own border, radius, and paint belong to the `.form-select` rule, which ships, so the
`form-floating-select` frame shows the floated label over the styled select; the text control's
belong to the `.form-control` rule, which Veneer ships, so every floating text-control frame shows
the floated label over the styled control.

### Input group classes

The input group key ships every selector the release records for it: the group row, the text
control, select, and floating wrapper that take its free space, the focus and button lifts, the text
addon, the large and small sizes, the squared inner corners with the dropdown toggle's own count,
the overlap margin, and the width a group takes inside a toolbar. Where a size rule and a
validation state carry the same specificity, the state wins under the forms order § Styles states,
so a failing control in a sized group keeps the padding its mark sits in. The feedback and tooltip
keys close with it, because the overlap rule this partial writes is the one rule they share with the
group; each element's own rules ship from the `src/styles/components/_validation.scss` partial,
which § Validation classes describes.

Every child after the first pulls back by `--bs-border-width`, so two neighbours paint one line,
where each neighbour's border is one `--bs-border-width` wide, and the group squares each corner a
neighbour touches while the group's outer corners keep the child's own radius. Feedback and tooltip
elements are the children left in place, so neither pulls back nor loses a corner: feedback wraps
onto a line of its own under the row, and a tooltip is positioned absolutely below the group
(`position: absolute; top: 100%`), so it takes no part in the wrap. A group carrying the
`has-validation` class ends with its feedback, so the squaring counts one child further from the end
and the last child on the row keeps its trailing corners. A control inside a floating wrapper is
squared through the wrapper, because the control carries the border.

A button in a group sits one step above a control at rest, so its border paints over the one they
share. A focused text control, select, or floating wrapper, and a focused button, lift to the
group's top step, above both the button and the level a validation state gives a child. The rules
that stack a passing or a failing child carry the state in their own selector and ship from the
validation partial, which writes them once for both states.

A dropdown toggle is left out of the rule that squares every child but the last, because its menu
follows it as a hidden sibling, so the toggle can be the row's visible end while it is not the last
child. The toggle is squared on a count of its own instead: while at least two children follow it,
and while at least three follow it in a group carrying the `has-validation` class, whose feedback is
the extra child. Every class is set in markup, and the Dropdown `plugin` row in § Compatibility
records the behavior J-ENGINE owns. The `.form-control`, `.form-select`, and `.form-floating` rules
ship, so a grouped control carries its own `--bs-border-width` border and focus ring under the
group's rules.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The addon and the size classes read the scale tokens.** The addon's padding, font size, weight,
  and line height read `--vn-space-3`, `--vn-space-6`, `--vn-size-3`, `--vn-weight-body`, and
  `--vn-line-body`; the large and small classes read `--vn-space-4` and `--vn-space-8` with
  `--vn-size-5`, and `--vn-space-2` and `--vn-space-4` with `--vn-size-2`; the room a sized select
  keeps for its indicator is `calc(var(--vn-space-6) * 4)`, four of the select's inline steps, which
  is the multiple the release writes. Each token already resolves to the release's own value, so the
  group renders at the release's size and rescales with `--vn-factor-density`.
- **The feedback and tooltip keys carry the validation partial's departures.** Their spacing, type,
  and tooltip text read the tokens § Validation classes names, and the ledger lists each one under
  its own key.

The addon's text, fill, border, and radius read `--bs-body-color`, `--bs-tertiary-bg`,
`--bs-border-width`, `--bs-border-color`, and `--bs-border-radius`, and the sizes read
`--bs-border-radius-lg` and `--bs-border-radius-sm`, each of which this package already declares,
so each matches the official value and records no departure. The addon therefore repaints with the
color mode, and its corners follow `--vn-factor-radius`.

The input group proof reads the resolved treatment in the browser; see [the input group
classes](../tests/src/styles/components/input-group.test.ts). It reads the row and the child that
grows, the overlap against the published border width, every squared and kept corner on the addon,
the control, the button, and a control inside a floating wrapper, the count a group reporting
validation moves, the leading dropdown toggle squared and the trailing one kept with and without the
`has-validation` class, the feedback and tooltip left in place with the tooltip below the group,
each size on every child it names, the room a failing control keeps for its mark in a sized group,
the focus and button lifts after keyboard focus, the grouped button's own ring, the toolbar width,
and the addon's paint, factors, override, and mode. The text control and select classes write their
corners from `--bs-border-radius` through the `input-border` mixin. The proof holds every kept
corner to the radius the same element carries outside a group, and it holds the control's and the
select's kept corners to the value that the `--bs-border-radius` custom property resolves to. Every
corner the group squares reads zero. The group's free-space and focus-lift rules select the floating
wrapper, so the proof reads them on the wrapper. The wrapper draws no border, so the proof reads the
corners the group squares on the control or select inside it. No wrapper the proof mounts holds a
label, so the proof reads no floated label. The addon takes no position, so a grouped control
already paints over it at rest; the focus lift matters against a grouped button, which rests one
step up at `z-index: 2`. The page frame the capture journey writes shows the `Input group button`
specimen's control under keyboard focus, lifted to `z-index: 5`, with its ring over the grouped
button. The capture journey writes a resting element frame of the `Input group valid tooltip`
specimen and one of the `Input group invalid tooltip` specimen. In each, the validated group's
revealed tooltip hangs over the button-led group the specimen renders beneath that validated group.
The journey reads that the tooltip ends inside the frame and paints over that group's button,
because the tooltip rule writes `z-index: 5` and a grouped button rests at `z-index: 2`.

### Validation classes

The validation keys ship whole in their own partial: the `.was-validated` scope, the `.is-valid` and
`.is-invalid` classes, and the feedback and tooltip elements each state reveals. The partial writes
each state's cascade from the same loop over the state list, because the release emits them from a
shared mixin as well.

A state paints through the `--bs-form-valid-*` and `--bs-form-invalid-*` aliases the theme mixin
already declares, so retuning `--vn-form-valid` and `--vn-form-invalid` retunes a passing and a
failing control together. The mark a state carries is an escaped SVG data URI: a data URI cannot
read a custom property, so the glyph is an asset in `src/styles/_tokens.scss` rather than a token
expression, and the partial reads it into the control's `background-image` and into the select's
`--bs-form-select-bg-icon`. The release withholds that mark from a select showing more than one
value, and so does this cascade.

These are the keys' recorded departures.

- **The focus ring reads the published focus width.** The release compiles `0.25rem`; the partial
  writes `var(--vn-focus-width)`, which resolves to `0.1875rem` and is the binding `.btn` already
  carries. The ring's color stays the release's own `rgba(var(--bs-success-rgb), 0.25)` and its
  danger twin, because each triplet is a variable this cascade declares.
- **The feedback and tooltip spacing reads the space and size scales.** The feedback gap and the
  tooltip padding read `--vn-space-2` and `--vn-space-4`, so each one rescales with
  `--vn-factor-density`; the tooltip's type reads `--vn-size-2`, which the size scale holds fixed.
  The icon geometry stays literal: its lengths are an `em`-based system shared with the control's
  own padding, and rescaling one member of it would move the mark off the control.
- **The color control's width reads the space token.** The release writes
  `calc(3rem + calc(1.5em + 0.75rem))`; the partial writes its `3rem` term as `var(--vn-space-24)`,
  the token the resting `.form-control-color` rule reads, and Sass flattens the nested call to
  `calc(var(--vn-space-24) + 1.5em + 0.75rem)`. The resting and validated widths therefore retune
  together under `--vn-factor-density`, and the icon room stays the release's literal, as the rest
  of the icon geometry does.

The `tests/src/styles/components/validation.test.ts` proof reads each resolved treatment in the
browser: the border and text paint in light and inside a dark island, the mark on a validated
control and on a single-value select, the focus ring, the reveal a sibling's state drives, the
tooltip's placement, the check label's tint, the stacking an input-group child takes, the outline a
focused validated control keeps under staged forced colors, and the validated color control's width
against the resting one at a doubled density and under a direct `--vn-space-24` override. It also
reads a required empty control inside a `.was-validated` form on arrival and again after the control
is filled, which is the scoped form the release reaches without a state class.

### Fade classes

The transition key ships whole. The fade partial writes the `.fade` rule and its hidden state, each
state a class set in markup. The release records the dialog, modal backdrop, and offcanvas backdrop
compounds under the same key, and the modal and offcanvas partials write those beside the rules
they compound; § Modal classes and § Offcanvas classes give them. § Compatibility records the
plugins that move an element between the classes as engine obligations.

The hidden state writes the `opacity: 0` declaration, and no other, on an element carrying the
`fade` class without the `show` class. A hidden element therefore keeps its box, its place in the
flow, its pointer target, and its place in the accessible tree. Adding the `show` class returns the
element to the opacity its own rules give it: no rule writes an opacity for the shown state.

The `.fade` rule transitions the opacity linearly over the `--vn-motion-feedback` token, which
resolves to the release's `0.15s` value, so the `--vn-factor-motion` factor rescales it. The
transition is written through the `transition` mixin, so the reduced-motion rule the release
records beside it is emitted with it, and the duration resolves to the `0s` value under that
preference. The hidden state carries no transition of its own.

The barrel loads the fade partial ahead of the collapse partial, the order in which the release's
`transitions` partial writes the fade rules and the collapse rules. The `.fade` rule and the
`.collapsing` rule each write a transition at one specificity, so an element carrying the `fade`
class and the `collapsing` class transitions its size, as it does in the release.

No rule here paints a color, so every state resolves the same in either color mode.

These are the key's recorded departures.

- **The duration reads the motion token.** The release writes the `opacity 0.15s linear` value;
  Veneer writes the `opacity var(--vn-motion-feedback) linear` value, which resolves to the same
  value and rescales with the `--vn-factor-motion` factor.

The Fade region renders a shown and a hidden card body, each under its card's header. The card
reserves the body's box, so the hidden frame is the card with its header over an empty body. The
hidden body carries the `aria-hidden` attribute, because the hidden state leaves its text in the
accessible tree.

The `tests/src/styles/components/fade.test.ts` proof reads each state in the browser: the written
