Filled roles bind resting and disabled background and border to `--vn-color-{role}-base`, and
text to `--vn-palette-white-base`. Hover and active backgrounds mix that fill with
`--vn-state-mixer` at `--vn-state-hover` and `--vn-state-active`; the border keeps the
resting fill. Outline roles use the role color for resting text and border over a transparent
background, fill on hover, and take the active mix while pressed. Their disabled state restores
the transparent surface and role text. The ring remains primary for every role.

The `.btn-link` class takes `--vn-link-base`, `--vn-link-hover-base`, and
`--vn-link-decoration`; its surface stays transparent. The small size and its group child take
space-2 block padding, space-4 inline padding, size-1 type, and radius-small. The large size and
its group child take space-4, space-8, size-3, and radius-large respectively.
The inherited `--bs-gradient` binding remains `var(--vn-surface-gradient)`.
The `--bs-btn-close-filter` declaration the theme scopes carry is measured in § Departures;
Button neither binds it nor defers it.

### Bootstrap variables Veneer retains

The theme scopes declare `--bs-carousel-indicator-active-bg`, `--bs-carousel-caption-color`, and
`--bs-carousel-control-icon-filter` with the release's own light and dark values, written through a
palette token where the release writes a literal. The release records those theme-scope declarations
under its `theme` vocabulary rather than under the `carousel` key, so no ledger row measures them
there. The `carousel` key measures the same variables where the `.carousel-dark` class declares
them, and its rows in § Departures record the black the class paints through
`--vn-palette-black-base`. The control marks keep the release's filter treatment, because a data URI
cannot read a custom property; a `mask-image` treatment is outside the baseline.
`--bs-btn-close-filter` belongs to the `btn` vocabulary instead, so § Departures measures it, and
its rows there record the empty light-scope declaration this cascade writes against the filter the
release records.

The `--bs-form-select-bg-img`, `--bs-form-switch-bg`, `--bs-accordion-btn-icon`,
`--bs-accordion-btn-active-icon`, and `--bs-navbar-toggler-icon-bg` variables are declared on the
select's, the switch's, the accordion button's, and the toggler icon's own dark rules by their
partials instead, so a light island nested inside a dark one keeps the dark caret, knob, chevrons,
and icon the same way the release does.

### Customization

Override a canonical token in your own unlayered rule. Veneer declares its tokens inside the
`@layer theme` block, so an unlayered rule wins, and every tier and every `--bs-*` alias derived
from the token you changed follows the override, because each one is an expression over that token.
A component rule that paints the release's fixed blue reads `--vn-palette-blue`, or keeps the
release's literal where its partial writes one, rather than the primary role, so a brand retune
leaves that paint where the release puts it; the component's own section names the rule and the
published property that moves it.

```css
:root {
	--vn-factor-density: 1.25;
	--vn-color-primary-base: #2e7d32;
	--vn-color-primary-rgb: 46, 125, 50;
}

[data-bs-theme='dark'] {
	--vn-color-primary-base: #66bb6a;
	--vn-color-primary-rgb: 102, 187, 106;
}

.brand-veil {
	background-color: rgba(var(--vn-color-primary-rgb), 0.5);
}
```

That rule rescales the space scale from 6 px to 7.5 px at `--vn-space-3`, repaints `--bs-primary` in
the color you named, and carries that color through `--bs-primary-bg-subtle`,
`--bs-primary-text-emphasis`, and `--bs-primary-border-subtle`. The channel triplet is a literal
rather than an expression, so override `--vn-color-primary-rgb` alongside the fill; the
`.brand-veil` rule, and any other rule of yours reading the triplet, otherwise keeps painting the
old brand. That rule is also the alpha form itself: a triplet is comma-separated, so it takes
`rgba(triplet, alpha)` and not the slash syntax a modern `rgb()` accepts. The
`[data-bs-theme='dark']` rule is what carries the brand into a dark island, which keeps its own fill
and mixes its own tiers from it. The `tests/src/styles/integration.test.ts` proof executes this
recipe and reads the rescaled spacing, the fill, the subtle, emphasis, and border tiers, the
triplet, the translucent fill the alpha form paints, what a fill override without the triplet
leaves that translucent fill painting, the dark island's own fill and tiers, and each palette paint
the recipe leaves in place: the active page and the active list item, the range thumb's declared
paint resolved on a stand-in element because Chromium withholds the part's computed style, the
focused and checked check, the focused select and text control, and the progress bar.

### Departures

Each row names one declaration the built cascade writes differently from Bootstrap 5.3.8, keyed the
way the official inventory is keyed: the component, the selector, the property, and the at-rule
enclosing the declaration. One table follows per component, in the order the shipped keys sort. The
`readDepartures` function in the `tests/setupServer.ts` module reads every one of them, and the
`collectLedger` function measures the same comparison over the unminified compile, so the
conformance proof reddens on a difference no row records and on a row no difference carries. Refresh
the rows with `npm run build:src && npm run test:conformance`: the ledger gates print every row to
add and every row to strike, one per line, as that row's cells joined by `|` in column order.

The comparison is textual. It reads the value each side writes, never the value a browser computes,
so a row can record a difference in notation whose computed value matches: `transparent` against
`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and `87.5%` against `0.875em` are such rows.

A `—` cell in the `Condition` column records a declaration under no at-rule, and a `—` cell in
either value column records a side that writes no declaration there at all. An `(empty)` cell
records a side that writes the declaration with nothing after the colon, which leaves the property
without a value while the declaration itself stands. The `Departure` cell names why the two values
differ: a `tokenized` row routes the release value through a Veneer token, an `aliased` row reads
another compatibility variable in its place, a `fallback` row keeps the release value behind a
`var()` fallback, a `dropped` row writes no declaration at all, and a `declared` row writes the
value in a form or at a value the other members do not name. An empty value against
a recorded one is a `declared` row rather than a `dropped` row, because the cascade writes the
declaration.

| ------------ | -------------------- | --------------- | --------- | --------------- | ------------------------------ | --------- |
| `blockquote` | `.blockquote`        | `margin-bottom` | —         | `1rem`          | `var(--vn-space-8)`            | tokenized |
| `blockquote` | `.blockquote`        | `font-size`     | —         | `1.25rem`       | `var(--vn-size-5)`             | tokenized |
| `blockquote` | `.blockquote-footer` | `margin-top`    | —         | `-1rem`         | `calc(var(--vn-space-8) * -1)` | tokenized |
| `blockquote` | `.blockquote-footer` | `margin-bottom` | —         | `1rem`          | `var(--vn-space-8)`            | tokenized |
| `blockquote` | `.blockquote-footer` | `color`         | —         | `#6c757d`       | `var(--vn-gray-600)`           | tokenized |

### Additions

Each row names one name this cascade emits that the official inventory lacks, attributed to the
shipped component whose vocabulary it joins. The `readAdditions` function in the
`tests/setupServer.ts` module reads this table, and the `collectLedger` function measures the same
additions, so the conformance proof reddens on a name no row records and on a row no name carries.
The `Category` cell names what was added: a `selector` the release does not write, a `declaration`
the release omits on a selector it does write, or a custom `property` the component's official
vocabulary lacks. An animation is never an addition; § Keyframes states how the ledger refuses one
no shipped key records. A `declaration` name is written `selector { property }`. The `Condition`
cell holds the at-rule enclosing the emitted rule, and a `—` cell records a rule under none, so a
selector the release writes unconditionally and this cascade also writes under a query the release
records for no rule of that selector is named at that query. The `Reason` cell is the only cell no
measurement fixes.

### Outside the ledger

The ledger measures the shipped components' own vocabulary. Canonical token values, role coverage,
names this release declares nowhere, and the Elements behaviors this package does not copy sit
outside that measurement, and are recorded here instead.

Canonical token values are the first. § Reference map records each `--vn-*` value beside the Bootstrap
name it answers to, and a value that differs is a difference this ledger never reads, because the
theme scopes the tokens are declared in belong to the release's `theme` vocabulary rather than to a
shipped component. `--vn-font-sans` drops the `"Noto Sans"`, `"Liberation Sans"`, and
`"Noto Color Emoji"` families the release lists, because no Elements specimen renders any of them.
`--vn-line-heading` at `1.2`, `--vn-radius-base` at `0.375rem`, and `--vn-font-mono-base` agree with
the release's own values, so a reader looking for them meets the agreement instead of an omission.
The `--bs-carousel-indicator-active-bg`, `--bs-carousel-caption-color`, and
`--bs-carousel-control-icon-filter` declarations in the theme scopes belong to that `theme`
vocabulary for the same reason, so § Bootstrap variables Veneer retains records them; the
`carousel` key measures only the declarations its dark class writes.

Role coverage is next. The `tertiary` role has no release counterpart, and the release's `light`
and `dark` roles have no Elements specimen, so each of those keeps the other project's value
unchanged.

Names this release declares nowhere follow. `scroll-padding` on the document waits on the first
sticky header, which fixes the offset, and the component-scoped tokens wait on the components that
paint them. The tooltip paints its hint surface from the release's `--bs-emphasis-color` and
`--bs-body-bg` aliases, so Veneer declares no hint surface token of its own. A name the cascade
never writes reaches neither table here nor § Deferred selectors, whose rows must sit in the pinned
inventory the `scanCompatibilityPresence` function reads.

The Elements behaviors this package does not copy close the list. Elements' disclosure interpolates
its content height when the engine reports `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; the `transition` mixin
emits the reduced-motion pair for every transition it writes, and the
`tests/src/styles/mixins.test.ts` proof reads the collapse. Elements' popover snaps open and fades
closed. The popover key ships no motion of its own: no popover rule the release records reads the
`fade` class or the `show` class, and the `.fade` rule that § Fade classes describes fades an
animated popover in and out alike. That asymmetry is recorded as an Elements decision for its owner,
J-ENGINE, which opens and closes a popover.

## Compatibility

This section is the ledger of what Veneer accepts from Bootstrap 5.3.8. The
tests/conformance.test.ts proof reads its rows and compares their named steps with the official
Button recording. The Component column carries the inventory key, so later component units extend
the same table; engine names the shared official engine and is never shipped as CSS.

The table records the Reboot obligations, the typography and media class obligations, the Button
obligations, and the engine obligations assigned to its unit. Each Obligation cell states what
Bootstrap's own recorded engine does, which is what the named Proof step replays; no cell states
what Veneer's engine does. The disabled-anchor accessibility row is where the recorded engine and
Veneer's delegate diverge: Bootstrap's recorded engine refuses that pointer activation, and
Veneer's delegate reads no disabled state, as § Surface states.
The installed Test `MediaOptions` contract stages forced colors through its `forced` axis, and the
forms proofs read under it the outline's style and width on each focused text control, select,
check, and range. Button's own forced-colors browser reading is B-PASSIVE-CLOSE-B's; until it lands,
the cascade's system-color fallbacks for the button have no browser reading.

A `plugin` row records a behavior J-ENGINE owns, while the classes that behavior sets ship in the
cascade and render in markup.

An accepted row records scope; a named Proof step obliges the official recording to agree with the
row. A shipped selector or variable row requires its official vocabulary less the deferrals under
§ Styles to be present in the built cascade; no deferred name may be present, and each must belong
to the official inventory of a component with a CSS row. The conformance component list includes a
key exactly when its selector and variable rows are shipped. Those CSS rows carry a dash in Proof,
as do source and engine obligations the Button interaction recording cannot drive. A `plugin` row's
Proof cell names instead the test file that proves the obligation, as a path from the workspace
root ending in `.test.ts`, after its engine unit ships; the conformance proof requires that file to
exist, and a row of any other kind refuses the file form. Transition, dismissal, sanitizer, and selector
engine rows record shared engine scope; they do not claim that Button dispatches transition events.
The jQuery rows retain the source inventory while the exclusion that follows limits the claim.

The compatibility claim excludes contextual Reboot selectors that combine bare tags: nested
ordered and unordered lists, code inside preformatted text or links, nested keyboard tags, and the
sibling after a legend. It also excludes the jQuery interface and plugin registration, the
window.bootstrap global and UMD namespace, and Bootstrap's Sass variables, maps, and mixins as a
source API. Popper pass-through positioning options remain accepted wire keys with platform
anchoring as an accepted difference. The sanitizer allowlist and sanitizer overrides are J-ENGINE's,
and the Tooltip row names the `Sanitizer` and `TemplateFactory` utilities that carry them.

## Showcase

The private application renders the Veneer heading, the Dark mode button, and a Showcase region.
After the Showcase region, the regions render in the order the `Showcase` class constructs them;
see [showcase mounting and destruction](../tests/app/browser/Showcase.test.ts), which pins that
order. The Content region carries the text specimens, lists, quotations, code, media,
tables, form controls, and interactive tags. Each helper key sits in the region whose subject it
belongs to rather than in a region of its own, which is how every other section is grouped: the icon
links sit in Links, the aspect-ratio boxes share Media with the image classes and the figure
classes, the vertical rule and the gap steps sit in Layout beside the gutters, the stacks sit in
Flex beside the flex utilities, the clearfix helper sits in Float beside the float utilities, the
stretched link sits in Links beside the icon links, and the list and quotation classes sit in Type.
The font utilities join Type beside the heading classes, whose sizes the size classes share. The
Flex beside the flex utilities, the truncation helper sits in Text beside the text utilities, the
color-and-background pairs sit in Color beside the text colors, and the list and quotation classes
sit in Type. The
showcase's own button drives the controller and announces the selected mode, and its entry
constructs a `Delegate` instance beside the showcase. The shell's own stylesheet reaches that button
through the `data-control` attribute the showcase sets on it, so no rule of the shell's reaches a
specimen through the element it happens to be. The hook is an attribute rather than a class, so the
button stays a bare button and keeps the published treatment the shell's border sits on. The
regions mount into a `main` element the shell carries no id on: a proof reaches it through the host
it mounted the showcase into, and each region through its accessible name. The application barrel
is a workspace implementation surface and is outside this guide's published API tables.

The shell's `viewport` class marks a frame that paints nothing. Layout containment makes the frame
the containing block of every fixed and absolute element inside it, and paint containment with a
clip keeps what such an element overflows inside the frame without making the frame scroll. So a
fixed bar holds to the frame's edge, and a backdrop sized to the viewport raises no scrollbar on the
frame or on the page. The frame's bounded height holds a default dialog at the 390 viewport and
gives a percentage height or offset a definite height to resolve against. Every Position specimen,
every Modal specimen, the Sizing region's `Height steps`, `Maximum sizes`, and `Viewport sizes`
specimens, the Toast region's `Stacked toasts` and `Centered toast` specimens, and every Overflow
specimen render inside an element carrying the shell's `viewport` class; the frame clips what a
card under the `visible` value spills and gives the axis cards a bounded height to share. The
sticky bars scroll inside an element carrying the shell's `scroller` class within the frame,
because the frame clips rather than scrolls; see
[position specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/PositionSection.test.ts), which proves the frame
at the 390 and 1280 viewports.
every Offcanvas specimen, the Sizing region's `Height steps`, `Maximum sizes`, and `Viewport sizes`
specimens, and the Navbar region's `Navbar with offcanvas` specimen render inside an element
carrying the shell's `viewport` class. The sticky bars scroll inside an element

The specimen and region names are what the capture registry addresses a frame by: every registered
scenario names the specimen or the region that is its subject, and § Tests gives the filename law
built on it, so a shipped key no region renders has no subject to register and no frame to be read
from.

Scaffold mandates the Vue toolchain for an `app/browser` environment, and this shell declares no
component in it: the shell is framework-free by design, so the showcase drives the published
cascade and the published engine with no framework between them and what renders.

The cascade carries every `--vn-*` token, every `--bs-*` root alias Bootstrap 5.3.8 declares, and
the document and body baseline; § Compatibility gives each shipped key and the classes it ships. The
document baseline also declares `interpolate-size: allow-keywords`, and the
`tests/src/styles/elements/html.test.ts` proof reads it there. That proves the declaration reaches
the document; what it interpolates is proved by the first unit that animates a keyword length.
§ Tokens gives each token's value and source.

The grow spinners are the specimens the capture registry declines: each one rests at
`transform: scale(0)` and `opacity: 0`, so its frame would carry an empty box and no subject, and at
the wider variants the declared region clips to no pixel at all. The showcase renders each of them,
and the spinner proof reads their running timelines, so what is declined is the frame rather than
the proof; see [cascade spinner classes](../tests/src/styles/components/spinner.test.ts).

The Carousel region renders no lone incoming slide and no swipe class, and the capture registry
declines both frames for the reason § Carousel classes states; see
[carousel specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/CarouselSection.test.ts) and
[cascade carousel classes](../tests/src/styles/components/carousel.test.ts).

The Fade region's hidden frame is the reserved empty frame: the card keeps the hidden body's box,
and the capture registry reads that frame on the card rather than on the body, because a region the
transparent body declares paints one color and the frame guard refuses it as a blank; see
[fade specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/FadeSection.test.ts) and
[cascade fade classes](../tests/src/styles/components/fade.test.ts).

The Toast region renders no toast carrying the `showing` class, and the capture registry declines
its frame for the reason § Toast classes states; see
[toast specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/ToastSection.test.ts) and
[cascade toast classes](../tests/src/styles/components/toast.test.ts).

The Modal region renders no backdrop carrying the `fade` class alone, and the capture registry
declines that frame for the reason § Modal classes states; see
[modal specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/ModalSection.test.ts) and
[cascade modal classes](../tests/src/styles/components/modal.test.ts).

The Tooltip and Popover regions render each tip inside an element carrying the shell's `viewport`
class, placed through the shipped position utilities that stand in for the placement the engine
writes, and each tip's box and arrow lie inside the frame at the 390 and 1280 viewports. The regions
render no tooltip without the `show` class and no automatic placement, and the capture registry
declines those frames for the reason § Tooltip classes states; see
[tooltip specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/TooltipSection.test.ts),
[popover specimens](../tests/app/browser/sections/PopoverSection.test.ts),
[cascade tooltip classes](../tests/src/styles/components/tooltip.test.ts), and
[cascade popover classes](../tests/src/styles/components/popover.test.ts).

The Offcanvas region renders no panel carrying the `showing` class or the `hiding` class and no
backdrop carrying the `fade` class alone, and the capture registry declines those frames for the
reason § Offcanvas classes states; see

The journey run also writes the capture portfolio an appearance round is ruled on. Each frame is
named `<scenario>--<theme>-<viewport>.png`: the stem names the scenario alone, and the token after
the separator is the variant that rendered it, which is its theme and its viewport together. A run
photographs only the mode its own variant names, so the theme a filename claims and the theme its
frame shows are one reading, and no token names the project that shot the frame.

A scenario's stem is its own subject's stem, and a driven state follows that stem: the `Primary`
specimen held under the pointer is `primary-active`. A subject is a specimen one of the showcase
tables declares, or the region a page frame reads the surface through. The `tests/setup.ts` module
declares that grammar as the types the registry rows are written in, so a scenario spelling a
project suffix or a mode token fails the typecheck at the row declaring it. The registry proof holds
every registered subject against those tables and against the rendered surface, so a scenario whose
subject the showcase stops rendering reddens rather than photographing something else under the same
name; see [showcase journeys](../tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts).

The stem is what lets this portfolio be sorted against a counterpart portfolio by subject rather
than by hand. The rule comes from the Bootstrap 5.3.8 portfolio the CL13 round shot of the same
markup, whose stems match that registry's specimen names. Nothing here pairs the two directories:
no listing of that portfolio is retained in this repository, so the appearance round that reads one
pairs the rows and rules on the alignment.

The following table gives examples of the stem rule: a resting element frame, a driven state, and
the page frame. The capture registry declares every stem and its subject; see
[the capture registry](../tests/setup.ts).

| Veneer stem        | Subject            | Frame                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `capped-container` | `Capped container` | A resting element frame of the specimen's own container |
| `primary-hover`    | `Primary`          | A driven state: the specimen under the pointer          |
| `showcase`         | `Showcase`         | The page's opening and the region, at rest              |

An element frame carries its whole specimen and the background that specimen renders against, and
the element the scenario is about is the frame's declared region. A crop of that element alone
carries one role link and none of the paint behind it, which is why the frame is the specimen and
the region is the reading. The written frame is read back through the installed `readFrame` function
for its size and its floor, the one color its bottom row paints. Its declared region is read for the
fraction of pixels differing from that floor, or from the region's own first pixel where the bottom
row paints several colors, and a region showing the floor alone is refused as a blank. The journey
shoots each resting element frame on a copy of its specimen lifted to the document's start below a
padded top, after releasing the pointer, so the released pointer rests off every copy and no resting
frame carries a hover paint.

A frame is shot in a bounded document. For each shot, every child of the showcase's `main` element
that holds neither the scenario's subject nor its frame is taken out of the layout through the
`hidden` attribute, and laid out again when the placement returns. A page frame therefore carries
the page's opening (the heading and the Dark mode control) and the one section holding its subject.
The arrival frame's subject is the Showcase region, so that frame carries the opening and the region
alone. An element frame of a specimen lifted to the document's start is shot beside the opening with
every section out of the layout, so the specimen's viewport-height lengths resolve against the
variant's viewport. A section added to the showcase grows no frame shot outside it. The declared
region is read with the pane staged at the height the capture reaches, which is the variant's
viewport or the bounded document's height, whichever is taller, and only after the pane is staged
there again and a second reading of the document's height agrees with the first. A frame larger
than the largest frame a run has read back is refused before it is shot, on every run, naming its
scenario; see [the capture registry](../tests/setup.ts). A page frame carries a focus state and
never a pointer state, because taking the other sections out of the layout can move its subject out
from under the pointer, so every pointer state is an element frame of a specimen lifted to the
document's start.

The guard's population is the frames on disk under the `tmp/capture/states` directory, discovered
from the registry's own expansion and read back whether or not this run wrote a file, so an ordinary
journey run guards the frames an earlier capture run left. Each frame is paired with the region its
scenario declared while the shot was staged, because the written file carries no box and the
handed-back document no longer holds one. A directory holding no frame is reported as that, and held
to the directory rather than passed over as a clean sweep.

One accessibility artifact covers one subject and one variant, and it is named
`<subject>--<theme>-<viewport>-accessibility.txt`. Its stem is the subject's where a frame's stem is
the scenario's, so the Button scenarios' frames share the `primary` and the `toggle` artifact. Each
artifact names its subject, its variant, and the state its reading was taken in, which is `rest`:
the reading is taken on arrival while a driven frame shows focus, the pointer, or a press. It
carries that subject's accessible tree and its keyboard focus order, both read through a scope
enclosing the subject, so a subject that is itself a control records its own role and name rather
than reporting itself unreachable. The per-variant `tmp/capture/<variant>.txt` manifest keeps the
whole page's tree, the focus inventory, the interaction log, and every reading the journeys took.

The two portfolios read side by side within one stated limit: a counterpart frame is shot on a blank
page carrying the specimen alone, and a Veneer frame is shot inside the mounted showcase, on a
specimen lifted to the document's start or where its section renders it, with every other section
out of the layout. The hosts are not the same document, so inherited context is not proven
identical, and a difference between the sides is bounded by that before it is read as a cascade
difference.

Those proofs resolve declarations against the cascade's layer order; § Styles states that order and
names the partial that declares it.
The Tailwind proofs run in the `service` project: they compile each profile through the installed
PostCSS plugin in Node and drive the pinned Chromium over the built cascade; see
[stylesheet profiles](../tests/service/tailwind/profiles.test.ts),
[the consumer pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/consumer.test.ts), and
[the preflight pairing](../tests/service/tailwind/preflight.test.ts). § Tailwind names the profiles, the
recipe each one carries, the shared class names that recipe withholds, and every property preflight
moves.

The conformance proofs pin the official release and its artifact digests, reject runtime boundary
escapes, check shipped CSS vocabulary and recorded animations, compare each declaration's priority
at its media condition, hold the media condition and keyframes tables against the built cascade and
the release, compare each live Button step with its fixture, and cross-check the compatibility rows;
see [Bootstrap conformance](../tests/conformance.test.ts).
The helper proofs read compatibility, media condition, and keyframes tables, built CSS, and the
pinned inventory, and verify the service readiness and its stage; see
[the Node-only readers and recorder](../tests/setupServer.test.ts) and
[the service readiness and stage](../tests/setupService.test.ts).
